Vipassanādiñāṇappabhedāyāti pubbenivāsañāṇādiñāṇapabhedāya. Tatthāti cetokhilasutte (ma. ni. 1.185) “sa kho so, bhikkhave, evaṃ ussoḷhipannarasaṅgasamannāgato bhikkhu bhabbo abhinibbidāyā”ti āgatattā ussoḷhipannarasehi aṅgehi samannāgatabhāvoti evaṃ yaṃ opammasaṃsandanaṃ āgataṃ, taṃ opammasaṃsandanaṃ idha imasmiṃ sekhasutte yojetvā veditabbanti sambandho.

27. For the benefit of insight, by the preliminary practice consisting of virtue, etc., which, as it grows, brings about ever higher distinctions. That very preliminary practice, being well cultivated, inevitably grasps the coming distinction, like an egg; thus it is an 'egg'. Because it is untainted by defilements, it is an 'unrotten egg' (apūti aṇḍaṃ); he who has this is an 'apuccaṇḍa'—a person who stands having striven for insight. His state is 'apuccaṇḍatā'. By 'for the variety of knowledges such as insight' (vipassanādiñāṇappabhedāya) is meant for the variety of knowledges such as the knowledge of past lives, etc. In that regard, because it is stated in the Cetokhila Sutta (MN 1.185): 'Indeed, monks, a monk endowed with these fifteen factors of exertion is capable of breaking through,' the connection is to be understood by applying to this Sekha Sutta the simile that appears there of being endowed with the fifteen factors of exertion.

28. Mahaggatādibhāvena heṭṭhimānaṃ jhānānaṃ anurūpampi attano visesena te uttaritvā atikkamitvāna ṭhitanti anuttaraṃ, tenāha – “paṭhamādijjhānehi asadisaṃ uttama”nti. Dutiyādīsupi [V 2.0018] abhinibbhidāsu. Pubbenivāsañāṇaṃ uppajjamānaṃ yathā attano visayapaṭicchādakaṃ kilesandhakāraṃ vidhamantameva [M 2.0019] uppajjati, evaṃ attano visaye kañci visesaṃ karontameva uppajjatīti āha – “pubbenivāsañāṇena paṭhamaṃ jāyatī”ti, sesañāṇadvayepi eseva nayo.

28. It is 'unsurpassed' (anuttaraṃ) because, even though it is suitable for the lower jhānas by virtue of its loftiness, etc., it stands having surpassed and transcended them by its own distinction. Hence he says, 'supreme and dissimilar to the first jhāna and others.' The same applies to the second and subsequent breakthroughs. Just as the knowledge of past lives arises while dispelling the darkness of defilements that conceals its own object, so too it arises while producing a certain distinction in its own object. Thus he says, 'it first arises by means of the knowledge of past lives.' The same principle applies to the remaining two knowledges.

29. Caraṇasminti paccatte bhummavacananti āha “caraṇaṃ nāma hotīti attho”ti. Tenāti karaṇatthe karaṇavacanaṃ agatapubbadisāgamane tesaṃ sādhakatamabhāvato.

29. He says that 'caraṇasmiṃ' is a locative case in the sense of 'self,' meaning 'it is called caraṇa.' By 'tena' (by that) is meant an instrumental case in the sense of 'means,' because it is the most effective means for them to go to a direction they had not gone to before.

Aṭṭha ñāṇānīti idha āgatāni ca anāgatāni ca ambaṭṭhasuttādīsu (dī. ni. 1.254 ādayo) āgatāni gahetvā vadati. Vinivijjhitvāti pubbenivāsapaṭicchādakādikilesatamaṃ bhinditvā padāletvā.

By 'the eight knowledges' (aṭṭha ñāṇāni), he speaks here taking into account both those that have been mentioned here and those that have not, which are found in the Ambaṭṭha Sutta and others (DN 1.254ff.). By 'having penetrated' (vinivijjhitvā) is meant having broken and shattered the darkness of defilements, such as that which conceals past lives.

30. Sanaṅkumārenāti sanantanakumārena. Tadeva hi tassa sanantanakumārataṃ dassetuṃ “cirakālato paṭṭhāyā”ti vuttaṃ. So attabhāvoti yena attabhāvena manussapathe jhānaṃ nibbattesi, so kumārattabhāvo, tasmā brahmabhūtopi tādisena kumārattabhāvena carati.

30. "By Sanaṅkumāra" means by the Eternal Youth. Indeed, to show his state of being the Eternal Youth, it was said, "From a long time ago." "That existence" refers to the existence in which he generated jhāna on the human plane. That is the youthful existence; therefore, even having become a Brahmā, he fares with just such a youthful existence.

Janitasmiṃ-saddo eva i-kārassa e-kāraṃ katvā “janetasmi”nti vutto, janitasminti ca janasminti attho veditabbo. Janitasminti sāmaññaggahaṇepi yattha catuvaṇṇasamaññā, tattheva manussaloke. Khattiyo seṭṭhoti lokasamaññāpi manussalokeyeva, na devakāye brahmakāye vāti dassetuṃ “ye gottapaṭisārino”ti vuttaṃ. Paṭisarantīti “ahaṃ gotamo, ahaṃ kassapo”ti pati pati attano gottaṃ anusaranti paṭijānanti vāti attho.

The word "janitasmiṃ" itself is spoken as "janetasmi" by changing the 'i' vowel to an 'e', and its meaning should be understood as "janasmiṃ" (among people). Even when taken generally, "janitasmiṃ" refers to the human world where the designation of the four castes exists. 'The Khattiya is the best' is a worldly convention that applies only in the human world, not in the realm of devas or the realm of Brahmā. To indicate this, it is said, "those who are concerned with lineage." "They are concerned with" means they follow or acknowledge their own lineage again and again, saying, "I am a Gotama," "I am a Kassapa"—this is the meaning.

Ettāvatāti “sādhu sādhu ānandā”ti ettakena sādhukāradānena. Jinabhāsitaṃ nāma jātantiādito paṭṭhāya yāva pariyosānā therabhāsitaṃ buddhabhāsitameva nāma jātaṃ. “Kimpanidaṃ suttaṃ satthudesanānuvidhānato jinabhāsitaṃ, udāhu sādhukāradānamattenā”ti evarūpā codanā idha anokāsā therassa desanāya bhagavato desanānuvidhānahetukattā sādhukāradānassāti. Yaṃ panettha atthato avibhattaṃ, taṃ suviññeyyameva.

"By this much" means by this much giving of approval: "Well said, well said, Ānanda." "It has become known as the Conqueror's speech" means that from beginning to end, the Elder's speech has become known as the Buddha's own speech. A question such as, "Is this sutta called the speech of the Conqueror because it follows the Teacher’s instruction, or merely because of the approval given?" has no place here, because the giving of approval was caused by the Elder’s teaching according with the Blessed One’s instruction. Whatever is not analyzed here in terms of its meaning is very easily understood.

Sekhasuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

The elucidation of the hidden meaning in the commentary on the Sekha Sutta is complete.

4. Potaliyasuttavaṇṇanā

4. The Commentary on the Potaliya Sutta.

31. Aṅgā [M 2.0020] nāma [V 2.0019] janapadino rājakumārā, tesaṃ nivāso ekopi janapado ruḷhivasena aṅgātveva vuccatīti āha “aṅgāyeva so janapado”ti. Mahiyā panassa uttarena yā āpoti mahiyā nadiyā yā āpo tassa janapadassa uttarena honti. Tāsaṃ avidūrattā so janapado uttarāpoti vuccati. Sā pana mahī katthaci katthaci bhijjitvā gatāti āha “kataramahiyā uttarena yā āpo”ti. Tatthāti tassā mahiyā āgamanato paṭṭhāya ayaṃ āvibhāvakathā. Yasmā (a. ni. ṭī. 3.8.19) lokiyā jambudīpo himavā tattha patiṭṭhitasamuddadahapabbatanadiyoti etesu yaṃ yaṃ na manussagocaraṃ, tattha sayaṃ sammūḷhā aññepi sammohayanti, tattha tattha sammohavidhamanatthaṃ “ayaṃ kira jambudīpo”tiādimāraddhaṃ. Dasasahassayojanaparimāṇo āyāmato ca vitthārato cāti adhippāyo. Tenāha “tatthā”tiādi. Udakena ajjhotthaṭo tadupabhogisattānaṃ puññakkhayena.

31. The inhabitants of the country were princes named Aṅga. Their dwelling, even a single country, was called Aṅga by established usage; hence, it is said, 'That country is indeed Aṅga.' The water to the north of this Mahī means that the water of the Mahī river is to the north of that country. Because of its proximity to that water, that country is called Uttarāpa. But that Mahī, having split here and there, has gone; hence, it is said, 'Of which Mahī is the water to the north?' 'There' means: from the coming of that Mahī, this is a clear exposition. Because worldly people, concerning Jambudīpa, Himavā, and the oceans, lakes, mountains, and rivers established there—in regard to whatever among these is not within the range of humans, they themselves are confused and confuse others. To dispel confusion in those various places, the exposition beginning with 'This, it seems, is Jambudīpa' was undertaken. The meaning is that it measures ten thousand yojanas in both length and breadth. Therefore, it is said, 'There...' and so on. It was overwhelmed by water due to the exhaustion of the merit of the beings who enjoyed it.

Sundaradassanaṃ kūṭanti sudassanakūṭaṃ, yaṃ loke “hemakūṭa”nti vuccati. Mūlagandho kāḷānusāriyādi. Sāragandho candanādi. Pheggugandho salalādi. Tacagandho lavaṅgādi. Papaṭikagandho kabitthādi. Rasagandho sajjādi, pattagandho tamālahiriverādi. Pupphagandho nāgakuṅkumādi. Phalagandho jātiphalādi. Gandhagandho sabbesaṃ gandhānaṃ gandho. Yassa hi rukkhassa sabbesampi mūlādīnaṃ gandho atthi, so idha gandho nāma. Tassa gandhassa gandho gandhagandho. Sabbāni puthulato paññāsayojanāni, āyāmato pana ubbedhato viya dviyojanasatānevāti vadanti.

A peak beautiful to see is Sudassana Peak, which in the world is called 'Hemakūṭa.' Root-fragrance is that of kāḷānusāri and others. Heartwood-fragrance is that of sandalwood and others. Sapwood-fragrance is that of salala and others. Bark-fragrance is that of cloves and others. Outer-bark-fragrance is that of wood-apple and others. Resin-fragrance is that of sajja and others. Leaf-fragrance is that of tamāla, hirivera, and others. Flower-fragrance is that of nāgakuṅkuma and others. Fruit-fragrance is that of nutmeg and others. The fragrance of fragrance is the fragrance of all fragrances. For whatever tree has the fragrance of all its parts, beginning with the root, that here is named 'fragrance.' The fragrance of that fragrance is the 'fragrance of fragrance.' All of them are fifty yojanas in width, but in length, they say, it is two hundred yojanas, just as in height.

Manoharasilātalānīti otaraṇatthāya manuññasopānasilātalāni. Supaṭiyattānīti tadupabhogisattānaṃ sādhāraṇakammānubhāvena suṭṭhu paṭiyattāni suppavattitāni honti. Macchakacchapādayo udakaṃ malinaṃ karonti, tadabhāvato phalikasadisanimmaludakāni. Tiriyato dīghaṃ uggatakūṭanti “tiracchānapabbata”nti āha.

'Delightful stone terraces' means pleasant stone terraces with steps for descending. 'Well-prepared' means they are excellently arranged and well-established through the power of the common kamma of the beings who enjoy them. Fish, turtles, and the like make the water impure; due to their absence, the waters are stainless, like crystal. A long peak rising horizontally, he called a 'transverse mountain.'

Āpaṇāni [M 2.0021] eva vohārassa mukhabhūtānīti āha “āpaṇamukhasahassānī”ti. Vibhattānīti [V 2.0020] vavatthitāni aññamaññāsambhinnāni. Vasanaṭṭhānanti attano yathāphāsukaṃ vasitabbaṭṭhānaṃ. Āsati etthāti āsanaṃ, nisīditabbaṭṭhānāni.

Shops are indeed the face of commerce; hence, it is said, 'a thousand shop-fronts.' 'Divided' means distinct and unmixed with one another. 'A dwelling place' is a place to live in according to one's comfort. 'One sits here,' thus it is a seat; places for sitting.

Asāruppaṃ paṭicca uppajjanakassa chādanato channaṃ anucchavikaṃ, tadeva ajjhāsayasampattiṃ patirūpeti pakāsetīti patirūpaṃ. Tenāha “nappatirūpa”nti. Kāraṇavevacanānīti ñāpakakāraṇavevacanāni. Ñāpakañhi kāraṇaṃ adhippetaṃ. Atthaṃ ākaroti pakāsetīti ākāro, tameva līnaṃ guḷhaṃ atthaṃ gametīti liṅgaṃ, so tena nimīyatīti nimittanti vuccati. Idāni tamevatthaṃ vivarituṃ “dīghadasavattha…pe… nimittāti vuttā”ti āha. Teti ākārādayo. Tathā hi pana metiādinā potaliyo gahapati “paribbājakaniyāmena ahaṃ jīvāmi, tasmā gahapati na homīti vadati. Ovadantoti anusāsanto. Upavadantoti paribhāsanto.

Because it covers what is unsuitable, which arises depending on what is unfitting, it is 'channaṃ' (secret). That very thing represents, that is, reveals, the accomplishment of one's disposition, thus it is 'patirūpaṃ' (appearing as suitable). Therefore, he said, 'unsuitable.' 'Synonyms for cause' means synonyms for an indicative cause, for an indicative cause is intended here. 'It makes known, reveals the meaning,' thus it is 'manner' (ākāra). 'It conveys that same hidden, concealed meaning,' thus it is 'sign' (liṅga). 'One infers by that,' thus it is called 'mark' (nimitta). Now, to explain that very meaning, he said: 'a cloth with long tassels... etc. ... are called marks.' These are the manner, and so forth. Indeed, just as Potaliya the householder says, 'I live by the rule of a wanderer; therefore, I am not a householder.' 'Instructing' means advising. 'Reproving' means rebuking.

32. Gedhabhūto lobhoti gijjhanasabhāvo lobho. Agijjhanalakkhaṇo na lobho, anindābhūtaṃ aghaṭṭananti nindāya paṭipakkhabhūtaṃ paresaṃ aghaṭṭanaṃ. Nindāghaṭṭanāti nindāvasena paresaṃ ghaṭṭanā akkosanā. Byavahāravohāropīti kayavikkayalakkhaṇo sabyohāropi dānaggahaṇaṃ vohāro. “Datto tisso” tiādinā voharaṇaṃ paññāpananti paññatti vohāro. Yathādhippetassa atthassa voharaṇaṃ kathanaṃ bodhananti vacanaṃ vohāro. Yāthāvato ayāthāvato ca voharati etenāti vohāro, cetanā. Ayamidhādhippetoti ayaṃ cetanālakkhaṇo vohāro idha imasmiṃ atthe adhippeto, so ca kho sāvajjova samucchedassa icchitattā. Idāni catubbidhassapi vohārassa idha sambhavaṃ dassetuṃ “yasmā vā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Gihīti cetanā natthīti ahaṃ gihīti cetanāpavatti natthi. Gihīti vacanaṃ natthīti gihīti attano paresañca vacanappavatti natthi. Gihīti paṇṇatti natthīti gihīti samaññā natthi. Gihīti byavahāro natthīti samudācāro natthi.

32. Greed (lobha) is being greedy; that is, greed has the nature of craving. What is characterized by non-craving is not greed. 'Not provoking' (aghaṭṭana) is being blameless; it is not provoking others, which is the opposite of blame. 'Provoking by blame' is provoking others by way of blame, which is reviling. 'Transactional expression' (byavahāravohāra) is characterized by buying and selling; also a transaction, giving and receiving, is 'expression' (vohāra). Expression by means of 'Given to Tissa,' and so on, is making known; this is 'conventional expression' (paññatti vohāra). The expression, speaking, and making understood of the intended meaning is 'verbal expression' (vacana vohāra). 'One expresses by this, truly or untruly,' thus it is 'expression' (vohāra), which is intention (cetanā). This is intended here: this expression characterized by intention is intended here in this sense, and it is indeed blameworthy because its eradication is desired. Now, to show the possibility of all four kinds of expression here, 'Because...' and so on was said. 'There is no intention "I am a householder"' means the process of intention 'I am a householder' does not occur. 'There is no utterance "I am a householder"' means the process of utterance by oneself or others 'I am a householder' does not occur. 'There is no designation "I am a householder"' means the convention 'householder' does not exist. 'There is no transaction "I am a householder"' means the customary practice does not exist.

33. Pāṇātipātova saṃyojanaṃ. Kasmā? Bandhanabhāvena pavattanato nissarituṃ appadānato. Pāṇātipātassa atthitāya so puggalo [M 2.0022] “pāṇātipātī”ti vuccatīti āha – “pāṇātipātassa…pe… hotī”ti. Yañhi yassa atthi, tena so apadissatīti. Bahutāyāti acakkhukādibhedena bahubhāvato. Pāṇātipātassa paṭipakkho apāṇātipāto. So pana atthato kāyadvāriko sīlasaṃvaroti āha “kāyikasīlasaṃvarenā”ti. Attāpi maṃ upavadeyyātiādi pāṇātipāte ādīnavadassanaṃ. Ādīnavadassino hi tato oramaṇaṃ. Desanāvasenāti [V 2.0021] aññattha sutte abhidhamme ca dasasu saṃyojanesu pañcasu nīvaraṇesu desanāvasena apariyāpannampi saṃyojanantipi nīvaraṇantipi idha vuttaṃ. Kasmā? Tadatthasambhavato. Tenāha – “vaṭṭabandhanaṭṭhena hitappaṭicchādanaṭṭhena cā”ti, pāṇātipāto hi apāṇātipātapaccayaṃ hitaṃ paṭicchādentova uppajjatīti. Eko avijjāsavoti idaṃ sahajātavasena vuttaṃ, upanissayavasena pana itaresampi āsavānaṃ yathārahaṃ sambhavo veditabbo. Pāṇātipātī hi puggalo “tappaccayaṃ atthaṃ karissāmī”ti kāme pattheti. Diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti, bhavavisesaṃ paccāsīsati. Tattha uppannaṃ vihanati bādhatīti vighāto, dukkhaṃ, pariḷāhanaṃ anatthuppādavasena upatāpanaṃ pariḷāho, ayametesaṃ viseso. Sabbatthāti sabbesu vāresu. Iminā upāyenāti atidesena pana pariggahito attho parato āgamissatīti.

33. Killing living beings is a fetter. Why? Because it proceeds by way of binding and does not allow for escape. Because of the existence of killing living beings, a person is called 'one who kills living beings'; thus, it is said: 'Because of killing living beings... he is...' For by whatever one possesses, by that one is designated. 'By abundance' means because of being manifold, with distinctions such as being without eyes, etc. The opposite of killing living beings is abstaining from killing living beings. That, in meaning, is restraint of virtue through the body door; thus, it is said, 'by bodily restraint of virtue.' 'Even myself might reprove me,' and so on, is seeing the danger in killing living beings. For one who sees the danger, there is abstention from it. 'By way of teaching' means: although not included among the ten fetters or the five hindrances elsewhere in the suttas and Abhidhamma, it is here called a fetter and a hindrance by way of teaching. Why? Because its meaning is possible here. Therefore, it is said: 'in the sense of binding to the round of existence and in the sense of concealing what is beneficial.' For killing living beings arises while concealing the benefit that is conditioned by abstaining from killing living beings. 'One taint of ignorance': this is said in the sense of co-nascence, but in the sense of decisive support, the possibility of the other taints should be understood as is appropriate. For a person who kills living beings desires sensual pleasures, thinking, 'I will accomplish my purpose because of that.' He takes up a view; he hopes for a particular existence. Therein, what has arisen, 'it vexes, it oppresses,' thus it is distress (vighāta); suffering (dukkha); torment (pariḷāha) is a burning that torments by producing harm. This is the distinction among them. 'In all' means in all instances. 'By this method' means: but the meaning grasped by extension will come later.

34-40. Imasmiṃ padeti etena sattasupi vāresu tathā āgataṃ padaṃ sāmaññato gahitaṃ. Tenāha “iminā”tiādi. Rosanaṃ kāyikaṃ vācasikañcāti tappaṭipakkho arosopi tathā duvidhoti āha “kāyikavācasikasaṃvarenā”ti. Yathā abhijjhā lobho, anabhijjhā alobho, evaṃ akodhūpāyāso abyāpādo, saṃvare sukhanti saṃvaroti daṭṭhabbo, anatilobho pana satisaṃvare, anatimāno ñāṇasaṃvare saṅgahaṃ gacchatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Imesu pana padesu evaṃ sabbavāresu yojanā kātabbāti sambandho.

34-40. By 'in this passage,' the term that has come up in all seven instances is taken generally. Therefore, he said, 'by this,' etc. Since provocation is bodily and verbal, its opposite, non-provocation, is likewise twofold; thus he said, 'by bodily and verbal restraint.' Just as covetousness is greed and non-covetousness is non-greed, so too non-anger and non-distress are non-ill-will. It should be understood that restraint is happiness in restraint. It should be understood, however, that non-excessive greed is included in restraint by mindfulness, and non-excessive conceit is included in restraint by wisdom. The connection is that in these passages, the application should be made in this way in all instances.

Evaṃ āsavuppatti veditabbāti ettha vuttassapi ekajjhaṃ vuccamānattā “puna ayaṃ saṅkhepavinicchayo”ti vuttaṃ. Asammohatthaṃ ārammaṇassa. Purimesu tāva catūsu vāresu viramituṃ na sakkomīti vattabbaṃ. “Attāpi maṃ upavadeyyā”ti etassa padassa atthavaṇṇanāyaṃ “na sakkomī”ti, “anuvijjāpi maṃ viññū garaheyyu”nti etassa padassa atthavaṇṇanāyaṃ “na sakkotī”ti [M 2.0023] vattabbaṃ, iminā nayena pacchimesupi catūsu yathārahaṃ yojanā veditabbā. Atimāne bhavāsavaavijjāsavāti vuttaṃ mānena saha diṭṭhiyā anuppajjanato, atimāno pana kāmarāgenapi uppajjatevāti “atimāne kāmāsavaavijjāsavā”ti vattabbaṃ siyā, svāyaṃ nayo vuttanayattā suviññeyyoti na dassito. Pātimokkhasaṃvarasīlaṃ kathitaṃ ādito catūhi chaṭṭhena vāti pañcahi vārehi, sesehi tīhi pātimokkhasaṃvarasīle ṭhitassa bhikkhuno paṭisaṅkhāpahānaṃ, sabbehipi pana bhikkhubhāve ṭhitassa gihivohārasamucchedo kathito. Tattha sabbattha vattaṃ “idañcidañca mayhaṃ kātuṃ nappatirūpa”nti paṭisaṅkhānavasena akaraṇaṃ pajahanañca paṭisaṅkhāpahānaṃ.

Here, regarding 'Thus the arising of the taints should be understood,' because what has been said is stated together in one place, it is said, 'Again, this is the brief analysis.' This is for the sake of non-confusion regarding the object. In the first four instances, it should be said, 'I am unable to abstain.' In the explanation of the phrase, 'Even I might reproach myself,' it should be said, 'I am unable.' In the explanation of the phrase, 'The wise, having investigated, might censure me,' it should be said, 'he is unable.' By this method, the application should be understood as appropriate in the latter four instances as well. Regarding excessive conceit, the taint of existence and the taint of ignorance are mentioned because conceit does not arise together with wrong view; but since excessive conceit does indeed arise with sensual lust, it should be said, 'In excessive conceit, there are the taints of sensuality and ignorance.' This method, being a stated method, is easily understood and thus not shown. The virtue of Pātimokkha restraint is discussed in the first four instances and the sixth, thus in five instances. In the remaining three, abandoning by reflection for a monk established in the virtue of Pātimokkha restraint is discussed. Furthermore, in all instances, for one established in the state of a monk, the cutting off of worldly convention is discussed. Therein, in every case, the practice is: the non-doing and abandoning by way of reflection that 'This and that are not suitable for me to do' is abandoning by reflection.

Kāmādīnavakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Dangers of Sensual Pleasures

42. Upasumbheyyāti [V 2.0022] ettha upa-saddo samīpattho, sumbhanaṃ vikkhepanaṃ. Teneva tamenanti bhummatthe upayogavacananti āha – “tassa samīpe khipeyyā”ti, tassa kukkurassa samīpe aṭṭhikaṅkalaṃ khipeyyāti attho. Nimmaṃsattā kaṅkalanti vuccatīti iminā vigatamaṃsāya aṭṭhikaṅkalikāya uraṭṭhimhi vā piṭṭhikaṇṭake vā sīsaṭṭhimhi vā kaṅkala-saddo niruḷhoti dasseti. Sunikkantanti nillikhitaṃ katvāva nibbisesaṃ likhitaṃ.

42. Regarding `Upasumbheyya`: here the prefix `upa-` has the sense of proximity; `sumbhanaṃ` is scattering. Therefore, this is a statement of application in the locative sense, so he says, 'one should throw near it.' The meaning is, one should throw a skeleton of bones near that dog. By the phrase 'because it is fleshless, it is called a skeleton,' he shows that the word `kaṅkala` is established for a small skeleton devoid of flesh, whether it be the breastbone, the spine, or the skull. `Sunikkantaṃ` means scraped without remainder, having been scraped clean.

Ekattupaṭṭhānassa ajjhupekkhanavasena pavattiyā ekattā. Tenāha “catutthajhānupekkhā”ti. Yasmā panassa ārammaṇampi ekasabhāvameva, tasmā āha “sā hī”tiādi. Lokāmisasaṅkhātāti apariññātavatthunā lokena āmasitabbato, loke vā āmisoti saṅkhaṃ gatāya vasena kāmaguṇānaṃ kāmabhāvo ca āmisabhāvo ca, so eva nippariyāyato āmisanti vattabbataṃ arahati. Kāmaguṇāmisāti kāmaguṇe chandarāgā. Gahaṇaṭṭhena bhusaṃ ādānaṭṭhena.

Because of the oneness of the occurrence of the establishment of one-pointedness by way of regarding with equanimity. Therefore, he said, 'the equanimity of the fourth jhāna.' And since its object is also of a single nature, therefore he said, 'for it is,' etc. 'Designated as worldly allurements': because they are to be handled by the world with its uncomprehended object-base; or because, with respect to the sense-qualities, the state of sensuality and the state of being an allurement have come to be designated as 'allurement in the world'; that alone, in a non-figurative sense, deserves to be called 'allurement.' 'Allurement in the sense-qualities' means desire and lust for the sense-qualities. In the sense of grasping, in the sense of intensely taking up.

43. Ḍayanaṃ ākāsena gamananti āha “uppatitvā gaccheyyā”ti. Gijjhādīnaṃ vāsipharasu na hotīti āha – “mukhatuṇḍakena ḍasantā taccheyyu”nti. Vissajjeyyunti ettha “vissajjana”nti ākaḍḍhanaṃ adhippetaṃ anekatthattā dhātūnaṃ, ākaḍḍhanañca anubandhitvā pātananti āha “maṃsapesiṃ nakhehi kaḍḍhitvā pāteyyu”nti.

43. `Ḍayanaṃ` is going through the sky, so he said, 'having flown up, one would go.' Since vultures and others do not have an adze or axe, he said, 'biting with their beaks, they would hew.' Regarding `vissajjeyyuṃ`, here `vissajjana` is intended to mean 'pulling,' because roots have many meanings; and pulling is pursuing and causing to fall, so he said, 'having dragged the piece of flesh with their claws, they would cause it to fall.'

47. Purisassa [M 2.0024] ārohanayogyaṃ poriseyyaṃ.

47. That which is suitable for a man to mount is `poriseyyaṃ`.

48. Sampannaṃ sundaraṃ phalamassāti sampannaphalaṃ. Phalūpapannanti phalehi upetanti āha “bahuphala”nti.

48. It has excellent, beautiful fruit, thus it is `sampannaphalaṃ`. `Phalūpapannaṃ` means endowed with fruits, so he said, 'abundant in fruit.'

50. Suvidūravidūreti ariyassa vinaye vohārasamucchedato suṭṭhu vidūrabhūte eva vidūre ahaṃ ṭhito. Kassaci nāma atthassapi ajānanato na ājānantīti anājānīyāti kattusādhanamassa dassento ajānanaketi ajānantabhojanasīsena tesaṃ dātabbapaccaye vadati. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva.

50. `Suvidūravidūre` means: in the discipline of the noble one, I stand very far, in a place that has become truly distant, because of the cutting off of worldly convention. Because of not knowing the meaning of anything whatsoever, `anājānīya` means 'they do not know.' Showing this as an agentive formation, regarding `ajānaka`, he speaks of the requisites to be given to them under the heading of 'food for one who does not know.' The rest is easily understood.

Potaliyasuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

The Clarification of the Hidden Meaning in the Commentary on the Potaliya Sutta is complete.

5. Jīvakasuttavaṇṇanā

5. The Commentary on the Jīvaka Sutta

51. Kumārena [V 2.0023] bhato posāpitoti kumārabhato, kumārabhato eva komārabhacco yathā “bhisakkameva bhesajja”nti.

51. He was supported and raised by the prince, thus he is `Kumārabhato`. `Kumārabhato` itself is `Komārabhacca`, just as in the saying, 'the physician is the medicine.'

Ārabhantīti ettha ārabha-saddo kāmaṃ kāmāyūhanayaññuṭṭhāpanaāpattiāpajjanaviññāpanādīsupi āgato, idha pana hiṃsane icchitabboti āha – “ārabhantīti ghātentī”ti. Uddisitvā katanti (a. ni. ṭī. 3.8.12; sārattha. ṭī. mahāvagga 3.294) attānaṃ uddisitvā māraṇavasena kataṃ nibbattitaṃ. Paṭiccakammanti ettha kamma-saddo kammasādhano atītakālikoti āha – “attānaṃ paṭicca kata”nti. Nimittakammassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ “paṭicca kammaṃ phusatī”tiādīsu (jā. 1.4.75) viya. Nimittakammassāti nimittabhāvena laddhabbakammassa, na karaṇakārāpanavasena. Paṭiccakammaṃ ettha atthīti maṃsaṃ paṭiccakammaṃ yathā “buddhaṃ etassa atthīti buddho”ti. Tesanti nigaṇṭhānaṃ. Aññepi brāhmaṇādayo taṃladdhikā attheva.

Regarding `ārabhanti`: although the word `ārabha` is found in such senses as desire, striving, instigating a sacrifice, incurring an offense, informing, and so on, here it should be taken in the sense of harming; thus he said, '`ārabhanti` means they kill.' `Uddisitvā kataṃ` means done, produced, by way of killing, having designated oneself. Regarding `paṭiccakamma`: here the word `kamma` is an instrumental formation referring to the past; thus he said, 'done on account of oneself.' This is a designation for `nimittakamma`, as in such phrases as 'an action based on a condition touches one.' `Of nimittakamma` means of an action to be obtained by way of a sign, not by way of doing or causing to be done. The flesh is `paṭiccakamma` in the sense that '`paṭiccakamma` exists here,' just as 'he has the Buddha, thus he is a Buddhist (`buddho`).' `Tesaṃ` means of the Nigaṇṭhas. Other brahmins and so on who hold that view are also included.

Kāraṇanti ettha yutti adhippetā, sā eva ca dhammato anapetattā “dhammo”ti vuttāti āha – “kāraṇaṃ nāma tikoṭiparisuddhamacchamaṃsaparibhogo”ti. Anukāraṇaṃ nāma mahājanassa tathā byākaraṇaṃ yuttiyā dhammassa anurūpabhāvato maṃsaṃ paribhuñjitabbanti anuññātaṃ tatheva kathananti katvā. Tanti “jānaṃ uddissakataṃ maṃsaṃ paribhuñjatī”ti evaṃ vuttaṃ paribhuñjanaṃ neva kāraṇaṃ hoti [M 2.0025] sabbena sabbaṃ abhāvato sati ca ayuttiyaṃ adhammoti katvā. Tathā byākaraṇanti “jānaṃ uddissakataṃ maṃsaṃ paribhuñjatī”ti kathanaṃ yuttiyā dhammassa ananurūpabhāvato na anukāraṇaṃ hoti. Parehi vuttakāraṇena sakāraṇo hutvāti pare titthiyā ‘jāna’ntiādinā dhammaṃ kathenti vadanti, tena kāraṇabhūtena sakāraṇo hutvā. Tehi tathā vattabbo eva hutvā tumhākaṃ vādo vā anuvādo vā “maṃsaṃ paribhuñjitabba”nti pavattā tumhākaṃ kathā vā parato parehi tathā pavattitā tassā anukathā vā. Viññūhi garahitabbakāraṇanti titthiyā tāva tiṭṭhantu, tato aññehi paṇḍitehi garahitabbakāraṇaṃ. Koci na āgacchatīti garahitabbataṃ na āpajjatīti attho. Abhibhavitvā ācikkhantīti abhibhuyya madditvā kathenti, abhibhūtena akkosantīti attho.

Herein, by `kāraṇa` (reason), justification is intended, and because this is not contrary to the Dhamma, it is called ‘Dhamma.’ Thus he said: ‘The reason is the consumption of fish and meat that is pure in three respects.’ `Anukāraṇa` (a conforming reason) is the declaration by the great populace to that effect; because of its conformity to justification and the Dhamma, it is a statement that 'it is permitted that meat may be consumed.' That consumption spoken of as ‘he knowingly eats meat prepared for his sake’ is no reason at all, because it is entirely non-existent, and being an unreason, it is not the Dhamma. Similarly, the declaration ‘he knowingly eats meat prepared for his sake’ is not a conforming reason because of its non-conformity to justification and the Dhamma. `Having a reason because of a reason stated by others`: others, the heretics, teach and speak of the Dhamma using terms like ‘knowingly’; thus one has a reason based on what has become their reason. `Being one who should be addressed by them in that way`: this refers to your thesis or counter-thesis, your talk that proceeds as ‘meat should be consumed,’ or a subsequent talk about that which was similarly put forth by others. `A reason to be censured by the wise`: let the heretics be; it is a reason to be censured by other wise people. `Koci na āgacchati` means one does not incur censurability. `They declare having overpowered` means they speak after having overcome and crushed; the meaning is, they revile one who has been overpowered.

52. Kāraṇehīti [V 2.0024] paribhogacittassa avisuddhatāhetūhi. Bhikkhū uddissakataṃ diṭṭhaṃ. Tādisamaṃsañhi paribhogānārahattā cittaavisuddhiyā kāraṇaṃ cittasaṃkilesāvahato. Idāni diṭṭhasutaparisaṅkitāni sarūpato dassetuṃ “diṭṭhādīsū”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha tadubhayavimuttaparisaṅkitanti “diṭṭhaṃ suta”nti imaṃ ubhayaṃ anissāya – “kiṃ nu kho imaṃ bhikkhuṃ uddissa vadhitvā sampādita”nti kevalameva parisaṅkitaṃ. Sabbasaṅgāhakoti sabbesaṃ tiṇṇaṃ parisaṅkitānaṃ saṅgaṇhanako.

52. `By reasons` means by the causes for the impurity of the mind that consumes. `Diṭṭhaṃ` (seen) is meat prepared for the bhikkhus. For such meat, because it is unsuitable for consumption, is a cause of mental impurity, as it brings about mental defilement. Now, to show the seen, heard, and suspected in their own nature, the passage beginning ‘in the seen, etc.’ was stated. Therein, `suspected independently of those two` means what is merely suspected without relying on those two, ‘seen’ and ‘heard,’ thus: ‘I wonder, was this killed and prepared for this bhikkhu?’ `All-inclusive` means that which includes all three kinds of suspicion.

Maṅgalādīnanti ādi-saddena āhunapāhunādikaṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Nibbematikā hontīti sabbena sabbaṃ parisaṅkitābhāvamāha. Itaresanti ajānantānaṃ vaṭṭati, jānato evettha āpatti hoti. Teyevāti ye uddissa kataṃ, teyeva.

In `maṅgalādīnaṃ` (of auspicious things, etc.), the word `ādi` (etc.) includes offerings for guests and the like. `They are without doubt` states the complete absence of suspicion. `Itaresaṃ` (for others): it is allowable for those who do not know; an offense occurs here only for one who knows. `Teyeva` (those very ones) means only those for whom it was prepared.

Uddissakatamaṃsaparibhogato akappiyamaṃsaparibhogassa visesaṃ dassetuṃ “akappiyamaṃsaṃ panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Purimasmiṃ sacittakā āpatti, itarasmiṃ acittakā. Tenāha – “akappiyamaṃsaṃ ajānitvā bhuttassapi āpattiyevā”ti. Paribhoganti paribhuñjitabbanti vadāmīti attho.

To show the distinction between consuming meat prepared for one's sake and consuming unallowable meat, the passage beginning ‘But as for unallowable meat...’ was stated. In the former case, the offense is intentional; in the latter, it is unintentional. Therefore it is said: ‘Even for one who has eaten unallowable meat without knowing, there is still an offense.’ `Paribhogaṃ ti`: the meaning is, ‘I say it is to be consumed.’

53. Tādisassāti tikoṭiparisuddhassa macchamaṃsassa paribhoge. Mettāvihārinopīti api-saddena amettāvihārinopi. Mettāvihārino paribhoge sikhāppattā anavajjatāti dassetuṃ “idha, jīvaka, bhikkhū”tiādi [M 2.0026] vuttaṃ. Aniyametvāti avisesetvā sāmaññato. Yasmā bhagavatā – “yato kho, vaccha, bhikkhuno taṇhā pahīnā hotī”tiādinā mahāvacchagottasutte (ma. ni. 2.194) attā aniyametvā vutto. Tathā hi vacchagotto – “tiṭṭhatu bhavaṃ gotamo, atthi pana bhoto gotamassa ekabhikkhupi sāvako āsavānaṃ khayā…pe… upasampajja viharatī”ti āha, “idha, bhāradvāja, bhikkhu aññataraṃ gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā upanissāya viharatī”tiādinā caṅkīsutte (ma. ni. 2.430) attā aniyametvā vutto. Tathā hi tattha parato – “yaṃ kho pana ayamāyasmā dhammaṃ deseti, gambhīro so dhammo duddaso duranubodho santo paṇīto atakkāvacaro nipuṇo paṇḍitavedanīyo, na so dhammo sudesanīyo luddenā”tiādinā desanā āgatā, tasmā vuttaṃ “bhagavatā hi mahāvacchagottasutte, caṅkīsutte imasmiṃ sutteti tīsu ṭhānesu attānaṃyeva sandhāya desanā katā”ti. Maṃsūpasecanova adhippeto macchamaṃsasahitassa āhārassa paribhogabhāvato macchamaṃsassa ca idha adhippetattā.

53. `Tādisassa` (of such a one) refers to the consumption of fish and meat that is pure in three respects. `Mettāvihārinopi` (even one dwelling in loving-kindness): by the word `api` (even), one not dwelling in loving-kindness is also included. To show that the blamelessness in the consumption by one dwelling in loving-kindness has reached its peak, the passage beginning ‘Here, Jīvaka, a bhikkhu...’ was stated. `Aniyametvā` (without specifying) means without particularizing, in a general way. For in the Mahāvacchagottasutta, the Blessed One spoke of himself without specifying, saying: ‘When, Vaccha, a bhikkhu’s craving is abandoned...’ Similarly, in the Caṅkīsutta, he spoke of himself without specifying, saying: ‘Here, Bhāradvāja, a bhikkhu dwells depending on some village or town...’ For there it is later said: ‘The Dhamma that this venerable one teaches is profound, difficult to see, difficult to understand, peaceful, sublime, beyond the scope of conjecture, subtle, to be experienced by the wise; that Dhamma cannot be easily taught by one who is greedy.’ Therefore it is said: ‘The Blessed One, in the Mahāvacchagottasutta, the Caṅkīsutta, and in this sutta—in these three places—gave the teaching with reference to himself.’ `With meat as a relish` is what is intended, because it is the consumption of food together with fish and meat, and because fish and meat are intended here.

Agathito [V 2.0025] appaṭibaddho. Taṇhāmucchanāyāti taṇhāyanavasena mucchāpattiyā. Anajjhopanno taṇhāya abhibhavitvā na ajjhotthaṭo, gilitvā pariniṭṭhapetvā na saṇṭhitoti attho. Tenāha – “sabbaṃ ālumpitvā”tiādi. Idha ādīnavo āhārassa paṭikūlabhāvoti āha “ekarattivāsenā”tiādi. Ayamattho āhāraparibhogoti atthasaṃyojanaparicchedikā “yāvadeva imassa kāyassa ṭhitiyā”tiādinā (dī. ni. 3.182; ma. ni. 1.23; 2.24; 3.75; saṃ. ni. 4.120) pavattā āhārapaṭibaddhachandarāganissaraṇabhūtā paññā assa atthīti nissaraṇapañño. Idamatthanti etamatthāya. Evaṃ santeti “brahmāti ca mettāvihārino samaññā”ti avatvā ye dhammā mettāvihārassa paṭipakkhabhūtā, tattha sāvasesaṃ pahāsi brahmā, anavasesaṃ pahāsi bhagavāti sace te idaṃ sandhāya bhāsitaṃ, evaṃ sante tava idaṃ yathāvuttavacanaṃ anujānāmi, na mettāvihāritāsāmaññamattatoti attho.

`Agathito` means not tied; `appaṭibaddho` means not bound. `By infatuation with craving` means by falling into infatuation through the power of craving. `Anajjhopanno` (not overwhelmed) means not having been overcome and submerged by craving, not having swallowed it down and settled for it; that is the meaning. Therefore it is said: ‘having made it all into one lump,’ etc. Here, the danger is the repulsive nature of food; thus it is said, ‘by a single night’s stay,’ etc. He is one with the wisdom of escape (`nissaraṇapañño`) because he possesses the wisdom that serves as an escape from desire and lust connected with food, a wisdom that proceeds from the passage defining the purpose: ‘just for the maintenance of this body….’ `Idam atthaṃ` means for this purpose. `This being so`: If you have said this with reference to the fact that Brahmā has abandoned with remainder those things that are the opposite of dwelling in loving-kindness, while the Blessed One has abandoned them without remainder—rather than saying, ‘Brahmā is a designation for one who dwells in loving-kindness’—then, this being so, I approve of this statement of yours as correctly spoken, not on account of the mere commonality of dwelling in loving-kindness. That is the meaning.

55. “Pāṭiyekko [M 2.0027] anusandhī”ti vatvā visuṃ anusandhibhāvaṃ dassetuṃ “imasmiṃ hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Dvāraṃ thaketīti macchamaṃsaparibhogānuññāya aññesaṃ vacanadvāraṃ pidahati, codanāpathaṃ nirundhati. Kathaṃ sattānuddayaṃ dasseti? Sattānuddayamukhena bāhirakānaṃ macchamaṃsaparibhogapaṭikkhepo tayidaṃ micchā, tikoṭiparisuddhasseva macchamaṃsassa paribhogo bhagavatā anuññāto. Tathā hi vuttaṃ – ‘tīhi kho ahaṃ, jīvaka, ṭhānehi maṃsaṃ paribhoganti vadāmī’tiādi (ma. ni. 2.52). Vinayepi (pārā. 409; cūḷava. 343) vuttaṃ – “tikoṭiparisuddhaṃ, devadatta, macchamaṃsaṃ mayā anuññāta”nti. Tikoṭiparisuddhañca bhuñjantānaṃ sattesu anuddayā niccalā. “Sattānuddayaṃ dassetī”ti saṅkhepato vuttamatthaṃ vivaranto “sace hī”tiādimāha.

55. Having said, ‘The connection is specific,’ the passage beginning ‘For in this...’ was stated to show that it is a separate connection. `He closes the door` means that by permitting the consumption of fish and meat, he shuts the door of speech for others, blocking the path of accusation. How does he show compassion for beings? The rejection of the consumption of fish and meat by outsiders, using compassion for beings as a pretext, is wrong, for the consumption of fish and meat pure in three respects has been permitted by the Blessed One. For it has been said: ‘Jīvaka, I say that meat may be consumed on three grounds...’ And in the Vinaya it is said: ‘Devadatta, fish and meat pure in three respects has been permitted by me.’ For those who eat what is pure in three respects, compassion for beings is unshakable. Elaborating on the meaning stated concisely as ‘He shows compassion for beings,’ he said, ‘For if...,’ etc.

Paṭhamena kāraṇenāti desanāvasenapi payogavasenapi paṭhamena parūpaghātahetunā. Kaḍḍhito so pāṇo. Galena pavedhentenāti yottagalena karaṇena asayhamānena. Bahupuññameva hoti āsādanāpekkhāya abhāvato, hitajjhāsayattā vāti adhippāyo. Esāhaṃ, bhantetiādi kasmā vuttaṃ, saraṇagamanavaseneva gahitasaraṇoti codanaṃ sandhāyāha “aya”ntiādi. Ogāhantotiādito paṭṭhāya yāva pariyosānā suttaṃ anussaranto atthaṃ upadhārento. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva.

`By the first reason`: by the first cause, the harming of others, both by way of teaching and by way of application. `That living being was dragged.` `Shaking by the neck`: by the instrument of a yoke on the neck, being unable to endure. It is indeed very meritorious, either because there is no expectation of assailing or because of the disposition for their welfare; this is the intention. Why was the passage beginning ‘I, venerable sir...’ stated? With reference to the objection that ‘refuge has been taken simply by the act of going for refuge,’ he said the passage beginning ‘this...’ From ‘plunging into,’ etc., up to the conclusion, recollecting the sutta and reflecting on the meaning. The rest is very easy to understand.

Jīvakasuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

The Elucidation of the Hidden Meaning of the Commentary on the Jīvaka Sutta is concluded.

6. Upālisuttavaṇṇanā

6. The Commentary on the Upāli Sutta

56. Pāvāraṃ [V 2.0026] pārupatīti pāvāriko, idaṃ tassa kulasamudāgataṃ nāmaṃ, so pana mahaddhano mahābhogo nagare seṭṭhiṭṭhāne ṭhito. Tenāha “dussapāvārikaseṭṭhino”ti. Dīghattā dīghatamattā. So kira pamāṇato upavacchayato diyaḍḍharatanaṃ atikkamma ṭhito. Evaṃladdhanāmoti “dīghatapassī”ti laddhasamañño. Bāhirāyataneti titthiyasamaye piṇḍapātoti vohāro natthi, tasmā sāsanavohārena “piṇḍapātappaṭikkanto”ti vuttanti adhippāyo.

56. Because he wears a cloak (pāvāra), he is a pāvārika; this is his family name. He was very wealthy and of great fortune, established in the position of a banker in the city. Hence it is said, 'of the banker Dussapāvārika.' Because of his great height. It is said that in measurement, he stood over one and a half cubits tall. Thus he acquired the name; he was designated 'Dīgha Tapassī,' the Tall Ascetic. Regarding 'from an external sphere': among the sectarians, there is no term for 'almsfood'; therefore, using the terminology of the Dispensation, it is said, 'having returned from the alms round'—this is the intended meaning.

Dassetīti [M 2.0028] deseti. Ṭhapetīti aññamaññasaṅkarato vavatthapeti. Kiriyāyāti karaṇena. Pavattiyāti pavattanena. Daṇḍāni paññapetīti ettha kasmā bhagavatā āditova tathā na pucchitanti? Yasmā sā tasmiṃ atthe sabhāvanirutti na hoti, sāsane loke samayantaresu ca tādiso samudācāro natthi, kevalaṃ pana tasseva nigaṇṭhassāyaṃ koṭṭhālakasadiso samudācāroti imamatthaṃ dassetuṃ “kammāni paññapeti” iccevāha. Acittakanti cittarahitaṃ, cittena asamuṭṭhāpitanti attho. Kathaṃ pana tadubhayassa cittena vinā sambhavoti codanaṃ sandhāya tattha nidassanamāha “yathā kirā”tiādi. Paṭivibhattānanti atthato bhinnānaṃ. Paṭivisiṭṭhānanti visesanapadavasena saddatopi bhinnānaṃ. Vacanaṃ patiṭṭhapetukāmoti dīghatapassino yathāvuttavacanaṃ patiṭṭhapetukāmo. Tasmiñhi patiṭṭhāpite tenappasaṅgena āgato, upāli gahapati tasmiṃ padese dhammaṃ disvā sāsane abhippasīdissati.

'He teaches' means he explains. 'He establishes' means he defines by separating from mutual confusion. 'By action' means by doing. 'By occurrence' means by causing to occur. Regarding '[he] lays down punishments,' why did the Blessed One not ask about this from the very beginning? Because for that meaning there is no natural expression, and in the Dispensation, in the world, and in other systems there is no such usage. Rather, this is merely a usage of that Nigaṇṭha, like that of a pedantic classifier. To show this meaning, he just said, 'He lays down actions.' 'Without mind' means devoid of mind, that is, not originated by mind. But how is it possible for both of those to exist without mind? With reference to this objection, he provides an illustration, saying: 'Just as, it is said…' 'Separately divided' means different in meaning. 'Specifically distinguished' means different also in word by way of qualifying terms. 'Wishing to establish the statement' means wishing to establish the aforesaid statement of Dīgha Tapassī. For when that is established, the householder Upāli, who has come on that occasion, will see the Dhamma in that place and gain faith in the Dispensation.

Kathā eva upari vādāropanassa vatthubhāvato kathāvatthu. Kathāyaṃ patiṭṭhapesīti kathāvatthusmiṃ, tadatthe vā patiṭṭhapesi. Yathā taṃ vādāropanabhayena na avajānāti, evaṃ tassaṃ kathāyaṃ, tasmiṃ vā atthe dīghatapassiṃ yāvatatiyaṃ vāde patiṭṭhapesi. Vādanti dosaṃ.

The talk itself is the basis for raising a dispute; hence, it is a 'topic of discussion.' 'He established it in the discussion' means he established it in the topic of discussion, or for the sake of that meaning. Just as one does not show contempt out of fear of raising a dispute, so in that discussion, or on that point, he established Dīgha Tapassī in the argument up to the third time. 'Argument' means fault.

57. Idāni cetanāsampayuttadhammampi gahetvā kāyakammādivasena saṅgahetvā dassetuṃ “apicā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha tividhaṃ kāyaduccaritaṃ kāyakammaṃ nāmātiādi “kammassa kiriyāyā”ti pāḷiyaṃ akusalakammassa adhigatattā vuttaṃ, pubbe pana aṭṭhakāmāvacarakusalacetanātiādi sāvajjaṃ anavajjañca sāmaññato ekajjhaṃ katvā dassitaṃ. Kasmā panettha cetanā na gahitāti āha “imasmiṃ sutte kammaṃ dhura”nti. Kāyakammādibhedaṃ kammameva [V 2.0027] dhuraṃ jeṭṭhakaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ, na cetanāmattameva. Evamāgatepīti kammānīti evaṃ nāmena āgatepi cetanā dhuraṃ, tattha cetanaṃ jeṭṭhakaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ katvā vuttanti adhippāyo. Kathaṃ pana tattha kammanti vā kammānīti vā āgate tesaṃ cetanāya dhurabhāvoti āha “yattha katthaci…pe… labhatī”ti. Tattha yattha katthacīti yasmiṃ kismiñci dvāre. Sā vuttāvāti sā cetanā vuttāva, yā kāyasaṅkhārādipariyāyena (yassa kassaci kammassa kāyadvārādīsu pavattāpanacetanā) sampayuttadhammāpi [M 2.0029] tadaggena lokiyāpi lokuttarāpi kammameva, abhijjhādayo pana cetanāpakkhikāti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

57. Now, to show the states associated with volition by including them and grouping them by way of bodily action, etc., the phrase 'Furthermore…' and so on is stated. Therein, 'threefold bodily misconduct is called bodily action,' etc., is stated because unwholesome kamma has been taken up in the Pāli text with the phrase 'of the action, by the doing.' But previously, the eight sense-sphere wholesome volitions, etc.—the blameworthy and the blameless—were shown generally, having been combined. Why is volition not taken up here? He says: 'In this sutta, kamma is primary.' Kamma itself, in its division into bodily kamma, etc., is the primary factor, the chief, and the foremost, not merely volition alone. Even when it comes thus, that is, even when it comes with the name 'kammāni' (actions), volition is primary. The meaning is that volition is spoken of there as being chief and foremost. But how, when 'kamma' or 'kammāni' is mentioned, is volition primary for them? He says: 'Wherever… etc. … one finds.' Therein, 'wherever' means at any door whatsoever. 'That is stated' means that volition is indeed stated. That volition which, by the term 'bodily formation,' etc. (the volition that initiates any kamma whatsoever through the bodily door, etc.), and its associated states—with that volition as chief, whether mundane or supramundane—are kamma itself. But covetousness and so on should be understood as being on the side of volition.

Mahantanti kaṭukaphalaṃ. Na kilamati sappāṭihāriyattā paṭiññāya. Idāni tesaṃ sappāṭihāriyataṃ dassetuṃ “tathā hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yadi akusalaṃ patvā kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ mahantanti vadanto na kilamati, atha kasmā bhagavā idha akusalaṃ manokammaṃ mahāsāvajjaṃ kathesīti āha “imasmiṃ pana ṭhāne”tiādi. Yāvatatiyaṃ patiṭṭhāpanamattena gatamaggaṃ paṭipajjanto. Tenāha “kiñci atthanipphattiṃ apassantopī”ti.

'Great' means having a painful fruit. He does not become weary because his assertion is demonstrable. Now, to show its demonstrable nature, 'For so…' and so on is said. If one does not become weary when, having come to the unwholesome, one declares that bodily and verbal actions are great, then why did the Blessed One here describe unwholesome mental action as greatly blameworthy? He explains with 'But on this occasion…' and so on. By merely establishing it up to the third time, he follows the trodden path. Therefore, it is said, 'Even without seeing any accomplishment of purpose.'

58. Nivāsaṭṭhānabhūto bālako etissā atthīti bālakinī. Satthupaṭiññātatāya nigaṇṭhānaṃ mahāti sambhāvitattā mahānigaṇṭho.

58. Because a boy exists for her as a dwelling place, she is called a bālakinī. Because he is acknowledged by the Nigaṇṭhas as their great teacher and is so esteemed, he is a Mahānigaṇṭha.

60. Āvaṭṭeti purimākārato nivatteti attano vase vatteti etāyāti āvaṭṭanī, māyā. Tenāha “āvaṭṭetvā gahaṇamāya”nti. Satthupaṭiññānaṃ buddhadassane cittameva na uppajjati, ayamettha dhammatā. Sace pana so taṃ paṭiññaṃ appahāya buddhānaṃ sammukhībhāvaṃ upagaccheyya, sattadhā muddhā phaleyya, tasmā bhagavā “mā ayaṃ bālo vinassī”tiāditova yathā sammukhībhāvaṃ na labhati, tathā karoti. Svāyamattho pāthikaputtasamāgamena dīpetabbo. Dassanasampattiniyāmamāha “tathāgataṃ hī”tiādi. Āgamā nu kho idha tumhākaṃ santikaṃ.

60. By this it turns, it turns back from its former state, it keeps under its own control; therefore it is 'turning,' that is, illusion (māyā). Hence it is said, 'the illusion that entraps by turning one away.' Regarding the Teacher's assertion, when seeing a Buddha the thought to maintain it does not even arise; this is the nature of things here. But if, without abandoning that assertion, he were to come into the presence of the Buddhas, his head would split into seven pieces. Therefore the Blessed One, thinking, 'May this fool not be destroyed!,' acts from the very beginning in such a way that he does not come into his presence. This meaning should be illustrated by the encounter with Pāthikaputta. He states the rule about the attainment of vision: 'For the Tathāgata…' etc. Has some doctrine indeed come to you here?

61. Vacīsacce patiṭṭhahitvāti yathāpaṭiññātāya paṭiññāya ṭhatvā.

61. 'Having become established in verbal truth' means having stood by the assertion as it was asserted.

62. Sītodake amatā pāṇā pānakāle pana maranti, tepi tena sītodakaparibhogena māritā honti, tasmā tapassinā nāma sabbena sabbaṃ sītodakaṃ na paribhuñjitabbanti tesaṃ laddhi. Pākatikaṃ vā udakaṃ sattoti purātanānaṃ nigaṇṭhānaṃ laddhi. Tenāha “sattasaññāya sītodakaṃ paṭikkhipantī”ti. Tesaṃ taṃ adhunātananigaṇṭhānaṃ vādena virujjhati. Te hi pathavīādinavapadatthato [V 2.0028] aññameva jīvitaṃ paṭijānanti. Cittena sītodakaṃ pātukāmo paribhuñjitukāmo hoti roge ṭhatvāpi sattānaṃ cittassa tathā na vitatatā. Tenāha – “tenassa manodaṇḍo tattheva bhijjatī”ti. Tenāti sītodakaṃ pātuṃ paribhuñjituñca icchanena. Assāti yathāvuttassa nigaṇṭhassa. Tatthevāti tathācittuppādane eva. Bhijjati saṃvarassa vikopitattā. Tathābhūto so nigaṇṭho sītodakaṃ [M 2.0030] ce labheyya, katipayaṃ kālaṃ jīveyya, alābhena pana parisussamānakaṇṭhoṭṭhatālujivhāādiko sabbaso paridāhābhibhūto mareyya. Tenāha – “sītodakaṃ alabhamāno kālaṃ kareyyā”ti. Kasmā? Yasmā sītodakaṃ pivāya sannissitacittassa maraṇaṃ hoti, tasmā vuttaṃ “manodaṇḍo pana bhinnopi cutimpi ākaḍḍhatī”ti. Yasmā pana tathābhūtacittassa nigaṇṭhassa manosattesu nāma devesu upapatti hotīti titthiyānaṃ laddhi, tasmā vuttaṃ “manodaṇḍo pana bhinnopi paṭisandhimpi ākaḍḍhatī”ti. Itīti evaṃ “idhāssa nigaṇṭho”tiādiākārena. Nanti upāliṃ gahapatiṃ. Mahantoti vadāpesi “manopaṭibaddho kālaṅkarotī”ti vadantoti adhippāyo.

62. Living beings in cold water are immortal, but at the time of drinking they die; they too are killed by that use of cold water. Therefore, their doctrine is that an ascetic should not use any cold water at all. Or, the doctrine of the ancient Nigaṇṭhas is that natural water is a living being. Hence it is said: 'They reject cold water with the perception of it as a living being.' That doctrine of theirs contradicts the theory of the modern Nigaṇṭhas, for they profess that life is something different from the nine categories beginning with earth. One may wish to drink or use cold water with the mind; even when one is ill, the mind of beings is not so extensive. Hence it is said: 'Thereby his mental rod breaks right there.' 'Thereby' means by wishing to drink and use cold water. 'His' means of the aforesaid Nigaṇṭha. 'Right there' means at the very arising of such a thought. It breaks because restraint has been violated. Such a Nigaṇṭha, if he were to get cold water, would live for some time; but not getting it, with his throat, lips, palate, tongue, etc., drying up, he would die, completely overcome by a burning fever. Hence it is said: 'Failing to obtain cold water, he would pass away.' Why? Because death occurs for one whose mind is attached to the wish to drink cold water. Therefore it is said: 'Though the mental rod is broken, it still draws one to death.' Moreover, according to the doctrine of the sectarians, a Nigaṇṭha with such a mind is reborn among the 'mind-beings' deities. Therefore it is said: 'Though the mental rod is broken, it still draws one to rebirth.' 'Thus' means in the manner of 'Here, this Nigaṇṭha…' etc. 'Him' refers to the householder Upāli. 'Great' means he made him say; the intention is, he made him say, 'One bound by the mind passes away.'

Upāsakassāti upālissa gahapatissa. Mucchāvasenātiādinā anvayato byatirekato ca manodaṇḍassa mahantataṃ vibhāveti. Cittasantatippavattimattenevāti vinā kāyadaṇḍena vacīdaṇḍena ca kevalaṃ cittasantatippavattimattena. Bhijjitvāpīti ettha pi-saddena abhijjitvāpi. Aniyyānikāti appāṭihīrā, ayuttāti attho. Sallakkhesi upāsakoti vibhattiṃ vipariṇāmetvā yojanā. Pañhapaṭibhānānīti ñātuṃ icchite atthe uppajjanakapaṭibhānāni.

'Of the lay follower' means of the householder Upāli. By 'Through infatuation,' etc., he clarifies the greatness of the mental rod both positively and negatively. 'By the mere occurrence of a mental continuum' means without a bodily rod or a verbal rod, solely by the occurrence of a mental continuum. 'Even having been broken': here the particle 'pi' also implies 'even without being broken.' 'Not leading out' means not demonstrable, that is, unsuitable. 'The lay follower observed': the construction is by changing the case ending. 'Intuitive replies to questions' means the ready wit that arises concerning a meaning one wishes to know.

“Manopaṭibaddho kālaṃ karotī”ti vadantena atthato manodaṇḍassa taduttarabhāvo paṭiññāto hotīti āha “idāni manodaṇḍo mahantoti idaṃ vacana”nti. Tathā ceva vuttaṃ – “manodaṇḍova balavā mahantoti vadāpesī”ti.

By saying, 'One bound by mind passes away,' the speaker has in effect acknowledged the preponderance of the mental rod. Therefore, he says: 'Now this statement: "The mental rod is great."' And it was said similarly: 'He made him say: "The mental rod alone is powerful and great."'"

63. Pāṇātipātādito yamanaṃ yāmo, catubbidho yāmo catuyāmo, catuyāmasaṅkhātena saṃvarena saṃvuto cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana yāma-saddo koṭṭhāsapariyāyoti “iminā catukoṭṭhāsenā”ti vuttaṃ. Piyajātikaṃ rūpādiārammaṇaṃ rāgavasena bālehi bhāvanīyattā “bhāvita”nti vuccatīti āha “bhāvitanti pañca kāmaguṇā”ti.

63. Restraining from killing living beings and so on is restraint (yāma); a fourfold restraint is a catuyāma; one restrained by the restraint reckoned as fourfold is 'restrained by the fourfold restraint' (cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto). In the commentary, however, the word 'yāma' is a synonym for 'division'; thus it is said, 'by this fourfold division.' An object such as a form, which is of a dear nature, is called 'developed' because it is to be cultivated by fools out of lust. Hence it is said: '"Developed" means the five cords of sensual pleasure.'

Yo sabbaṃ pāpaṃ āsavañca vāretīti sabbavārī, tassa navasu padatthesu sattamo padattho, tena sabbavārinā pāpaṃ vāritvā ṭhitoti sabbavārivārito[M 2.0031]. Tenāha “sabbena pāpavāraṇena vāritapāpo”ti. [V 2.0029] Tato eva sabbassa vāritabbassa āsavassa dhunanato sabbavāridhuto. Vāritabbassa nivāraṇavasena sabbavārino phuṭo phusitoti sabbavāriphuṭo. Saṅghātanti sahasā hananaṃ, asañcetanikavadhanti attho. Katarasmiṃ koṭṭhāseti tīsu daṇḍakoṭṭhāsesu katarakoṭṭhāse.

He who wards off all evil and taints is a 'warder-off-of-all' (sabbavārī). This is the seventh of the nine meanings of the term. Because evil is warded off by that 'warding-off-of-all,' he is 'one-whose-evil-is-warded-off' (sabbavārivārito). Therefore it is said: 'one whose evil is warded off by the complete warding off of evil.' Then, because he has shaken off all taints that should be warded off, he is 'one-who-has-shaken-off-all-that-is-to-be-warded-off' (sabbavāridhuto). Because he is touched by the 'warding-off-of-all,' which prevents what should be warded off, he is 'one-suffused-by-the-warding-off-of-all' (sabbavāriphuṭo). 'A blow' (saṅghāta) means a sudden striking, that is, an unpremeditated killing. 'In which category?' means in which of the three categories of punishment.

64. Khaliyati samādiyatīti khalaṃ, rāsīti āha – “ekaṃ maṃsakhalanti ekaṃ maṃsarāsi”nti. Vijjādharaiddhiyā iddhimā. Sā pana iddhi yasmā ānubhāvasampannasseva ijjhati, na yassa kassaci. Tasmā āha “ānubhāvasampanno”ti. Vijjānubhāvavaseneva ānubhāvasampanno. Citte vasībhāvappatto ānubhāvāya eva vijjāya paguṇabhāvāpādanena. Etena vasībhāvaṃ lokiyasamaññāvasena bhagavā upāliṃ gahapatiṃ paññapetukāmo evamāha. Lokikā hi “bhāvanāmayaiddhiyā iddhimā cetovasībhāvappatto parūpaghātaṃ karotī”ti maññanti. Tathā hi te isayo paresaṃ saṃvaṇṇenti, isīnaṃ ānubhāvaṃ kittenti. Yaṃ panettha vattabbaṃ, taṃ parato āgamissatīti.

64. 'It is gathered together' (khaliyati samādīyati), thus it is a 'threshing floor' (khalaṃ); it is called a 'heap' (rāsi). Thus it is said: 'one threshing floor of flesh' means 'one heap of flesh.' One possessing psychic power by the psychic power of a knowledge-holder. But that psychic power succeeds only for one endowed with spiritual power, not for just anyone. Therefore it is said, 'endowed with spiritual power.' He is endowed with spiritual power precisely through the power of knowledge, having attained mastery over the mind by bringing that very knowledge to proficiency for the sake of spiritual power. With this, the Blessed One, wishing to explain mastery to the householder Upāli in terms of worldly convention, spoke thus. For worldly people think: 'One possessing psychic power born of meditation, having attained mastery over the mind, harms others.' Thus they praise other seers and extol the spiritual power of seers. Whatever should be said on this will come later.

65. Araññameva hutvāti sabbaso araññameva hutvā. Araññabhāvena araññaṃ jātaṃ, na nāmamattena. Isīnaṃ atthāyāti isīnaṃ āsādanatthāya.

65. 'Having become a forest' means having become a forest in every way. It became a forest by its very nature as a forest, not merely in name. 'For the sake of the seers' means for the purpose of assailing the seers.

Godhāvarītīrato nātidūre. Usūyamānoti “na maṃ esa jano parivāretī”ti usūyaṃ karonto. Kiliṭṭho vatāti paṅkadantarajasiratādīhi kiliṭṭhasarīro. Anañjitamaṇḍitoti anañjitakkhiko sabbena, sabbaṃ amaṇḍito ca. Tasmiṃ kāle “kālasseva akkhīnaṃ añjanaṃ maṅgala”nti manussānaṃ laddhi, tasmā anañjanaṃ visuṃ gahitaṃ.

Not too far from the bank of the Godhāvarī. 'Being envious' means being envious, thinking: 'These people do not attend on me.' 'Soiled indeed!' means his body was soiled with mud, dirt on the teeth, dust on the head, and the like. 'Unanointed and unadorned' means with eyes completely unanointed and entirely unadorned. At that time, people held the view that 'anointing the eyes in the morning is auspicious'; therefore 'unanointed' is mentioned separately.

Rājā tassa vacanaṃ gahetvāti “vedesu īdisaṃ āgataṃ bhavissatīti evaṃ, bhante”ti rājā tassa purohitassa vacanaṃ gahetvā. Usumajātahadayoti uttattahadayo. Nāsikānaṃ appahonte mukhena assasanto.

'The king, having accepted his word' means the king accepted the word of his purohita, thinking: 'Venerable sir, it must be that such a thing is found in the Vedas.' 'With a heart become feverish' means with a heated heart. Breathing through his mouth as his nostrils were not sufficient.

Vijitajayehi āgantvā nakkhattayuttaṃ āgamentehi nisīditabbaṭṭhānaṃ jayakhandhāvāraṭṭhānaṃ. Udakavuṭṭhipātanādi tasmiṃ pāpakamme asamaṅgibhūtānampi samanuññatāya [M 2.0032] antokaraṇatthaṃ kataṃ. Katabhaṇḍavuṭṭhīti ābharaṇavassaṃ. Mahājano samanuñño jātoti yojanā. Mātuposakarāmoti mātari sammāpaṭipanno rāmo nāma eko puriso. Asamaṅgibhūtānanti asamanuññānaṃ.

The place where those who have come having conquered should sit, arriving at an auspicious astrological conjunction, is the site of the victory camp. The causing of a shower of water and so on was done for the purpose of including, by their consent, even those who were not party to that evil deed. 'A shower of finished goods' means a rain of ornaments. The construction is: 'The great populace became consenting.' 'Rāma the mother-supporter' means a certain man named Rāma who was of good conduct towards his mother. 'Those not party to it' means those not consenting.

Avakiriyāti [V 2.0030] asussūsataṃ paṭicca. Phuliṅgānīti aggikaṇāni. Patanti kāyeti kāye ito cito nipatanti. Ete kira nirayaṃ vivaritvā mahājanassa dassenti.

'Scattering' is on account of disobedience. 'Sparks' means particles of fire. 'They fall on the body' means they fall down on the body here and there. They, it seems, open up hell and show it to the great populace.

Yathāphāsukaṭṭhānanti mayaṃ kañcipi desaṃ uddissa na gacchāma, yattha pana vasantassa pabbajitassa phāsu hoti, taṃ yathāphāsukaṭṭhānaṃ gacchāmāti adhippāyo. Saṅghāti saṃhatā. Gaṇāti taṃtaṃseṇibhāvena gaṇitabbatāya gaṇā. Gaṇībhūtāti ekajjhāsayā hutvā rāsibhūtā. Adinnādānantiādīsupi niraye paccitvā manussalokaṃ āgatassa vipākāvasesenāti ānetvā yojetabbaṃ.

'A comfortable place': the intention is, 'We do not go aiming for any particular region, but we go to whatever is a comfortable place, that is, wherever it is comfortable for one who has gone forth to dwell.' 'Throngs' (saṅghā) means united. 'Flocks' (gaṇā) are so called because they are to be counted as a flock in the sense of this or that category. 'Having formed flocks' (gaṇībhūtā) means having become of a single intention, they have become a mass. In the case of taking what is not given and so on, too, it should be connected thus: 'by the residual result of kamma for one who has come to the human world after having been tormented in hell.'

Paggaṇhissāmīti sambhāvanaṃ uppādessāmi. Nesaṃ kattabbanti cintesīti yojanā. Kiṃ cintesi? Āghātaṃ uppādetvā anatthakaraṇūpāyaṃ. Tenāha “so dhammakathāpariyosāne”tiādi. Nāgabalapicchillādīnanti nāgabalasāsapaaṅkolatelakaṇikāraniyyāsādīnaṃ cikkhallānaṃ. Viheṭhayiṃsu nirayādikathāhi ghaṭṭentā. Chadvārārammaṇeti cakkhādīnaṃ channaṃ dvārānaṃ ārammaṇabhūte rūpādivisaye.

'I will support them' means 'I will generate esteem for them.' The construction is: 'He thought of doing it to them.' What did he think? A means of causing harm after having generated aversion. Therefore it is said: 'at the conclusion of the Dhamma talk,' and so on. 'Of nāgabala, picchilla, etc.' means of the slimes of nāgabala, mustard, aṅkola oil, kaṇikāra resin, and so on. They harassed them, agitating them with talks about hell and so on. 'In the objects of the six doors' means in the domain of forms and so on, which are the objects of the six doors, that is, the eye, etc.

Nava vuṭṭhiyoti udakavuṭṭhi sumanapupphavuṭṭhi māsakavuṭṭhi kahāpaṇavuṭṭhi ābharaṇavuṭṭhi āvudhavuṭṭhi aṅgāravuṭṭhi pāsāṇavuṭṭhi vālikāvuṭṭhīti imā nava vuṭṭhiyo. Avañcayīti sakkāraṃ karonto viya hutvā asakkāraṃ karonto anatthacaraṇena vañcayi. Adūsaketi anaparādhe.

'Nine showers': these are the nine showers: a shower of water, a shower of jasmine flowers, a shower of māsaka coins, a shower of kahāpaṇa coins, a shower of ornaments, a shower of weapons, a shower of embers, a shower of stones, and a shower of sand. 'He deceived': he deceived by unbeneficial conduct, acting disrespectfully while seeming to act respectfully. 'The innocent' means those without offense.

“Diṭṭhamaṅgalikā brāhmaṇakaññā”ti jātakaṭṭhakathādīsu (jā. aṭṭha. 4.15.mātaṅgajātakavaṇṇanā) āgataṃ, idha pana “seṭṭhidhītā”ti. Vāreyyatthāyāti āvāhatthāya, assāti pesitapuggalassa. Tādisena nīcakulasaṃvattaniyena kammunā laddhokāsena caṇḍālayoniyaṃ nibbatto.

'Diṭṭhamaṅgalikā, the brahmin maiden' is what is found in the Jātaka commentary and so on (Jā-a IV 375ff), but here it is 'the treasurer's daughter.' 'For the sake of choosing' means for the purpose of marriage; 'his' refers to the person who was sent. He was reborn in an outcaste's womb, having found the opportunity through such a kamma that leads to a low-class family.

Cammageheti [M 2.0033] cammena chādite gehe. Mātaṅgotvevassa nāmaṃ ahosi jātisamudāgataṃ. Tanti ghaṇṭaṃ. Vādento tālanena saddaṃ karonto. Mahāpathaṃ paṭipajji diṭṭhamaṅgalikāya gehadvārasamīpena.

'In a leather house' means in a house covered with leather. His name was indeed Mātaṅga, derived from his birth. 'A stringed instrument' means a bell. 'Playing' means making a sound by striking. He took to the great road near the door of Diṭṭhamaṅgalikā's house.

Tassā veyyāvaccakarā ceva upaṭṭhākamanussā paṭibaddhā ca surāsoṇḍādayo jāṇukapparādīhi sukoṭṭitaṃ koṭṭitabhāvena mucchaṃ āpannattā matoti saññāya chaḍḍesuṃ.

Her attendants and servants, who were attached to her, drunkards and so on, abandoned him, perceiving him as dead because he had fallen into a faint from being well beaten with knees, elbows, and the like.

Atha bodhisatto [V 2.0031] āyuavasesassa atthitāya mandamande vāte vāyante cirena saññaṃ paṭilabhati. Tenāha “mahāpuriso”tiādi. Gehaṅgaṇeti gehassa mahādvārato bahi vivaṭaṅgaṇe. Patitoti pātaṃ katvā icchitatthanipphattiṃ antaraṃ katvā anuppavesena nipanno. Diṭṭhamaṅgalikāyāti diṭṭhamaṅgalikākāraṇena.

Then the Bodhisatta, because a remainder of his life-span existed, regained consciousness after a long time as a gentle wind was blowing. Therefore it is said: 'the great being,' and so on. 'In the house-courtyard' means in the open courtyard outside the main gate of the house. 'Fallen' means having fallen down, he lay there without entering, having made the accomplishment of his desired aim an intermediate matter. 'Because of Diṭṭhamaṅgalikā' means for the sake of Diṭṭhamaṅgalikā.

Yasanti vibhavaṃ kittisaddañca. Candanti candamaṇḍalaṃ, candavimānanti attho. Ucchiṭṭhageheti parehi paribhuttagehe. Maṇḍapeti nagaramajjhe mahāmaṇḍape.

'Fame' means wealth and the sound of glory. 'The moon' means the moon's disk, that is, the moon mansion. 'In a leftover house' means in a house used by others. 'Causes to be decorated' means in a great pavilion in the middle of the city.

Khīramaṇimūlanti khīramūlaṃ, pādesu baddhamaṇimūlañca. Yāvatā vācuggatā pariyattīti yattako manussavacīdvārato uggato nikkhanto pavatto, yaṃkiñci vacīmayanti attho. Ākāsaṅgaṇeti vivaṭaṅgaṇe.

'The price of milk and gems' means the price of milk and the price of gems tied to the feet. 'As far as the verbal learning extends' means however much has been uttered, issued forth, and proceeded from the human door of speech, whatever is made of speech—that is the meaning. 'In the open-air courtyard' means in an open courtyard.

Dummavāsīti dhūmo dhūsaro, anañjitāmaṇḍitoti adhippāyo. Otallakoti nihīnajjhāsayo, appānubhāvoti attho. Paṭimuñca kaṇṭheti yāva galavāṭakā pārupitvā. Ko re tuvanti are ko nāma tvaṃ.

'Clad in smoke' means smoky, dust-colored; the intention is 'unanointed and unadorned.' 'A contemptible one' means one of base disposition, that is, of little spiritual power. 'Drape it on your neck' means having covered yourself up to the throat. 'Who are you, fellow?' means 'Hey, what is your name?'

Pakatanti paṭiyattaṃ nānappakārato abhisaṅkhataṃ. Uttiṭṭhapiṇḍanti antaragharaṃ upagamma ṭhatvā laddhabbapiṇḍaṃ, bhikkhāhāranti attho. Labhatanti lacchatu. Sapākoti mahāsatto jātivasena yathābhūtaṃ attānaṃ āvikaroti.

'Prepared' means prepared, fashioned in various ways. 'Alms received while standing' means almsfood to be received by going inside a house and standing; the meaning is begged food. 'Let him receive' means 'may he receive.' 'An outcaste': the great being reveals himself as he really is in accordance with his birth.

Atthatthitaṃ saddahatoti samparāyikassa atthassa atthibhāvaṃ saddahantassa. Apehīti apagaccha. Ettoti imasmā ṭhānā. Jammāti lāmaka.

'For one who believes, desirous of the goal' means for one who has faith in the existence of a goal relating to the future life. 'Go away!' means depart. 'From here' means from this place. 'Wretch!' means base person.

Anūpakhetteti [M 2.0034] ajaṅgale udakasampanne khette phalavisesaṃ paccāsīsantā. Etāya saddhāya dadāhi dānanti ninnaṃ thalañca pūrento megho viya guṇavante nigguṇe ca dānaṃ dehi, evaṃ dento ca appeva ārādhaye dakkhiṇeyyeti. Dakkhiṇeyyeti sīlādiguṇasamannāgate.

'In a fertile field' means in a field that is not a jungle and is endowed with water, while hoping for a special fruit. 'Give a gift with this faith' means: 'Give a gift to the virtuous and the virtueless alike, like a cloud filling up low and high ground; and giving thus, one might just satisfy one worthy of offerings.' 'Worthy of offerings' means those endowed with such qualities as virtue.

Tānīti te brāhmaṇā. Veṇupadarenāti veḷuvilīvena.

'They' means those brahmins. 'With a bamboo splinter' means with a strip of bamboo.

Giriṃ nakhena [V 2.0032] khaṇasīti pabbataṃ attano nakhena khaṇanto viya ahosi. Ayoti kālalohaṃ. Padahasīti abhibhavasi, attano sarīrena abhibhavanto viya ahosi.

'You dig a mountain with a fingernail' is as if one were digging a mountain with one's own fingernail. 'Iron' means black metal. 'You attack' means you overpower; it is as if one were overpowering with one's own body.

Āvedhitanti calitaṃ viparivattetvā ṭhitaṃ. Piṭṭhitoti piṭṭhipassena. Bāhuṃ pasāreti akammaneyyanti akammakkhamaṃ bāhudvayaṃ thaddhaṃ sukkhadaṇḍakaṃ viya kevalaṃ pasāreti, na samiñjeti, setāni akkhīni parivattanena kaṇhamaṇḍalassa adissanato.

'Trembling' means having moved and turned about, he stood still. 'From behind' means on the back side. 'He stretches out his arms, unserviceable': he just stretches out his pair of arms, which are incapable of work, stiff like dry sticks; he does not bend them. His eyes are white because the black pupils are not seen due to their rolling.

Jīvitanti jīvanaṃ.

'Life' means living.

Vehāyasanti ākāse. Pathaddhunoti pathabhūtaddhuno viya.

'In the air' means in the sky. 'A highwayman' is like one who is a road-destroyer.

Saññampi na karotīti “ime kulappasutā”ti saññāmattampi na karoti. Dantakaṭṭhakucchiṭṭhakanti khāditadantakaṭṭhattā vuttaṃ. Etasseva upari patissati appaduṭṭhapadosabhāvato, mahāsattassa tadā ukkaṃsagatakhettabhāvato. Iddhivisayo nāma acinteyyo, tasmā kathaṃ sūriyassa uggantuṃ nādāsīti na cintetabbaṃ. Aruṇuggaṃ na paññāyatīti tasmiṃ padese aruṇapabhā na paññāyati, andhakāro eva hoti.

'He does not even form a perception' means he does not form even a mere perception that "these are of good families." 'A chewed tooth-stick' is said because it is a chewed tooth-cleaning stick. It will fall upon that very one because of his malice toward one who is not corrupt and because the great being was then a supreme field of merit. The range of psychic power is inconceivable; therefore, one should not ponder, "How did he not allow the sun to rise?" 'The rising of the dawn is not perceived' means that in that region the light of dawn was not visible; there was only darkness.

Yakkhāvaṭṭo nu kho ayaṃ kālavipariyāyo. Mahāpaññanti mahantānaṃ paññānaṃ adhiṭṭhānabhūtaṃ. Janapadassa mukhaṃ passathāti imassa janapadavāsino janassa upaddavena maṅkubhūtaṃ mukhaṃ passatha.

"This reversal of time must be the work of a yakkha." 'Of great wisdom' means the foundation of great wisdoms. 'See the face of the country' means: see the face of the people dwelling in this country, who have become downcast because of the disaster.

Etassa kathā etasseva upari patissatīti yāhi tena pāramitāparibhāvanasamiddhāhi nānāsamāpattivihāraparipūritāhi sīladiṭṭhisampadāhi susaṅkhatasantāne mahākaruṇādhivāse mahāsatte ariyūpavādakammaabhisapasaṅkhātā pharusavācā pavattitā, sā abhisapi tassa khettavisesabhāvato tassa ca ajjhāsayapharusatāya diṭṭhadhammavedaniyakammaṃ hutvā [M 2.0035] sace so mahāsattaṃ na khamāpeti, sattame divase vipaccanasabhāvaṃ jātaṃ, khamāpite pana mahāsatte payogasampatti paṭibāhitattā avipākadhammataṃ āpajjati ahosikammabhāvato. Ayañhi ariyūpavādapāpassa diṭṭhadhammavedaniyassa dhammatā, tena vuttaṃ ‘etassa kathā etasseva upari patissatī’tiādi. Mahāsatto pana taṃ tassa upari patituṃ na adāsi, upāyena mocesi. Tena vuttaṃ cariyāpiṭake (cariyā. 2.64) –

Regarding the statement, "His words will fall upon his own head": When that harsh speech—reckoned as a curse, the kamma of reviling a noble one—was uttered by him against the great being—who was endowed with the successful cultivation of the perfections, replete with various meditative attainments, possessed of virtue and right view, whose mental continuum was well-composed, and who was a repository of great compassion—that curse, because of the special nature of that field of merit and the harshness of the ascetic's intention, became a kamma to be experienced in this very life. If he does not obtain the great being's forgiveness, it is its nature to ripen on the seventh day. But when the great being has been asked for and has granted forgiveness, since the successful undertaking of the curse is obstructed, it becomes a kamma that does not ripen, having become defunct. For this is the nature of the evil of reviling a noble one, which is to be experienced in this very life. Hence it was said, "His words will fall upon his own head," and so on. The great being, however, did not allow it to fall upon him; he released him by a skillful means. Therefore it is said in the Cariyāpiṭaka:

“Yaṃ so [V 2.0033] tadā maṃ abhisapi, kupito duṭṭhamānaso;

Tasseva matthake nipati, yogena taṃ pamocayi”nti.

"The curse that he, angry and with a corrupt mind, then uttered against me, would have fallen upon his own head; but by a stratagem I released him."

Yañhi tattha sattame divase bodhisattena sūriyuggamananivāraṇaṃ kataṃ, ayamettha yogoti adhippeto. Yogena hi ubbaḷhā sarājikā parisā nagaravāsino negamā ceva jānapadā ca bodhisattassa santikaṃ tāpasaṃ ānetvā khamāpesuṃ. So ca bodhisattassa guṇe jānitvā tasmiṃ cittaṃ pasādesi. Yaṃ panassa matthake mattikāpiṇḍassa ṭhapanaṃ, tassa ca sattadhā phālanaṃ kataṃ, taṃ manussānaṃ cittānurakkhaṇatthaṃ. Aññathā hi – “ime pabbajitā samānā cittassa vase vattanti, na pana cittaṃ attano vase vattāpentī”ti mahāsattampi tena sadisaṃ katvā gaṇheyyuṃ, tadassa tesaṃ dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāyāti. Tenāha “athassā”tiādi.

For the prevention of the sun's rising done by the Bodhisatta on the seventh day—this is what is intended here by 'stratagem.' For by this stratagem, the distressed assembly with its king—the city-dwellers, townsfolk, and country-folk—brought the ascetic to the Bodhisatta and had him ask for forgiveness. And he, having come to know the Bodhisatta's virtues, clarified his mind towards him. As for the placing of a lump of clay on his head and its splitting into seven pieces, that was done for the sake of protecting the people's minds. For otherwise, thinking, "These ascetics, though alike, act under the sway of their minds and do not bring their minds under their own sway," they might have regarded the great being as being just like him, and that would have led to their long-term harm and suffering. Therefore it is said, "Then to him," and so on.

Lohakūṭavassanti ayaguḷavassaṃ. Tadā hi ratanamattāni diyaḍḍharatanamattānipi tikhiṇaṃsāni ayaguḷamaṇḍalāni ito cito ca nipatantā manussānaṃ sarīrāni khaṇḍakhaṇḍakāni akaṃsu. Kalalavassanti tanukakaddamapaṭalakaddamaṃ. Upahaccāti āghāṭetvā. Tadeva majjhāraññaṃ.

'A rain of iron hammers' means a rain of iron balls. For at that time, sharp-edged iron discs the size of a fist or one and a half fists fell here and there, cutting people's bodies to pieces. 'A rain of mud' means a thin layer of mire and thick mud. 'Having struck' means having struck. That very middle of the forest.

67. Anuviccakāranti anuviccakaraṇaṃ. Kāraṇehi dvīhi aniyyānikasāsane ṭhitānaṃ attano sāvakattaṃ upagate paggahaniggahāni dassetuṃ “kasmā”tiādi vuttaṃ.

67. 'Acting after investigation' means the act of investigating. The words "Why?" and so on were said for two reasons: to show commendation and censure to those who, while established in a teaching that does not lead to deliverance, had become his disciples.

69. Anupubbiṃ kathanti (dī. ni. ṭī. 2.75-76; a. ni. ṭī. 3.8.12) anupubbiyā anupubbaṃ kathetabbakathaṃ, kā pana sā? Dānādikathā. Dānakathā tāva pacurajanesupi pavattiyā sabbasādhāraṇattā sukarattā sīle patiṭṭhānassa upāyabhāvato ca āditova kathitā[M 2.0036]. Pariccāgasīlo hi puggalo pariggahavatthūsu nissaṅgabhāvato sukheneva sīlāni samādiyati, tattha ca suppatiṭṭhito hoti. Sīlena dāyakapaṭiggahaṇavisuddhito parānuggahaṃ vatvā parapīḷānivattivacanato, kiriyadhammaṃ vatvā akiriyadhammavacanato, bhogayasasampattihetuṃ vatvā bhavasampattihetuvacanato ca dānakathānantaraṃ sīlakathā kathitā. Tañca sīlaṃ vaṭṭanissitaṃ, ayaṃ bhavasampatti tassa phalanti dassanatthaṃ, imehi ca dānasīlamayehi paṇītacariyabhedabhinnehi puññakiriyavatthūhi etā cātumahārājikādīsu paṇītatarādibhedabhinnā aparimeyyā bhogabhavasampattiyoti dassanatthaṃ tadanantaraṃ saggakathā. Svāyaṃ saggo rāgādīhi upakkiliṭṭho sabbadā anupakkiliṭṭho ariyamaggoti dassanatthaṃ saggānantaraṃ maggo, maggañca kathentena [V 2.0034] tadadhigamūpāyasandassanatthaṃ saggapariyāpannāpi pageva itare sabbepi kāmā nāma bahvādīnavā aniccā addhuvā vipariṇāmadhammāti kāmānaṃ ādīnavo. Hīnā gammā pothujjanikā anariyā anatthasañhitāti tesaṃ okāro lāmakabhāvo, sabbepi bhavā kilesānaṃ vatthubhūtāti tattha saṃkileso. Sabbaso kilesavippamuttaṃ nibbānanti nekkhamme ānisaṃso ca kathetabboti ayamattho maggantīti ettha iti-saddena dassitoti veditabbaṃ.

69. Gradual instruction (dī. ni. ṭī. 2.75-76; a. ni. ṭī. 3.8.12) means the instruction that should be given in gradual sequence. What is that? The instruction beginning with giving. The talk on giving is given first because it is common to all, easy to do, and is a means for becoming established in virtue. For a person of generous character, being unattached to possessions, easily undertakes the moral precepts and becomes well established in them. The talk on virtue is given after the talk on giving because, with virtue, having spoken of benefiting others, one speaks of refraining from harming others; having spoken of a principle of action, one speaks of a principle of inaction; and having spoken of the cause for attaining wealth and fame, one speaks of the cause for attaining a good existence. To show that this virtue is dependent on the round of existence and that this attainment of a good existence is its fruit, and to show that through these meritorious actions—differentiated into the refined practices of giving and virtue—immeasurable attainments of wealth and good existence are achieved, distinguished as progressively more refined in the realms of the Four Great Kings and so on, the talk on heaven is given next. To show that this heaven is defiled by lust and so on, while the noble path is always undefiled, the path is taught after the talk on heaven. And when speaking of the path, to show the means for its attainment, it should be explained that all sensual pleasures—even those pertaining to heaven, let alone others—are full of dangers, being impermanent, transient, and subject to change: this is the danger in sensual pleasures. That they are base, vulgar, worldly, ignoble, and unbeneficial: this is their inferiority and baseness. That all forms of existence are a basis for the defilements: this is their defilement. And that Nibbāna is complete release from all defilements: this is the benefit in renunciation. It should be understood that this meaning is indicated by the word "iti" in the phrase "up to the path" (magganti).

Sukhānaṃ nidānanti diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ samparāyikānaṃ nibbānasañhitānañcāti sabbesampi sukhānaṃ kāraṇaṃ. Yañhi kiñci loke bhogasukhaṃ nāma, taṃ sabbaṃ dānanidānanti pākaṭo ayamattho. Yaṃ pana jhānavipassanāmaggaphalanibbānapaṭisaṃyuttaṃ sukhaṃ, tassapi dānaṃ upanissayapaccayo hotiyeva.
