“Rasodakena” means with water mixed with the sap of resinous trees. “Āvattanaparivatte katvā” means bending by way of twisting and turning. “Aṭṭhapadakaracanāya” means with an eight-section design for walls, gables, half-moons, and the like.

Viravamāneti “ayaṃ palāyati, gaṇha gaṇhā”ti viravamāne. Hiraññasuvaṇṇaorodheti vattabbaṃ.

“Viravamāne” means shouting, “This one is fleeing, catch him, catch him!” “Hiraññasuvaṇṇaorodheti” should be stated.

303. Ussitāya ussitāyāti kulavibhavabāhusaccapaññāsampattiyā uggatāya uggatāya. Abhilakkhito uḷārabhāvena.

303. “Ussitāya ussitāya” means elevated, elevated by the abundance of family prosperity, learning, and wisdom. “Abhilakkhito” means marked by eminence.

304. Parijuññānīti [V 2.0142] parihānāni. Ye byādhinā abhibhūtā sattā jiṇṇakappā vayohānisattā viya honti, tato nivattento “jarājiṇṇo”ti āha. Vayovuḍḍho, na sīlādivuḍḍho. Mahattaṃ lāti gaṇhātīti mahallako, jātiyā mahallako, na vibhavādināti jātimahallako[M 2.0144]. Dvattirājaparivattasaṅkhātaṃ addhānaṃ kālaṃ gato vītivattoti addhagato. Tathā ca paṭhamavayaṃ majjhimavayañca atīto hotīti āha “addhānaṃ atikkanto”ti. Jiṇṇādipadehi paṭhamavayamajjhimavayassa bodhitattā anuppattatāvisiṭṭho vaya-saddo osānavayavisayoti āha “pacchimavayaṃ anuppatto”ti.

304. “Parijuññāni” means declines. Those beings who are overcome by illness are like those who have wasted away with age and loss of vitality; turning back from that, it is said, “aged and worn out.” He is advanced in years, but not in virtue and the like. One who attains greatness is called “mahallaka”; great by birth, not by wealth and the like, hence “jātimahallaka.” Having passed through a period of time reckoned by the reigns of two or three kings, he is called “addhagata” (one who has traveled the road). And because he has passed the first and middle stages of life, it is said, “having passed the time.” Because the first and middle stages of life are signified by words like “jiṇṇa,” the word “vaya,” when qualified by “anuppatta,” refers to the final age; thus it is said, “having reached the final stage of life.”

“Appiccho, appaḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphasso”ti (a. ni. 10.11) evamādīsu viya appa-saddo abhāvatthoti adhippāyenāha “appābādhoti arogo, appātaṅkoti niddukkho”ti. Appattho vā idha, tatthāpi appa-saddo daṭṭhabbo. Evañhi “yo hi, gahapati, imaṃ pūtikāyaṃ pariharanto muhuttampi ārogyaṃ paṭijāneyya kimaññatra bālyā”ti (saṃ. ni. 3.1) suttapadaṃ samatthitaṃ hoti. Vipaccanaṃ vipāko, so eva vepāko. Samo vepāko etissā atthīti samavepākinī, tāya. Teneva samavepākinibhāvena sabbampi sammadeva gaṇhāti dhāretīti gahaṇī. Gahaṇisampattiyā hi yathābhuttaāhāro sammadeva jīranto sarīre tiṭṭhati, no aññathā bhuttabhutto āhāro jīrati gahaṇiyā tikkhabhāvena. Tatheva tiṭṭhatīti bhuttākāreneva tiṭṭhati gahaṇiyā mandabhāvato. Bhattacchando uppajjateva bhuttaāhārassa sammā pariṇāmaṃ gatattā. Tenevāti samavepākinibhāveneva. Pattānaṃ bhogānaṃ parikkhiyamānaṃ na sahasā ekajjhaṃyeva parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, atha kho anukkamena, tathā ñātayopīti āha “anupubbenā”ti. Chātakabhayādināti ādi-saddena byādhibhayādiṃ saṅgaṇhāti.

In contexts such as “of few desires, little troubled by flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and creeping things” (AN 10.11), the word “appa” conveys the sense of absence; with this intention it is explained: “‘Appābādha’ means healthy, ‘appātaṅka’ means without pain.” Or here, the word “appa” should be understood as meaning “little.” For thus, the sutta passage “For, householder, if one carrying this foul body were to claim health even for a moment, what else is that but folly?” (SN 3.1) is appropriately supported. “Vipaccana” is ripening; that very thing is “vepāka.” “Samavepākinī” means having balanced ripening; by that quality. Because of this very quality of balanced ripening, it takes in and sustains everything properly; hence it is called “gahaṇī” (digestion). For with the perfection of digestion, the food consumed is properly digested and remains in the body. Otherwise, due to the sharpness of the digestive faculty, the food consumed is not digested; likewise, due to its weakness, it remains just as it was eaten. The desire for food arises precisely because the consumed food has been properly transformed. “Teneva” means by the very state of balanced ripening. The possessions of those who have attained them, when they are being used up, do not suddenly vanish all at once, but gradually; thus it is said, “anupubbena.” And so too with relatives. “Chātakabhayādinā” means by the word “ādi,” it includes the fear of disease and the like.

305. Uddesasīsena niddeso gahitoti āha “dhammaniddesā uddiṭṭhā”ti. Yasmā vā ye dhammā uddisitabbaṭṭhena “uddesā”ti vuccanti. Teva dhammā niddisitabbaṭṭhena niddesāti “dhammaniddesā uddiṭṭhā”ti attho vutto. Atha vā ye dhammā aniccatādivibhāvanavasena uddhaṃ uddhaṃ desessanti, te dhammā tatheva nissesato desessantīti evaṃ uddesaniddesapadānaṃ anatthantaratā veditabbā. Tatthāti jarāmaraṇasantike. Addhuvoti niddhuvo na thiro, aniccoti attho. Tenāha “dhuvaṭṭhānavirahito”ti, ajātābhūtāsaṅkhatadhuvabhāvakāraṇavivittoti attho. Upanīyyatīti vā [M 2.0145] jarāmaraṇena loko sammā nīyati, tasmā addhuvoti evamettha attho daṭṭhabbo. Tāyitunti jātiādibyasanato rakkhituṃ samatthena issarena attanā virahitoti. “Imaṃ lokaṃ ito vaṭṭadukkhato mocessāmi, jarābyādhimaraṇānaṃ taṃ adhibhavituṃ na dassāmī”ti evaṃ abhisaratīti [V 2.0143] abhissaraṇaṃ, lokassa sukhassa dātā hitassa vidhātā koci issaro, tadabhāvato āha “anabhissaroti asaraṇo”ti. Nissako mamāyitabbavatthuabhāvato, tenāha “sakabhaṇḍavirahito”tiādi. Taṇhāya vase jāto taṇhāya vijitoti katvā “taṇhāya dāso”ti vuttaṃ.

305. The exposition is taken under the heading of the summary; hence it is said, “the expositions of the Dhamma have been taught.” Alternatively, those teachings that are called “uddesa” because they are to be summarized, those very teachings are called “niddesa” because they are to be explained in detail; thus the meaning “the expositions of the Dhamma have been taught” is stated. Or, those teachings that will be explained progressively through the analysis of impermanence and so forth, those teachings will be explained completely in that very way; in this way, the non-difference in meaning between the terms “uddesa” and “niddesa” should be understood. “Tattha” means near aging and death. “Addhuva” means unstable, not firm; it means impermanent. Hence it is said, “devoid of a permanent state,” meaning devoid of the cause for a permanent, unarisen, unbecome, unconditioned state. Alternatively, “upanīyati” means the world is led on by aging and death, therefore it is impermanent; this is how the meaning should be seen here. “Tāyituṃ” means lacking a lord capable of protecting from the perils of birth and so forth. “Abhissaraṇa” is one who proceeds thinking, “I will free this world from the suffering of the cycle; I will not allow aging, sickness, and death to overpower it.” There is no such lord who is a giver of happiness or a dispenser of welfare for the world. Due to this absence, it is said, “anabhissara” means without refuge. “Nissaka” means lacking anything to be claimed as one’s own; hence it is said, “devoid of one’s own belongings,” and so forth. Being born under the sway of craving and conquered by craving, it is said, “a slave to craving.”

306. Hatthivisayattā hatthisannissitattā vā hatthisippaṃ “hatthī”ti gahitanti āha – “hatthisminti hatthisippe”ti, sesapadesupi eseva nayo. Sātisayaṃ ūrubalaṃ etassa atthīti ūrubalīti āha – “ūrubalasampanno”ti, tamevatthaṃ pākaṭaṃ katvā dassetuṃ “yassa hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Abhinnaṃ parasenaṃ bhindato bhinnaṃ sakasenaṃ sandhārayato upatthambhayato. Bāhubalīti etthāpi “yassa hi phalakañca āvudhañca gahetvā”tiādinā attho vattabbo, idha pana parahatthagataṃ rajjaṃ āharituṃ bāhubalanti yojanā. Yathā hi “ūrubalī”ti etthāpi bāhubalaṃ anāmasitvā attho, evaṃ “bāhubalī”ti ettha ūrubalaṃ anāmasitvā attho veditabbo, āhito ahaṃmāno etthāti attā, attabhāvo. Alaṃ samattho attā etassāti alamatthoti āha “samatthaattabhāvo”ti.

306. Because it falls within the domain of elephants or is connected with elephant training, the craft of elephants is designated “hatthī”; hence he said, “in elephantry,” meaning in the craft of elephants. This same method applies to the remaining words. Having superior thigh strength, he is called “ūrubalī”; hence he said, “endowed with thigh strength.” To make this meaning clear, “for whom indeed…” and so forth, was stated. He splits apart the unbroken army of the enemy, and rejoins his own split army, supporting it. In the case of “bāhubalī” as well, the meaning should be stated thus: “For whom having taken shield and weapon…” and so forth. Here, however, the connection is: “arm-strength” is used to bring back a kingdom gone into the hands of another. Just as in “ūrubalī” the meaning is conveyed without touching upon arm-strength, so also in “bāhubalī” the meaning should be understood without touching upon thigh-strength. “Attā” (self) or “attabhāva” (individuality) means that self-conceit is placed here. “Alamattho” means his self is adequate and capable; hence he said, “a capable individuality.”

Pariyodhāyāti vā parito ārakkhaṃ odahitvā. “Saṃvijjante kho, bho raṭṭhapāla, imasmiṃ rājakule hatthikāyāpi…pe… vattissantī”ti idampi so rājā upari dhammuddesassa kāraṇaṃ āharanto āha.

“Pariyodhāya” means enclosing with complete protection. “Indeed, friend Raṭṭhapāla, in this royal family there are elephant troops… and so forth… they will function.” This too the king said, bringing up a reason in addition to the Dhamma exposition.

Vuttasseva anu pacchā gāyanavasena kathanaṃ anugīti. Tā pana gāthā dhammuddesānaṃ desanānupubbiṃ anādiyitvāpi yathārahaṃ saṅgaṇhanavasena anugītāti āha “catunnaṃ dhammuddesānaṃ anugīti”nti.

The explanation following what has been said, by way of singing, is called “anugīti.” However, those verses are called “anugīti” because they are sung appropriately by way of summarizing, even without paying attention to the order of the teachings in the Dhamma expositions. Thus, he said, “the anugīti of the four Dhamma expositions.”

307. Ekanti ekajātiyaṃ. Vatthukāmakilesakāmā visayabhedena bhinditvā tathā vuttāti daṭṭhabbo.

307. “Eka” means in one existence. Vatthukāma (desire for objects) and kilesakāma (defiling desire) should be understood as having been stated thus, divided by their respective domains.

Sāgarantenāti [M 2.0146] sāgarapariyantena.

“Sāgarantena” means having the ocean as its boundary.

Aho vatāti socane nipāto, “aho vata pāpaṃ kataṃ mayā”tiādīsu viya. Amarātiādīsu [V 2.0144] āhūti kathenti. Mataṃ uddissa “amha”nti vattabbe sokavasena “amara”nti vuccati.

“Aho vata” is an interjection used in expressions of sorrow, as in, “Alas, I have done evil,” and so forth. In phrases such as “amarā,” they say it is an invocation. When referring to the dead, when “amha” (we are) should be said, due to sorrow it is said “amara” (we are immortal).

Vosānanti niṭṭhaṃ, pariyosānanti attho. Sāvāti paññā eva. Dhanatoti sabbadhanato. Uttamatarā seṭṭhā, tenevāha “paññājīviṃ jīvitamāhu seṭṭha”nti (saṃ. ni. 1.246; su. ni. 184).

“Vosāna” means completion; the meaning is conclusion. “Sāva” is indeed wisdom. “Dhanato” means from all wealth. “Uttamatarā” means best; therefore it was said, “They call the life lived by wisdom the best.”

Tesu pāpaṃ karontesu sattesu, niddhāraṇe cetaṃ bhummavacanaṃ. Paramparāyāti attabhāvaparamparāya. Saṃsāraṃ āpajjitvāti bhavādīsu saṃsārassa āpajjanahetuṃ āpajjanto paralokaṃ upeti, paralokaṃ upentova bahuvidhadukkhasaṅkhātaṃ gabbhañca upeti. Tādisassāti tathārūpassa gabbhavāsadukkhādīnaṃ adhiṭṭhānabhūtassa appapaññassa añño appapañño ca abhisaddahanto hitasukhāvahanti pattiyāyanto.

“Among those beings who commit evil”: this is a locative expression in the sense of specification. “Through succession” means through the succession of individual existences. “Having entered the cycle of existence” means: by entering the cause for entering the cycle of existence in states of becoming and so on, he goes to the next world. And in going to the next world, he enters the womb, which is designated as manifold suffering. “For such a one” means: for one of such a nature, who is the basis for the suffering of dwelling in the womb and so on, for one of little wisdom; another person of little wisdom, having faith in him, comes to believe that it brings benefit and happiness.

“Pāpadhammo”ti vuttattā tādisassa paraloko nāma duggati evāti āha “paramhi apāyaloke”ti.

Because it is said, “of evil nature,” for such a person the next world is indeed a bad destination; thus it is said, “in the next world, a state of misery.”

Vividharūpenāti rūpasaddādivasena tatthapi paṇītatarādivasena bahuvidharūpena.

“Of various forms” means in many different ways: in the sense of form, sound, and so on, and also in the sense of more refined forms, and so on.

Sāmaññamevāti samaṇabhāvo eva seyyo. Ettha ca ādito dvīhi gāthāhi catuttho dhammuddeso anugīto. Catutthagāthāya tatiyo. Pañcamagāthāya dutiyo. Chaṭṭhagāthāya dutiyatatiyā. Sattamagāthāya paṭhamo dhammuddeso anugīto, aṭṭhamādīhi pavattinivattīsu kāmesu nekkhamme ca yathārahaṃ ādīnavānisaṃsaṃ vibhāvetvā attano pabbajjakāraṇaṃ paramato dassento yathāvuttadhammuddesaṃ nigameti, tena vuttaṃ “tā pana gāthā dhammuddesānaṃ desanānupubbiṃ anādiyitvāpi yathārahaṃ saṅgaṇhanavasena anugītā”ti. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva.

“The state of a recluse” means the state of being a samaṇa is indeed best. Here, the fourth Dhamma exposition has been recited in the first two verses. The third, in the fourth verse. The second, in the fifth verse. The second and third, in the sixth verse. The first Dhamma exposition has been recited in the seventh verse. From the eighth verse onwards, having distinguished, as is fit, the drawbacks and advantages in regard to engagement and disengagement, in sensual pleasures and in renunciation, showing from a higher perspective the reason for his own going forth, he concludes the aforesaid Dhamma exposition. Therefore, it is said: “Those verses, however, even without adhering to the sequential teaching of the Dhamma expositions, are recited by way of gathering them together as is fit.” The rest is indeed easy to understand.

Raṭṭhapālasuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

Here ends the explanation of the hidden meaning in the commentary on the Raṭṭhapāla Sutta.

3. Maghadevasuttavaṇṇanā

3. The Commentary on the Maghadeva Sutta

308. Pubbe [M 2.0147][V 2.0145] maghadevo nāma rājāti atītakāle imasmiṃyeva kappe anekavassasahassāyukesu manussesu paṭipāṭiyā uppannānaṃ caturāsītisahassānaṃ cakkavattirājūnaṃ ādipuriso maghadevoti evaṃnāmo rājā.

308. “Formerly, there was a king named Maghadeva” means: in a past time, in this very aeon, when humans had a lifespan of many thousands of years, there was a king named Maghadeva, the first of the eighty-four thousand wheel-turning monarchs who arose in succession.

Dhammoti rājadhammoti lokikā vadanti. Mahābodhinidhānapāramitāsaṅkhāto pana dhammo atthīti dhammiko. Dhammenāti ñāyena. Tadā brahmavihārādibhāvanādhammassa rañño anadhigatattā tassapi vā anabhijjhādīhi samānayogakkhamattā vuttaṃ “dasakusalakammapathe ṭhito”ti. Dhammanti dhammato anapetaṃ. Tathā hi ca so pakkhapātābhāvato “samo”ti vuccatīti āha “samaṃ caratī”ti. Pakatiniyāmenevāti paveṇiyā āgataniyāmeneva. Yasmā nigamajanapadesu yebhuyyena gahapatīnaṃ saṅgaho, tasmā aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “gahapatikāna”ntveva vuttaṃ. Pāḷiyaṃ pana aññameva nāgaracārittaṃ, aññaṃ negamajanapadacārittanti te visuṃ gahitā “negamesu ceva janapadesu cā”ti. Paccuggamananiggamanavasena uposathassa paṭiharaṇaṃ pāṭihāriyo, so eva pāṭihāriko, pakkho. Ime divasāti ime cattāro divasā.

“Dhamma”: worldly people say this means the royal law. However, he is called “righteous” because the Dhamma, reckoned as the great treasure of the perfections for enlightenment, exists. “By Dhamma” means by justice. Because at that time the king had not attained the Dhamma of cultivating the divine abodes and so on, or because he was also possessed of equal application with regard to non-covetousness and so on, it is said, “established in the ten wholesome courses of action.” “Dhamma” means not deviating from what is right. For, because he was without bias, he is called “equitable”; thus it is said, “he acts equitably.” “By the established rule” means by the rule that has come down through tradition. Because in market towns and rural areas patronage is mostly from householders, therefore in the commentary it is said only “of householders.” But in the Pāḷi text, the conduct of city-dwellers is one thing, and the conduct of market-town and country-dwellers is another; thus they are taken separately as “in market towns and in rural areas.” The observance of the Uposatha by way of welcoming and sending off is the fortnightly observance; that itself is the fortnightly period, the fortnight. “These days” means these four days.

309. Devoti maccu abhibhavanaṭṭhena. Yathā hi devo pakatisatte abhibhavati, evaṃ maccu satte abhibhavati. “Ahaṃ asukaṃ maddituṃ āgamissāmi, tvaṃ tassa kese gahetvā mā vissajjehī”ti maccudevassa āṇākarā dūtā viyāti dūtāti vuccanti. Alaṅkatapaṭiyattāyāti idaṃ attano dibbānubhāvaṃ āvikatvā ṭhitāyāti dassetuṃ vuttaṃ. Devatābyākaraṇasadisameva hoti na cireneva maraṇasambhavato. Visuddhidevānanti khīṇāsavabrahmānaṃ. Te hi carimabhave bodhisattānaṃ jiṇṇādike dassenti.

309. “Deva” means death, in the sense of overcoming. Just as a deva overcomes ordinary beings, so does death overcome beings. They are called “messengers” because they are like agents carrying out the command of the deva of death, saying, “I will come to crush so-and-so; you, seize his hair and do not let go.” “Adorned and prepared” is said to show that she stood revealing her own divine power. It is just like a divine pronouncement, because death is possible before long. “Of the pure devas” means of the Brahmās whose taints are destroyed. For they, in the final existence of bodhisattas, show them old age and so on.

Dukhitañca byādhitanti byādhibhāvena sañjātadukkhanti attho. Antimabhavikabodhisattānaṃ visuddhidevehi upaṭṭhāpitabhāvaṃ upādāya tadaññesaṃ tehi anupaṭṭhāpitānampi paṇḍitānaṃ tathā voharitabbatā pariyāyasiddhāti āha “iminā pariyāyenā”ti.

“Afflicted and sick” means suffering that has arisen from the state of illness; this is the meaning. With reference to the fact that bodhisattas in their final existence are attended upon by pure devas, it is established by implication that other wise ones, though not attended upon by them, should be spoken of in the same way; hence it is said, “by this method.”

Disampatīti [M 2.0148] vibhattialopena niddeso, disāsīsena desā vuttāti desānaṃ adhipatirājāti [V 2.0146] attho. Uttamaṅge sirasi ruhantīti uttamaṅgaruhā, kesā. Te panettha yasmā palitattā avisesato sabbapacchimavayasandassakā honti, tasmā “vayoharā”ti vuttā.

“Disampati” is a reference with elision of the case ending. Because regions are spoken of by the head-word ‘direction,’ the meaning is “overlord king of the regions.” “Growing on the highest limb, the head” are `uttamaṅgaruhā`, that is, hairs. Here, because they, being grey, are indicators of the very last stage of life without exception, they are therefore called “age-bringers.”

Purisayugo yasmā tasmiṃ vaṃse sañjātapurisaṭṭhitiyā paricchinno, tasmā āha “vaṃsasambhave purise”ti. Rājagehato āhaṭabhikkhāya yāpentoti iminā kumārakapabbajjāya upagatabhāvaṃ dasseti.

Because a generation of men is defined by the continuity of men born in that lineage, therefore it is said, “a man born of lineage.” “They maintained themselves on alms brought from the royal house”: by this, he shows that he had undertaken the prince’s going-forth.

Parihariyamānovāti aññena aññena parihariyamāno viya velāya velāya tena mahatā parijanena upaṭṭhiyamāno kumārakīḷaṃ kīḷīti attho. Keci pana “parihariyamāno evā”ti avadhāraṇavasena atthaṃ vadanti, tathā sati caturāsītivassasahassāni thaññapāyī taruṇadārako ahosīti āpajjatīti tadayuttaṃ. Kumārakālaṃ vatvā tadanantaraṃ oparajjavacanato viruddhañcetaṃ. (Pañcamaṅgalavacanena unnaṅgalamaṅgalaukkantanamaṅgalakammahāyamaṅgaladussamaṅgalāni samupagatāni eva ahesunti daṭṭhabbaṃ).

“Being carried about” means: being attended upon from time to time by that great retinue, as if being carried from one place to another, he played the games of a prince; this is the meaning. Some, however, state the meaning emphatically as “just being carried about”; if so, it would follow that he was a young, suckling infant for eighty-four thousand years, which is inappropriate. And this is contradictory to the statement about the viceroyalty that comes immediately after speaking of his time as a prince. (It should be understood that by the “five auspicious utterances,” the auspicious ceremonies of unyoking the plough, cutting the hair, the great work, and cloths were indeed included).

311. Savaṃsavasena āgatā puttanattuādayo puttā ca paputtā ca etissāti puttapaputtakā paramparā. Nihatanti nihitaṃ ṭhapitaṃ, pavattitanti attho. Nihatanti vā satataṃ patiṭṭhitabhāvena vaḷañjitanti attho. Tenāha “kalyāṇavatta”nti. Atirekatarā dve guṇāti mahāsattassa maghadevakālato atirekatarā dve guṇā itararājūhi pana atirekatarā anekasatasahassappabhedā eva guṇā ahesunti.

311. The succession of sons and great-grandsons means: the sons, grandsons, and so on, who have come by way of his own lineage, are his sons and great-grandsons. “Established” means placed, set down; the meaning is set in motion. Or, “established” means used in a state of being constantly established. Therefore he said, “of virtuous conduct.” “Two more excellent qualities” means: the Great Being had two qualities more excellent than in the time of Maghadeva; however, compared with other kings, his qualities were indeed of many hundreds of thousands of different kinds, more excellent.

312. Tettiṃsa sahapuññakārino ettha nibbattāti taṃsahacaritaṭṭhānaṃ tettiṃsaṃ, tadeva tāvatiṃsaṃ, taṃnivāso etesanti tāvatiṃsā. Nivāsabhāvo ca tesaṃ tattha nibbattanapubbakoti āha – “devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānanti tāvatiṃsabhavane nibbattadevāna”nti. Raññoti nimimahārājassa. Ovāde ṭhatvāti “sīlaṃ arakkhanto mama santikaṃ mā āgacchatū”ti niggaṇhanavasenapi, “ekantato mama vijite vasantena sīlaṃ rakkhitabba”nti evaṃ pavattitaovādavasenapi ovāde ṭhatvā.

312. Because thirty-three co-merit-makers were born there, the place of their association is the Thirty-Three; that itself is Tāvatiṃsa. Those whose abode this is are the Tāvatiṃsa devas. And their state of dwelling is preceded by birth there; thus it is said: “of the Tāvatiṃsa devas” means “of the devas born in the Tāvatiṃsa realm.” “Of the king” means of the great king Nimi. “Standing in his admonition” means standing in his admonition both by way of the restraint, “Let one who does not guard virtue not come near me,” and by way of the established admonition, “Living entirely within my dominion, virtue must be guarded.”

Atha [M 2.0149] nanti mahājutikaṃ mahāvipphāraṃ mahānubhāvaṃ nimirājānaṃ. “Sakkohamasmi devindo, tava santikamāgato”ti attano sakkabhāvaṃ pavedetvā “kaṅkhaṃ te paṭivinodessāmī”ti āha. Tenāha “sabbabhūtānamissarā”tiādi.

The word "him" (naṃ) refers to King Nimi, who was of great radiance, vast influence, and great power. "I am Sakka, lord of gods, come into your presence," declaring his identity as Sakka, he said, "I will dispel your doubt." Hence, he said, "the lord of all beings," and so on.

Sīlaṃ [V 2.0147] upādāya omakatāya “ki”nti hīḷento vadati. Guṇavisiṭṭhatāyāti lābhayasādīnañceva piyamanāpatādīnañca āsavakkhayapariyosānānaṃ nimittabhāvena uttamaguṇatāya. Tadā sakko anuruddhatthero, so attano purimajātiyaṃ paccakkhasiddhaṃva dānato sīlaṃ mahantaṃ vibhāvento “ahañhī”tiādimāha. Tattha attanā vasiyamānaṃ kāmāvacaradevalokaṃ sandhāya “pettivisayato”ti vuttaṃ. Tassa hi kappasatasahassaṃ vivaṭṭajjhāsayassa pūritapāramissa devaloko petaloko viya upaṭṭhāsi. Tenevāha “accharāgaṇasaṅghuṭṭhaṃ, pisācagaṇasevita”nti (saṃ. ni. 1.46).

He speaks disparagingly of virtue, saying 'What?', because of its inferiority. 'Due to excellence in qualities' means: due to the supreme quality of being a sign of gains, fame, and so on, and of pleasant and agreeable things, and so on, culminating in the destruction of the taints. At that time, Sakka was the Elder Anuruddha. Explaining that virtue is greater than giving, as was directly evident in his own past life, he said, 'For I...,' and so on. Therein, referring to the sense-sphere divine world which was under his control, it is said, 'from the realm of the departed.' For to him, whose intention was for turning away from saṃsāra for a hundred thousand eons and who had fulfilled the perfections, the divine world appeared like the world of ghosts. Therefore he said, 'resounding with hosts of nymphs, attended by hordes of pisācas' (Saṃ. Ni. 1.46).

Khattiyeti khattiyajātiyaṃ. Visujjhatīti brahmalokūpapattiṃ sandhāya vadati kāmasaṃkilesavisujjhanato. Kāyāti ca brahmakāyamāha.

'Khattiya' means in the khattiya caste. 'Is purified' refers to attaining rebirth in the Brahma-world, being purified from the defilements of sensual desire. 'Body' refers to the Brahma-body.

Imassa mama adiṭṭhapubbarūpaṃ disvā “ahudeva bhaya”nti cintetvā āha “avikampamāno”ti. Bhāyanto hi cittassa aññathattena kāyassa ca chambhitattena vikampati nāma. Tenāha “abhāyamāno”ti. Sukhaṃ kathetuṃ hotīti puññaphalaṃ kathetuṃ sukhaṃ hoti.

Having seen this form of mine, which he had never seen before, he thought, 'There was indeed fear,' and said, 'without trembling.' For one who is afraid indeed trembles, due to the alteration of the mind and the agitation of the body. Therefore, he said, 'not fearing.' 'It is pleasant to speak' means it is pleasant to speak of the fruit of merit.

313. Manaṃ āgamma yuttāyeva hontīti mātalissa sakkasseva cittaṃ jānitvā yuttā viya honti, rathe yuttaājānīyakiccaṃ karonti devaputtā. Evaṃ tādise kāle tathā paṭipajjanti, yathā erāvaṇo devaputto hatthikiccaṃ. Naddhito paṭṭhāyāti rathapañjarapariyantena akkhassa sambandhaṭṭhānaṃ naddhī, tato paṭṭhāya. Akkho bajjhati etthāti akkhabaddho, akkhena rathassa baddhaṭṭhānaṃ. Yathā devalokato yāva candamaṇḍalassa gamanavīthi, tāva attano ānubhāvena heṭṭhāmukhameva rathaṃ pesesi, evaṃ candamaṇḍalassa gamanavīthito yāva rañño pāsādo, tāva tatheva pesesi. Dve magge dassetvāti patodalaṭṭhiyā ākāsaṃ vilikhanto viya attano ānubhāvena nirayagāmī devalokagāmī cāti dve magge [M 2.0150] dassetvā. Katamenātiādi desanāmattaṃ, yathā tena rathena gacchantassa nirayo devaloko ca pākaṭā honti, tathā karaṇaṃ adhippetaṃ.

313. 'They are yoked in accordance with the mind' means that the devaputtas, knowing the mind of Mātali and Sakka, are as if yoked; they perform the function of thoroughbreds yoked to the chariot. Thus, at such a time, they act in such a way, just as the devaputta Eravana performs the function of an elephant. 'From the strap' means: the place of connection for the axle at the end of the chariot-frame is the strap; from there onwards. 'Where the axle is bound' is `akkhabaddho`, the place where the chariot is bound by the axle. Just as from the divine world as far as the path of the moon's orb, he sent the chariot facing downwards by his own power, so from the path of the moon's orb as far as the king's palace, he sent it in the very same way. 'Having shown the two paths' means: as if drawing on the sky with his goad-stick, by his own power he showed the two paths, the one leading to hell and the one leading to the divine world. 'By which...,' and so on, is merely a teaching; the intention is the acting in such a way that for one going by that chariot, hell and the divine world become manifest.

Vuttakāraṇameva sandhāyāha mahāsatto “ubhayeneva maṃ mātali nehī”ti. Dugganti duggamaṃ. Vettaraṇinti evaṃnāmakaṃ nirayaṃ. Kuthitanti pakkuthitaṃ nipakkatelasadisajālaṃ. Khārasaṃyuttanti khārodakasadisaṃ.

Referring to the very reason that was stated, the great being said, 'Mātali, lead me by both.' `Dugga` means difficult to traverse. `Vettaraṇi` means the hell of that name. `Kuthita` means boiling, a flame like boiling oil. `Khārasaṃyutta` means like caustic water.

Rathaṃ nivattetvāti nirayābhimukhato nivattetvā. Bīraṇīdevadhītāyāti “bīraṇī”ti evaṃnāmikāya [V 2.0148] accharāya. Soṇadinnadevaputtassāti “soṇadinno”ti evaṃnāmakassa devaputtassa. Gaṇadevaputtānanti gaṇavasena puññaṃ katvā gaṇavaseneva nibbattadevaputtānaṃ.

'Having turned the chariot back' means having turned it back from facing hell. 'Of the deva's daughter Bīraṇī' means of the nymph named 'Bīraṇī'. 'Of the devaputta Soṇadinna' means of the devaputta named 'Soṇadinna'. 'Of the group-devaputtas' means of the devaputtas who were reborn as a group after having performed merit as a group.

Pattakāleti upakaṭṭhāya velāya. Atithinti paccekasambuddhaṃ. Kassapassa bhagavato sāsane ekaṃ khīṇāsavattherantipi vadanti. Mātāva puttaṃ sakimābhinandīti yathā pavāsato āgataṃ puttaṃ mātā sakiṃ ekavāraṃ āgatakāle abhinandati, tathā niccakāle abhinandi sakkaccaṃ parivisi. Saṃyamā saṃvibhāgāti sīlasaṃyamā saṃvibhāgasīlā. Jātaketi nimijātake.

`Pattakāle` means at the appropriate time. `Atithi` means a paccekabuddha. They also say it means a certain elder who was an arahant in the dispensation of the Blessed One Kassapa. 'A mother rejoices in her son once' means: just as a mother rejoices once, at the single time of his arrival, in a son who has returned from abroad, so too did he always rejoice and serve respectfully. `Saṃyamā saṃvibhāgā` means restraint in terms of virtue, and the virtue of sharing. `Jātake` means in the Nimi Jātaka.

Cittakūṭanti devanagarassa dakkhiṇadisāya dvārakoṭṭhakaṃ. Sakko cittaṃ sandhāretuṃ asakkontoti mahāsatte pavattaṃ devatānaṃ sakkārasammānaṃ paṭicca uppannaṃ attano usūyacittaṃ bahi anāvikatvā abbhantareyeva ca naṃ ṭhapetuṃ asakkonto. Aññesaṃ puññena vasāhīti sakkassa mahāsattaṃ rosetukāmatāya ārādhanaṃ nidasseti. Purāṇasakko dīghāyuko, taṃ upādāya jarājiṇṇaṃ viya katvā “jarasakko”ti vuttaṃ.

`Cittakūṭa` means the gate-chamber on the southern side of the city of the devas. 'Sakka, being unable to control his mind' means: being unable to keep his own jealous thought—which had arisen on account of the honor and respect shown by the deities towards the great being—from being revealed externally, and being unable to keep it just inside. 'Live by the merit of others' shows Sakka's invitation, born of his desire to anger the great being. The former Sakka was long-lived; with reference to him, having made himself seem old and decrepit, he was called 'the old Sakka'.

315. Sesaṃ sabbanti pabbajjupagamanā sesaṃ attano vaṃse porāṇarājūnaṃ rājacārittaṃ. Pākatikanti puna sabhāvattameva gato ahosi, apabbajitabhāvavacanenevassa brahmavihārabhāvanādīnaṃ pabbajjāguṇānaṃ abhāvo dīpito hoti.

315. `Sesaṃ sabbaṃ` means the remaining royal conduct of the ancient kings in his own lineage, other than going forth into homelessness. `Pākatika` means he returned to his natural state; by the very statement of his state of not having gone forth, the absence of the virtues of homelessness, such as the development of the divine abidings, is shown.

316. Vīriyaṃ akaronto samucchindati, na tāva samucchinnaṃ, kalyāṇamittasaṃsaggādipaccayasamavāye sati sīlavataṃ kalyāṇavattaṃ pavattetuṃ sakkoti[M 2.0151]. Dussīlena samucchinnaṃ nāma hoti tassa tattha nirāsabhāvena paṭipattiyā eva asambhavato. Satta sekhā pavattenti kalyāṇavattassa apariniṭṭhitakiccattā. Khīṇāsavena pavattitaṃ nāma pariniṭṭhitakiccattā. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva.

316. One who does not make an effort cuts it off, but it is not yet cut off; when there is a combination of conditions such as association with good friends, one is able to maintain the good conduct of the virtuous. By one who is immoral, it is said to be cut off, because, due to his lack of longing for it, practice is impossible. The seven trainees maintain it, because their task regarding good conduct is unfinished. By one whose taints are destroyed, it is said to be maintained, because his task is finished. The rest is easy to understand.

Maghadevasuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

The Elucidation of the Hidden Meaning, from the commentary on the Maghadeva Sutta, is completed.

4. Madhurasuttavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Madhura Sutta

317. Madhurāyanti [V 2.0149] uttaramadhurāyaṃ. Gundāvaneti kāḷasippalivane. Atimuttakavaneti ca vadanti. Catūsu vaṇṇesu brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo. Paṇḍaroti parisuddho. Kāḷakoti aparisuddho. Jātigottādipaññāpanaṭṭhānesūti jātigottādivasena suddhacintāyaṃ brāhmaṇā eva suddhajātikā, na itareti adhippāyo. Saṃsārato vā suddhacintāyaṃ brāhmaṇāva sujjhanti vedavihitassa suddhavidhino aññesaṃ avisayattāti adhippāyo. Taṃ panetaṃ tesaṃ virujjhati khattiyavessānampi mantajjhenassa anuññātattā, mantajjhenavidhinā ca saṃsārasuddhiyābhāvato. Puttā nāma anorasāpi honti, na tathā imeti āha “orasā”ti. Ure saṃvaḍḍhitaputtopi “orasa”nti vuccati. Ime pana mukhato niggato hutvā ure saṃvaḍḍhāti dassetuṃ “orasā mukhato jātā”ti vuttaṃ. Tato eva brahmato jātāti brahmajā, brahmasambhūtāpi “brahmajā”ti vuccanti, na tathā ime. Ime pana paccakkhato brahmunā nimmitāti brahmanimmitā, tato eva brahmato laddhabbavijjādidāyajjadāyādāti brahmadāyādāti sabbametaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ katthanāpalāpasadisaṃ viññūnaṃ appamāṇaṃ avimaddakkhamaṃ vācāvatthumattaṃ brahmakuttasseva abhāvato. Yaṃ panettha vattabbaṃ, taṃ visuddhimaggavaṇṇanāyaṃ vuttameva. Tenāha “ghosoyevā”tiādi. Vohāramattamevetanti etaṃ “brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo”tiādi vacanamattameva, na tassa attho tehi adhippetappakāro atthi.

317. "In Madhurā" means in Uttaramadhurā. "In Gundāvana" means in the Kāḷasippali forest. They also call it the Atimuttaka forest. "Among the four castes, the brahmin is the highest caste." "White" means pure. "Black" means impure. "In matters of declaring birth, clan, etc." means: with regard to the pure thought concerning birth, clan, etc., the meaning is that only brahmins are of pure birth, not others. Or, with regard to the pure thought concerning saṃsāra, the meaning is that only brahmins are purified, because the method of purification prescribed by the Vedas is not accessible to others. But this contradicts their view, because the study of the mantras is also permitted for khattiyas and vessas, and because there is no purification from saṃsāra through the method of studying the mantras. Sons can indeed be not born from the breast, but these are not so; thus he said "born from the breast." A son raised on the breast is also called "orasa" (born from the breast). But to show that these, having issued from the mouth, are raised on the breast, it is said, "born from the breast, born from the mouth." Therefore, "born from Brahmā" means brahmajā. Those sprung from Brahmā are also called "brahmajā," but these are not so. But these are "created by Brahmā" because they are directly created by Brahmā. Therefore, they are "heirs of Brahmā" because they are heirs to the inheritance of knowledge, etc., to be received from Brahmā. All this is like the boasting and prattling of the brahmins, unauthoritative for the wise, unable to withstand scrutiny, a mere matter of words, because there is no such thing as a Brahmā-deed. Whatever should be said here has already been said in the commentary on the Visuddhimagga. Therefore, he said, "It is only a sound," and so on. "It is merely a convention" means that this statement, "The brahmin is the highest caste," etc., is merely a saying; it does not have the kind of meaning intended by them.

318. Samijjheyyāti diṭṭhidīpanavasena attano ajjhāsayo nipphajjeyya. Tenāha “manoratho pūreyyā”ti. Khattiyopīti parakhattiyopi[M 2.0152]. Assāti samiddhadhanādiṃ pattassa. Tenāha – “issariyasampattassā”ti nesanti etesaṃ catunnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ ettha pubbuṭṭhāyibhāvādinā itarehi upacaritabbatāya na kiñci nānākaraṇanti yojanā.

318. "May it succeed" means: may his own inclination be accomplished by way of illuminating his view. Therefore, he said, "May his wish be fulfilled." "A khattiya also" means another khattiya. "Of him" means of one who has attained abundant wealth, etc. Therefore, he said, "of one who has attained sovereignty." The construction is: "there is no distinction whatsoever" among these four castes here, in that they should be served by the others by rising before them, etc.

322. Ahaṃ [V 2.0150] cīvarādīhi upaṭṭhāko, tumhākaṃ icchitacchitakkhaṇe vadeyyātha yenatthoti yojanā. Corādiupaddavanisedhanena rakkhāgutti, dānādinimittaupaddavanisedhanena āvaraṇagutti. Paccuppannānatthanisedhanena vā rakkhāgutti, āgāmianatthanisedhanena āvaraṇagutti. Ettha ca khattiyādīsu yo yo issaro, tassa itarena anuvattetabbabhāve, kusalākusalakaraṇena nesaṃ vasena laddhabbaabhisamparāye, pabbajitehi laddhabbasāmīcikiriyāya ca aṇumattopi viseso natthi, tasmā so visesābhāvo pāḷiyaṃ tattha tattha vāre “evaṃ sante”tiādinā vibhāvito. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva.

322. The construction is: "I am an attendant with robes, etc.; at the moment you desire, you should state what is needed." "Safeguard and protection" is by preventing calamities from thieves, etc. "Shelter and protection" is by preventing calamities caused by giving, etc. Or, "safeguard and protection" is by preventing present misfortunes; "shelter and protection" is by preventing future misfortunes. And here, among the khattiyas and others, whoever is a lord, there is not even the slightest difference in the fact that he should be followed by another, in the future state to be obtained through their power by doing what is wholesome and unwholesome, and in the proper conduct to be received from the renunciants. Therefore, this lack of difference is clarified in the Pāli text in various sections with the words, "This being so," etc. The rest is easily understood.

Madhurasuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

The Elucidation of the Hidden Meaning in the Commentary on the Madhura Sutta is concluded.

5. Bodhirājakumārasuttavaṇṇanā

5. The Commentary on the Bodhirājakumāra Sutta.

324. Olokanakapadumanti [V 2.0151] līlāaravindaṃ. Tasmāti kokanadasaṇṭhānattā kokanadoti saṅkhaṃ labhi.

324. "A lotus for looking at" means a lotus for amusement. "Therefore" means: because it has the shape of a red lotus, it obtained the name "kokanada."

325. Yāva pacchima…pe… phalakaṃ vuttaṃ tassa sabbapacchā santhatattā. Uparimaphalagatañhi sopānamatthakaṃ. Olokanatthaṃyevāti na kevalaṃ bhagavato āgamanaññeva olokanatthaṃ, atha kho attano patthanāya santharāpitāya celapaṭikāya akkamanassapi.

325. "As far as the last... etc... plank" is said because it was spread out last of all. For the top of the stairs is on the upper plank. "For the purpose of looking" means not only for the purpose of looking at the Blessed One's arrival, but also at his treading upon the strip of cloth that had been spread at his own request.

Sakuṇapotaketi kādambaṭiṭṭibhaputtake. Aññova bhaveyyāti tasmiṃ attabhāve mātugāmato añño idāni bhariyābhūto mātugāmo bhaveyya. Puttaṃ labheyyāti attano kammavasena puttaṃ, no tassa. Ubhohīti imehi eva ubhohi. Imehi kāraṇehīti tassa rājakumārassa buddhaṃ paṭicca micchāgahaṇaṃ, titthiyānaṃ ujjhāyanaṃ, anāgate manussānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ uddissa vippaṭisāroti imehi tīhi kāraṇehi. Paññattanti santhataṃ celapaṭikaṃ. Maṅgalaṃ icchantīti maṅgalikā.

"Young birds" means the young of geese and partridges. "Would be another" means: in that existence, the woman who is now his wife would be a different woman. "He would obtain a son" means a son through the power of his own kamma, not hers. "By both" means by these two alone. "For these reasons" means for these three reasons: the prince's wrong grasp concerning the Buddha, the complaining of the sectarians, and the future regret of people concerning the bhikkhus. "Prepared" means the spread strip of cloth. "They desire a good omen" means they are superstitious.

326. Tatiyaṃ [M 2.0153] kāraṇanti iminā bhikkhūsu vippaṭisārānuppādanamāha. Yaṃ kiñci paribhuñjana-sukhaṃ kāmasukhallikānuyogoti adhippāyena kāmasukhallikānuyogasaññī hutvā…pe… maññamāno evamāha.

326. By "the third reason," he speaks of the non-arising of regret in the bhikkhus. With the intention that "whatever pleasure of enjoyment is the practice of indulgence in sensual pleasures," having the perception of the practice of indulgence in sensual pleasures... etc... thinking thus, he spoke.

327. Atha naṃ bhagavā tato micchābhinivesato vivecetukāmo “so kho aha”ntiādinā attano dukkaracariyaṃ dassetuṃ ārabhi. Mahāsaccake(ma. ni. 1.364 ādayo) vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ “so kho aha”ntiādipāṭhassa tattha āgataniyāmeneva āgatattā. Pāsarāsisutte (ma. ni. 1.272 ādayo) vuttanayenāti etthāpi eseva nayo.

327. Then the Blessed One, wishing to detach him from that wrong adherence, began to show his own austere practice with the words, "I, indeed..." and so on. It should be understood in the same way as stated in the Mahāsaccaka Sutta, because the text beginning "I, indeed..." occurs there in the same manner. "In the way stated in the Pāsarāsi Sutta"—here too, the method is the same.

343. Aṅkusaṃ gaṇhanti etena tassa gahaṇe cheko hotīti aṅkusagahaṇasippaṃ. Meghautunti meghaṃ paṭicca uppannasītautuṃ. Pabbatautunti pabbataṃ paṭicca uṇhautuṃ. Ubhayavasena ca tassa [V 2.0152] tathā sītuṇhaututo eno āgatoti ta-kārassa da-kāraṃ katvā udenoti nāmaṃ akāsi.

343. "The skill of taking the goad" is so called because by this one becomes skilled in taking it. "The cloud-season" means the cold season that arises on account of the clouds. "The mountain-season" means the hot season that arises on account of the mountain. And because a fault came to him from both the cold and hot seasons in that way, he made the name "Udena" by changing the letter 't' to 'd'.

Tāpaso ogāḷhañāṇavasena rañño matabhāvaṃ ñatvā. Ādito paṭṭhāyāti kosambinagare parantaparañño aggamahesibhāvato paṭṭhāya. Pubbeti sīlavantakāle. Hatthiganthanti hatthīnaṃ attano vase vattāpanasatthaṃ. Tenevassa taṃ sikkhāpeti, kiccañca ijjhati.

The ascetic, having known through the power of his profound knowledge that the king was dead. "From the beginning" means from the time of being the chief queen of King Parantapa in the city of Kosambī. "Formerly" means at the time when he was virtuous. "The elephant lore" means the science of bringing elephants under one's own control. Therefore, he teaches it to him, and the task succeeds.

344. Padahanabhāvoti bhāvanānuyogo. Padhāne vā niyutto padhāniyo, padhāniyassa bhikkhuno, tasseva padhāniyabhāvassa aṅgāni kāraṇāni padhāniyaṅgāni. Saddhā etassa atthīti saddho. Kiñcāpi paccekabodhisattānampi abhinīhārato paṭṭhāya āgatā āgamanasaddhā eva, mahābodhisattānaṃ pana saddhā garutarāti sā eva gahitā. Acalabhāvena okappanaṃ “sammāsambuddho bhagavā, svākhyāto dhammo, suppaṭipanno saṅgho”ti kenaci akampiyabhāvena ratanattayaguṇe ogāhitvā kappanaṃ. Pasāduppatti ratanattaye pasīdanameva. Bodhinti catumaggañāṇanti vuttaṃ taṃnimittattā sabbaññutaññāṇassa, bodhīti vā sammāsambodhi. Sabbaññutaññāṇapadaṭṭhānañhi maggañāṇaṃ, maggañāṇapadaṭṭhānañca sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ “sammāsambodhī”ti vuccati. Nicchitasubuddhatāya dhammassa sudhammatā saṅghassa suppaṭipatti vinicchitā eva [M 2.0154] hotīti āha “desanāsīsameva ceta”ntiādi. Tassa padhānaṃ vīriyaṃ ijjhati ratanattayasaddhāya “imāya paṭipadāya jarāmaraṇato muccissāmī”ti padhānānuyoge avaṃmukhasambhavato.

344. "The state of striving" means the practice of meditation. Or, one engaged in striving is a striver; of a striving bhikkhu, the factors or causes of that very state of striving are the "limbs of striving." "Faithful" means one who has faith. Although for paccekabodhisattas also, from their aspiration onwards, there is only faith based on scripture, the faith of mahābodhisattas is weightier, so that alone is taken. "Conviction" is unwavering trust, a placing of confidence in the qualities of the Three Jewels with an unshakable quality by anyone, thinking, "The Blessed One is a perfectly enlightened one, the Dhamma is well-proclaimed, the Saṅgha is of good conduct." "The arising of confidence" is simply confidence in the Three Jewels. "Enlightenment" is said to be the knowledge of the four paths, because it is the cause of the knowledge of omniscience; or "enlightenment" is perfect self-enlightenment. For the knowledge of the path is the proximate cause of the knowledge of omniscience, and the knowledge of omniscience, which has the knowledge of the path as its proximate cause, is called "perfect self-enlightenment." Because the good Dhamma-nature of the Dhamma and the good conduct of the Saṅgha are determined by the certain perfect enlightenment, he said, "This is only the head of the teaching," and so on. His striving, his energy, succeeds because, through faith in the Three Jewels, there is no turning back in the practice of striving, thinking, "By this practice, I will be freed from old age and death."

Appābādhotiādi heṭṭhā vuttameva. Aguṇaṃ pakāsetā āyatiṃ saṃvaraṃ āpajjitā sammāpaṭipattiyā visodhanatthaṃ. Udayañca atthañca gantunti “avijjāsamudayā”tiādinā pañcannaṃ upādānakkhandhānaṃ udayañca vayañca jānituṃ. Tenāha “etenā”tiādi. Parisuddhāya upakkilesavinimuttāya. Nibbijjhitunti tadaṅgavasena pajahituṃ samucchedappahānassa paccayo bhavituṃ. Yaṃ dukkhaṃ khīyatīti kilesesu appahīnesu tena tadupanissayakammaṃ paṭicca yaṃ dukkhaṃ uppajjeyya, taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ.

The phrase beginning with 'of little affliction' has already been explained below. For the purpose of purification through right practice, having undertaken future restraint, he discloses his fault. 'To go to the arising and passing away' means to know the arising and passing away of the five aggregates of clinging, by way of the phrase beginning with 'from the arising of ignorance.' Therefore, he said the phrase beginning with 'by this.' By that which is pure, freed from defilements. 'To become disenchanted' means to abandon by way of substitution, to be a condition for eradication by cutting off. 'What suffering is destroyed' is said with reference to what suffering would arise, conditioned by the kamma that is supported by it, when defilements are not abandoned.

345. Sesadivaseti sattadivasato paṭṭhāya yāva dve rattindivā.

345. 'On the remaining days' means from the seventh day up to two days and nights.

346. Kucchisannissito [V 2.0153] gabbho nissayavohārena “kucchī”ti vuccati, so etissā atthīti kucchimatī. Tenāha “āpannasattā”ti. Ārakkho panassa paccupaṭṭhito hotīti mātarā gahitasaraṇaṃ gabbhavuṭṭhitassa tassa saraṇagamanaṃ pavedayitassa kusalaṃ saraṇaṃ nāma, mātu katarakkho puttassapi paccupaṭṭhitoti. Mahallakakāleti vacanatthaṃ jānanakāle. Sārentīti yathādiṭṭhaṃ yathābalaṃ ratanattayaguṇapatiṭṭhāpanavasena assa sārenti. Sallakkhetvāti vuttamatthaṃ upadhāretvā. Saraṇaṃ gahitaṃ nāma hoti ratanattayassa saraṇabhāvasallakkhaṇapubbakatanninnacittabhāvatova. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva.

346. The fetus, being dependent on the womb, is called 'womb' by way of relational designation; she who has this is 'one with a womb' (kucchimatī). Therefore, it is said, 'a pregnant woman' (āpannasattā). 'Protection is established for him' means that the refuge taken by the mother is called a wholesome refuge for him who has emerged from the womb, for whom the going for refuge has been made known; the protection made by the mother is also established for the son. 'At an older age' means at the time of knowing the meaning of words. 'They remind' means they remind him according to what has been seen and according to their ability, by way of establishing the qualities of the Three Jewels. 'Having discerned' means having considered the meaning that was spoken. The taking of refuge occurs precisely from the state of mind being inclined towards it, preceded by the discernment of the nature of the Three Jewels as a refuge. The rest is easy to understand.

Bodhirājakumārasuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

The explanation of the hidden meaning in the commentary on the Bodhirājakumāra Sutta is concluded.

6. Aṅgulimālasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Aṅgulimāla Sutta

347. Aṅgulīnaṃ [V 2.0154] mālaṃ dhāretīti iminā anvatthā tassa samaññāti dasseti. Tatrāti tasmiṃ ācariyavacanena aṅgulimālassa dhāraṇe. Karīsasahassakhette ekasālisīsaṃ viya apaññāyamānasakakicco hotīti adhippāyo. Takkasīlaṃ pesayiṃsu “tādisassa ācariyassa santike [M 2.0155] sippuggahasammāpayogena diṭṭhadhammike samparāyike ca atthe jānanto bhāriyaṃ na kareyyā”ti. Bāhirakā ahesuṃ ahiṃsakassa vattasampattiyā ācariyassa cittasabhāvato nibbattanatibhāvena. Sineheneva vadanteti sinehena viya vadante.

347. 'He wears a garland of fingers'—by this, it shows that his name is appropriate. 'There' means in that instance of wearing the garland of fingers by the teacher's word. The meaning is that his own task was imperceptible, like a single head of rice in a field of a thousand karīsas. They sent him to Takkasilā, thinking, 'Knowing the benefits in this life and in the future through the proper application of learning the craft in the presence of such a teacher, he would not do anything burdensome.' They became outsiders due to the excessive favor produced from the teacher's mental disposition on account of Ahiṃsaka's accomplishment in conduct. 'They speak with affection' means they speak as if with affection.

Gaṇanampi na uggaṇhātīti gaṇanavidhimpi na sallakkheti. Tattha kāraṇamāha “pakatiyā”tiādinā. Ṭhapitaṭṭhāneti rukkhagacchantarādike ṭhapitaṭṭhāne sakuntasiṅgālānaṃ vasena aṅguliyo vinassanti. Bhaggavoti kosalarañño purohitaṃ gottena vadati. Coro avissāsanīyo sāhasikabhāvato. Purāṇasanthatā sākhā avissāsanīyā vicchikādīnaṃ pavesanayogyattā. Rājā avissāsanīyo issariyamadena dhanalobhena ca kadāci jīvite saṅkābhāvato. Itthī avissāsanīyā lolasīlacittabhāvato. Anuddharaṇīyo bhavissati saṃsārapaṅkato.

'He does not even learn counting' means he does not discern the method of counting. Therein, he states the reason with the phrase beginning 'by nature.' 'In the place where they are put' means in a place where they are put, such as among trees and bushes, the fingers are destroyed by birds and jackals. 'Bhaggava'—he speaks of the chaplain of the king of Kosala by his clan name. A thief is untrustworthy because of his rash nature. An old mat is untrustworthy because it is suitable for scorpions and so on to enter. A king is untrustworthy due to intoxication with power and greed for wealth, and because there is sometimes no security in life from him. A woman is untrustworthy because of her fickle-natured mind. He will be un-rescuable from the mire of saṃsāra.

348. Saṅkaritvāti “mayaṃ ekajjhaṃ sannipatitvā coraṃ māretvā vā palāpetvā gamissāmā”ti saṅkaraṃ katvā. Iddhābhisaṅkhāranti abhisaṅkharaṇaṃ adhiṭṭhānaṃ. Abhisaṅkhāsīti adhiṭṭhahi. Saṃharitvāti saṃkhipitvā. Orabhāgeti corassa orabhāge.

348. 'Having made an agreement' means having made an agreement, thinking, 'Let us gather together, kill the thief or make him flee, and then go.' 'Psychic formation' means formation, determination. 'He formed' means he determined. 'Having drawn it together' means having contracted it. 'On the near side' means on the near side of the thief.

349. Daṇḍoti paharaṇahatthacchedanādiko daṇḍanasaṅkhāto daṇḍo. Pavattayitabboti ānetabbo. Apanetvāti attano santānato samucchedavasena pahāya. Paṭisaṅkhāyāti paṭisaṅkhānena. Avihiṃsāyāti karuṇāya. Sāraṇīyadhammesūti chasupi sāraṇīyadhammesu, ṭhito aṭṭhitānaṃ pāpadhammānaṃ bodhimūle eva samucchinnattā. Yathā atīte aparimitaṃ kālaṃ sandhāvitaṃ, evaṃ imāya paṭipattiyā anāgatepi sandhāvissatīti dassento “idānī”tiādimāha.

349. 'Punishment (daṇḍa)' refers to the punishment so-called, such as beating, cutting off hands, and the like. 'To be set in motion' means to be brought about. 'Having removed' means having abandoned by way of eradication from one's own mental continuum. 'Having reflected' means by reflection. 'For non-harming' means by compassion. 'In the qualities that make for fellowship' refers to the six qualities that make for fellowship; he is established in them, because unestablished evil qualities were completely uprooted right at the root of awakening. Showing that just as he has transmigrated for an immeasurable time in the past, so too by this current practice of his he will transmigrate in the future, he says the phrase beginning with 'now'.

Itvevāti iti eva, iti-saddo nidassanattho. Tenāha “evaṃ vatvā yevā”ti. Akirīti ākiri, pañcapi āvudhāni vikiri. Tena vuttaṃ “khipi chaḍḍesī”ti.

'Thus indeed' means 'iti eva'; the word 'iti' has the meaning of an example. Therefore, it is said, 'having spoken thus, indeed.' 'Akiri' means he scattered; he scattered all five weapons. Hence, it is said, 'he threw, he discarded'.

350. Ettovāti [V 2.0155] ato eva āgatamaggeneva sāvatthiṃ gatā. Adhivāsessatīti “coraṃ paṭisedhetuṃ gamissāmī”ti vutte tuṇhī bhavissati[M 2.0156]. Dāruṇakammena uppannanāmanti “aṅgulimālo”ti imaṃ nāmaṃ sandhāya vadati.

350. 'Just from here' means from that very place, she went to Sāvatthī by the very path she had come. 'He will consent' means he will remain silent when it is said, 'I will go to stop the thief.' 'A name that arose from a cruel deed'—he says this with reference to the name 'Aṅgulimāla'.

351. Hatthī araññahatthī honti manussānaṃ tattha gantuṃ asakkuṇeyyattā, evaṃ assāpi. Kūṭasahassānaṃ bhijjanakāraṇaṃ hoti therassa āgamanabhayena ghaṭe chaḍḍetvā palāyanena. Gabbhamūḷhāyāti byākulagabbhāya. Pabbajjābalenāti vuttaṃ, satthu desanānubhāvenāti pana vattabbaṃ. So hi tassāpi kāraṇanti. Ariyā nāma jāti pabbajjā ariyabhāvatthāya jātīti katvā.

351. Elephants are forest elephants, because humans are unable to go there; likewise for horses. The reason for the breaking of a thousand traps was the fleeing out of fear of the Elder's arrival, having abandoned their pots. 'For one with a confused womb' means for one with a disordered womb. 'By the power of the going forth' is said, but it should be said 'by the power of the Teacher's teaching.' For that indeed is the cause for her too. The noble birth is the going forth, it being considered a birth for the sake of the noble state.

Mahāparittaṃ nāmetanti mahānubhāvaṃ parittaṃ nāmetaṃ. Tathā hi naṃ thero sabbabhāvena ariyāya jāto saccādhiṭṭhānena akāsi. Tenāha “saccakiriyakataṭṭhāne”ti. Gabbhamūḷhanti mūḷhagabbhaṃ. Gabbho hi paripakko sampajjamāno vijāyanakāle kammajavātehi sañcāletvā parivattito uddhaṃpādo adhosīso hutvā yonimukhābhimukho hoti, evaṃ so kassaci alaggo sotthinā bahi nikkhamati, vipajjamāno pana viparivattanavasena yonimaggaṃ pidahitvā tiriyaṃ nipajjati, tathā yassā yonimaggo pidahati, sā tattha kammajavātehi aparāparaṃ parivattamānā byākulā mūḷhagabbhāti vuccati, taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “gabbhamūḷha”nti.

'This is the Great Protection' means this protection is of great power. For the Elder, born of the noble birth in every way, made it by a determination of truth. Therefore, he said, 'in the place where the act of truth was made.' 'Confused in the womb' means a confused fetus. For when the fetus is fully developed and about to be born, stirred by kamma-produced winds, it is turned and positioned head downwards, with feet upwards, facing the opening of the womb; thus, if it is not stuck anywhere, it emerges safely. But if something goes wrong, due to an incorrect turning it blocks the birth passage and lies sideways. So, the woman whose birth passage is blocked in this way, tossed repeatedly by kamma-produced winds, becomes agitated and is called 'one with a confused womb.' With reference to that, it is said, 'confused in the womb'.

Saccakiriyā nāma buddhāsayaṃ attano sīlaṃ paccavekkhitvā katā, tasmā saccakiriyā vejjakammaṃ na hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Therassapi cātiādinā upasaṅkamitabbakāraṇaṃ vadati. Ime dve hetū paṭicca bhagavā theraṃ saccakiriyaṃ kāresi. Jātinti mūlajātiṃ.

An act of truth is performed by reflecting on the Buddha’s intention and one’s own virtue. Therefore, it should be understood that an act of truth is not medical treatment. And with the phrase beginning 'Therassapi ca,' he states the reason why he should be approached. On account of these two reasons, the Blessed One had the elder perform the act of truth. 'Birth' refers to the original birth.

352. Pariyādāya āhacca bhinnena sīsena. Sabhāgadiṭṭhadhammavedanīyakammanti niraye nibbattanasakakammasabhāgabhūtaṃ diṭṭhadhammavedanīyakammaṃ. Sabhāgatā ca samānavatthukatā samānārammaṇatāekavīthipariyāpannatādivasena sabbathā sarikkhatā, sadisampi ca nāma tadevāharīyati yathā “tasseva kammassa vipāko”ti ca “sā eva tittirī tāneva osadhānī”ti ca. Idāni tameva sabhāgataṃ dassetuṃ “kammaṃ hī”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Kariyamānamevāti paccayasamavāyena paṭipāṭiyā nibbattiyamānameva. Tayo koṭṭhāse pūreti, diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaaparāpariyāyavedanīyaupapajjavedanīyasaṅkhāte tayo bhāge pūreti, tesaṃ tiṇṇaṃ bhāgānaṃ vasena pavattati.

352. Having overcome, struck, with a broken head. The term 'sabhāgadiṭṭhadhammavedanīyakamma' refers to immediately effective kamma that is similar in nature to kamma leading to rebirth in hell. And similarity (sabhāgatā) means being entirely alike in every way, such as having the same physical basis, the same object, and being comprised in one cognitive process. And even something similar is referred to as that very thing, as in 'the result of that very action' or 'that very partridge and those very medicinal herbs.' Now, to illustrate this similarity, the phrase beginning with 'kammaṃ hi' is begun. 'Being performed' means being sequentially produced by the combination of conditions. It fills three shares—namely, the three categories known as immediately effective (diṭṭhadhammavedanīya), indefinitely effective (aparāpariyāyavedanīya), and subsequently effective (upapajjavedanīya). It operates by means of these three shares.

Diṭṭhadhammo [M 2.0157][V 2.0156] vuccati paccakkhabhūto paccuppanno attabhāvo, tattha veditabbaphalaṃ kammaṃ diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṃ. Paccuppannabhavato anantaraṃ veditabbaphalaṃ kammaṃ upapajjavedanīyaṃ. Diṭṭhadhammānantarabhavato aññasmiṃ attabhāvapariyāye attabhāvaparivatte veditabbaphalaṃ kammaṃ aparāpariyāyavedanīyaṃ. Paṭipakkhehi anabhibhūtatāya, paccayavisesena paṭiladdhavisesatāya ca balavabhāvappattā tādisassa pubbābhisaṅkhārassa vasena sātisayā hutvā pavattā paṭhamajavanacetanā tasmiṃyeva attabhāve phaladāyinī diṭṭhadhammavedanīyā nāma. Sā hi vuttākārena balavati javanasantāne guṇavisesayuttesu upakārānupakāravasappavattiyā āsevanālābhena appavipākatāya ca itaradvayaṃ viya pavattasantānuparamāpekkhaṃ okāsalābhāpekkhañca kammaṃ na hotīti idheva pupphamattaṃ viya pavattivipākamattaṃ phalaṃ deti.

The present existence, which is directly perceptible, is called the visible state (diṭṭhadhamma); the kamma whose result is to be experienced therein is called immediately effective kamma. The kamma whose result is to be experienced immediately following the present existence is called subsequently effective kamma. The kamma whose result is to be experienced in a different cycle of existence, in another round of existence, beyond the existence immediately following the present one, is called indefinitely effective kamma. The first volition of impulsion, having attained a state of strength by not being overpowered by opposing factors and by attaining distinction through special conditions, and having become exceedingly powerful through the force of such previous formations, is productive of results in that very existence and is called immediately effective kamma. For it, being strong in the stream of impulsions as described, operating by way of help or harm towards those endowed with special qualities, gaining reinforcement through repetition, and having a result of little consequence, does not, like the other two, depend on the cessation of the ongoing stream of existence or await the gaining of an opportunity. Thus, in this very life, it gives a result that is merely its manifestation, like a mere flower.

Tathā asakkontanti kammassa phaladānaṃ nāma upadhipayogādipaccayantarasamavāyeneva hotīti tadabhāvato tasmiṃyeva attabhāve vipākaṃ dātuṃ asakkontaṃ. Ahosikammanti kammaṃyeva ahosi, na tassa vipāko ahosi, atthi bhavissati vāti evaṃ vattabbaṃ kammaṃ. Atthasādhikāti dānādipāṇātipātādiatthassa nipphādikā. Kā pana sāti āha “sattamajavanacetanā”ti. Sā hi sanniṭṭhāpakacetanā vuttanayena paṭiladdhavisesā purimajavanacetanāhi laddhāsevanā ca samānā anantare attabhāve vipākadāyinī upapajjavedanīyakammaṃ nāma. Tenāha “anantare attabhāve vipākaṃ detī”ti. Sati saṃsārappavattiyāti iminā asati saṃsārappavattiyā ahosikammapakkhe tiṭṭhati vipaccanokāsassa abhāvatoti.

"Unable thus" means unable to give a result in that very existence due to the absence of a convergence of other conditions, such as the substrate of existence and effort, by which the giving of kamma's fruit occurs. "Defunct kamma" (ahosikamma) is kamma of which it is to be said: "The kamma alone was; its result was not, is not, and will not be." "Accomplishing the purpose" means producing the purpose of giving, etc., or of killing living beings, etc. What is that? He says: "The volition of the seventh impulsion." For that volition, being the concluding volition which has attained distinction in the way described and has gained reinforcement from the preceding impulsions, gives a result in the immediately following existence and is called subsequently effective kamma. Therefore he said: "It gives its result in the immediately following existence." By the phrase "while the round of saṃsāra continues," it is shown that if the round of saṃsāra does not continue, it stands in the category of defunct kamma due to the absence of an opportunity for ripening.

Samugghāṭitāni vipaccanokāsassa anuppattidhammatāpādanena. Diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṃ atthi vipākārahābhāvassa anibbattitattā vipaccanokāsassa anupacchinnattā. Katūpacitañhi kammaṃ sati vipaccanokāse yāva na phalaṃ deti, tāva attheva nāma vipākārahabhāvato. “Yassa kho”ti idaṃ aniyamākāravacanaṃ bhagavatā kammasarikkhatāvasena sādhāraṇato vuttanti āha “yādisassa kho”ti.

Uprooted by bringing about the state of non-arising for the opportunity to ripen. Immediately effective kamma exists because its potential to give a result has not ceased and the opportunity for ripening has not been cut off. For kamma that has been performed and accumulated, as long as it does not give its fruit while there is an opportunity for ripening, it indeed exists because of its potential to give a result. The phrase "For whom" is an expression of an indefinite kind, spoken by the Blessed One in a general way due to the similarity of kamma; thus he says, "For whatever kind of person."

Pamādakilesavimuttoti pamādahetukehi sabbehi kilesehi vimutto.

"Freed from the defilements of negligence" means being freed from all defilements caused by negligence.

Pāpassa [M 2.0158] pidhānaṃ nāma avipākadhammatāpādananti āha “appaṭisandhikaṃ karīyatī”ti. Buddhasāsaneti [V 2.0157] sikkhāttayasaṅgahe buddhassa bhagavato sāsane. Yuttappayutto viharatīti akattabbassa akaraṇavasena, kattabbassa ca paripūraṇavasena pavattati.

The covering of evil is called bringing about the nature of non-ripening; hence it is said, "It is made incapable of relinking." "In the Buddha's Dispensation" means in the Dispensation of the Blessed One, the Buddha, which comprises the threefold training. "He dwells yoked and devoted" means he proceeds by way of not doing what should not be done and by way of fulfilling what should be done.

Dissanti kujjhantīti disā, paṭipakkhāti āha “sapattā”ti. Tappasaṃsapakāranti mettānisaṃsakittanākāraṃ. Kālenāti āmeḍitalopena niddesoti āha “khaṇe khaṇe”ti. Anukarontūti yesaṃ kalyāṇamittānaṃ santike suṇanti, yathāsutaṃ dhammaṃ tesaṃ anukarontu diṭṭhānugatikaraṇaṃ āpajjantu, attano veripuggalānampi bhagavato santike dhammassavanaṃ sammāpaṭipattiñca paccāsīsati.

"Enemies" (disā) are so called because they see one with anger; meaning opponents, he says "rivals" (sapattā). "The manner of praising that" means the manner of proclaiming the benefits of loving-kindness. "From time to time" (kālena) is a reference with elision of reduplication; thus he says "moment by moment." "Let them imitate" means: let them imitate those good friends in whose presence they listen, according to the Dhamma as heard; let them undertake to follow what has been seen. He hopes even for his own enemies that they may hear the Dhamma in the presence of the Blessed One and practice rightly.

Tasanti gatiṃ patthayantīti tasā bhavantarādīsu saṃsaraṇabhāvato. Tenāha “tasā vuccanti sataṇhā”ti.

Because they tremble (tasanti), desiring a destination, they are called tasā (trembling ones); this is due to their state of wandering in other existences and so on. Therefore he said: "Those with craving are called tasā."

Netabbaṭṭhānaṃ udakaṃ nayantīti nettikā. Bandhitvāti daḷhaṃ bandhitvā. Telakañjikenāti telamissitena kañjikena.

Because they lead water to the place where it is to be led, they are called irrigators (nettikā). "Having bound" means having bound firmly. "With oil-mixed sour gruel" means with sour gruel mixed with oil.

Yādisova aniṭṭhe, tādisova iṭṭheti iṭṭhāniṭṭhe nibbikārena tādī. Yesaṃ pana kāmāmisādīnaṃ vantattā rāgādīnaṃ cattattā kāmoghādīnaṃ tiṇṇattā tādibhāvo bhaveyya, tesaṃ bhagavatā sabbaso vantā cattā tiṇṇā, tasmā bhagavā vantāvīti tādī, cattāvīti tādī, tiṇṇāvīti tādī, yehi anaññasādhāraṇehi sīlādiguṇehi samannāgatattā bhagavā tādibhāvena ukkaṃsapāramippatto taṃniddeso, tehi guṇehi yāthāvato niddisitabbatopi tādī. Yathā yantarajjuyā yantaṃ nīyati, evaṃ yāya taṇhāya bhavo nīyati, sā “bhavanetti bhavarajjū”ti vuttā. Tenāha “tāya hī”tiādi, kammāni kusalādīni vipaccayanti apaccayanti etāyāti kammavipāko. Apaccayabhāvo nāma ariyamaggacetanāyāti āha “maggacetanāyā”ti. Yāva na kilesā pahīyanti, tāva ime sattā saiṇā eva aserivihārabhāvatoti āha “aṇaṇo nikkileso jāto”ti.

Just as one is in the face of the undesirable, so one is in the face of the desirable; one who is thus without change towards the desirable and undesirable is a tādī. For those by whom sensual pleasures and so on have been vomited, defilements like lust have been abandoned, and floods like sensual desire have been crossed, the state of being a tādī might exist. But by the Blessed One, all these have been completely vomited, abandoned, and crossed. Therefore, the Blessed One is a tādī because he has vomited, a tādī because he has abandoned, a tādī because he has crossed over. Because he is endowed with virtues such as morality and other qualities not shared by others, the Blessed One has attained the highest perfection in the state of being a tādī; this is his designation. He is also a tādī because he is to be designated truly by means of those qualities. Just as a machine is moved by a rope, so existence is led by craving; thus it is called 'the guide of existence, the rope of existence.' Hence it is said: 'By that indeed...' and so on. Through this, skillful and other actions ripen or do not ripen; this concerns the ripening of kamma. The state of non-ripening is the volition of the noble path; thus he says, 'by the volition of the path.' As long as defilements are not abandoned, these beings remain indebted, being in a state of not living independently. Thus it is said: 'He has become debtless, undefiled.'

Theyyaparibhogo (visuddhi. ṭī. 1.91) nāma sāmiparibhogābhāvato. Bhagavatāpi hi attano sāsane sīlavato paccayā anuññātā, na dussīlassa, dāyakānaṃ [M 2.0159] sīlavatoyeva pariccāgo, na dussīlassa attano kārānaṃ mahapphalabhāvassa paccāsīsanato. Iti satthārā ananuññātattā dāyakehi ca apariccattattā “dussīlassa paribhogo theyyaparibhogo nāmā”ti vuttaṃ[V 2.0158]. Iṇavasena paribhogo iṇaparibhogo. Paṭiggāhakato dakkhiṇāvisuddhiyā abhāvato iṇaṃ gahetvā paribhogo viyāti attho. Yasmā sekkhā bhagavato orasaputtā, tasmā te pitusantakānaṃ paccayānaṃ dāyādā hutvā te paccaye paribhuñjantīti tesaṃ paribhogo dāyajjaparibhogo nāma. Kiṃ pana te bhagavato paccaye paribhuñjanti, udāhu gihīhi dinnanti? Gihīhi dinnāpi te bhagavatā anuññātattā bhagavato santakā honti ananuññātesu sabbena sabbaṃ paribhogābhāvato anuññātesuyeva paribhogasambhavato. Dhammadāyādasuttañcettha (ma. ni. 1.29 ādayo) sādhakaṃ.

Use as a thief (theyyaparibhogo) is so called because there is no use as an owner. For the Blessed One has allowed requisites in his Dispensation to be used by the virtuous, not by the unvirtuous. The donors' gift is relinquished only to the virtuous, not to the unvirtuous, because they hope for great fruit from their actions. Thus, since it is not permitted by the Teacher and not relinquished by the donors, it is said: "The use by the unvirtuous is called use as a thief." Use by way of debt is debt-use (iṇaparibhogo). The meaning is that due to the absence of the purity of the offering on the part of the recipient, it is like using something after taking on a debt. Since the trainees are the Blessed One's own sons, they become heirs to the requisites belonging to the Father and use those requisites. Therefore, their use is called use as an heir (dāyajjaparibhogo). But do they use the requisites of the Blessed One, or those given by householders? Even though given by householders, they are the property of the Blessed One since they are permitted by him. For without permission, there is absolutely no use; use is possible only where it is permitted. And the Discourse on Heirs in the Dhamma (Majjhima Nikāya 1.29ff.) is evidence here.

Avītarāgānaṃ taṇhāparavasatāya paccayaparibhoge sāmibhāvo natthi, tadabhāvena vītarāgānaṃ tattha sāmibhāvo yathāruci paribhogasambhavato. Tathā hi te paṭikūlampi appaṭikūlākārena, appaṭikūlampi paṭikūlākārena tadubhayaṃ vivajjetvā upekkhākārena ca paccaye paribhuñjanti, dāyakānañca manorathaṃ paripūrenti. Sesamettha yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ visuddhimagge, taṃsaṃvaṇṇanāsu ca vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Kilesaiṇānaṃ abhāvaṃ sandhāya “aṇaṇo”ti vuttaṃ, na paccavekkhitaparibhogamattaṃ. Tenāha āyasmā ca bākulo – “sattāhameva kho ahaṃ, āvuso, saraṇo raṭṭhapiṇḍaṃ bhuñji”nti (ma. ni. 3.211).

For those who are not free from lust, there is no ownership in the use of requisites because they are dependent on craving. Due to the absence of that dependence, those who are free from lust have ownership therein, since use according to their wish is possible. Indeed, they use requisites by perceiving the repulsive as non-repulsive, the non-repulsive as repulsive, or, avoiding both, with equanimity, and they fulfill the wishes of the donors. Whatever else should be said here is to be understood in the way explained in the Visuddhimagga and its commentaries. "Debtless" is said with reference to the absence of the debt of defilements, not merely to use after reflection. Thus the Venerable Bākula said: "For only seven days, friend, did I eat the almsfood of the kingdom while in debt."

Vatthukāmakilesakāmehi taṇhāya pavattiākāraṃ paṭicca atthi ramaṇavohāroti āha – “duvidhesupi kāmesu taṇhāratisanthava”nti. Mantitanti kathitaṃ. Uppannehi satthupaṭiññehi. Saṃvibhattāti kusalādivasena khandhādīhi ākārehi vibhattā. Sundaraṃ āgamananti svāgataṃ. Tato eva na kucchitaṃ āgataṃ. Soḷasavidhakiccassa pariyositattā āha “taṃ sabbaṃ mayā kata”nti. Maggapaññāyameva tatiyavijjāsamaññāti āha – “tīhi vijjāhi navahi ca lokuttaradhammehī”ti.

Because of the manner of craving's occurrence dependent on sensual pleasures as objects and sensual pleasures as defilements, there is the designation 'delight'; thus he said: 'In both kinds of sensual pleasures, there is craving, delight, and intimacy.' 'Mantitanti' means spoken. 'Uppannehi' refers to those who have arisen with the claim of being a teacher. 'Saṃvibhattā' means distinguished by way of wholesome states and so on, and by the modes of the aggregates and so on. 'Sundaraṃ āgamananti' means welcome. Therefore, it is not a contemptible arrival. Because the sixteenfold duty has been completed, he said: 'All that has been done by me.' Because the wisdom of the path itself is designated as the third knowledge, he said: 'by the three knowledges and the nine supramundane states.'

Aṅgulimālasuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

The elucidation of the hidden meaning of the Commentary on the Aṅgulimāla Sutta is complete.

7. Piyajātikasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Piyajātika Sutta

353. Pakatiniyāmenāti [V 2.0159][M 2.0160] yathā sokuppattito pubbe iti kattabbesu asammohavasena cittaṃ pakkhandati, tāni cassa upaṭṭhahanti, na evaṃ sokassa cittasaṅkocasabhāvato. Tena vuttaṃ “pakatiniyāmena pana na paṭibhantī”ti. Keci pana “sāmantā katipaye na kuṭumbaṃ sandhāreti. Tenāha ‘na sabbena sabbaṃ paṭibhantī’ti” vadanti. Etthāti dutiyapade. Anekatthattā dhātūnaṃ “na paṭibhātī”ti padassa “na ruccatī”ti atthamāha. Na paṭibhātīti vā bhuñjitukāmatācittaṃ na upaṭṭhitanti attho. Patiṭṭhitokāsanti indriyāviṭṭhaṭṭhānaṃ vadati. Piyāyitabbato piyo jāti uppattiṭṭhānaṃ etesanti piyajātikā. Piyo pabhuti etesanti piyappabhutikāti vattabbe, u-kārassa va-kāraṃ, ta-kārassa ca lopaṃ katvā “piyappabhāvikā”ti vuttaṃ. Tenāha “piyato pabhavantī”ti.

353. 'By natural order' means: just as before the arising of sorrow the mind, through non-confusion, proceeds toward what should be done, and those things occur to it, so it is not with sorrow, due to its nature of contracting the mind. Therefore, it was said: 'But by natural order, they do not appear.' Some, however, say: 'In the neighborhood, some do not support the family. Therefore, he said: ‘They do not appear in every way.’' Here, in the second word, due to the multiple meanings of roots, for the word 'na paṭibhāti,' he gives the meaning 'is not pleasing.' Or, 'na paṭibhāti' means the mind with a desire to eat does not arise. 'Established place' refers to the location pervaded by the sense faculties. 'Piyajātikā' means those for whom what is dear is the place of birth, the place of origin, because it is to be cherished. When it should be said 'piyappabhutikā,' meaning 'those for whom the dear is the source,' it is said as 'piyappabhāvikā' by changing the 'u' to 'va' and eliding the 'ta.' Therefore, he said: 'they originate from the dear.'

355. Para-saddena samānatthaṃ ajjhattikabhāvanisedhanatthaṃ “pire”ti padanti āha “amhākaṃ pare”ti. Pireti vā “parato”ti iminā samānatthaṃ nipātapadanti āha “cara pireti parato gacchā”ti.

355. He said the word 'pire' means 'our enemies' (amhākaṃ pare), this being for the purpose of conveying a meaning similar to the word 'para' and negating the sense of 'internal'. Alternatively, he said 'pire' is a particle having the same meaning as 'parato' (away, from elsewhere), as in 'cara pire,' which means 'go away' (parato gacchā).

356. Dvidhā chetvāti ettha yadi itthī tassa purisassa piyā, kathaṃ dvidhā chindatīti āha “yadi hī”tiādi.

356. Regarding 'having cut in two': here, if a woman is dear to that man, how does one cut her in two? He says, 'If indeed,' and so on.

357. Kathaṃ katheyyanti yathā bhagavā etassa brāhmaṇassa kathesi, so ca me kathesi, tathā cāhaṃ katheyyaṃ. Maraṇavasena vipariṇāmo attabhāvassa parivattattā. Palāyitvā gamanavasena aññathābhāvo mittasanthavassa samāgamassa ca aññathābhūtattā.

357. 'How should I speak?' means: just as the Blessed One spoke to that brahmin, and as he spoke to me, so too should I speak. Alteration by way of death is due to the change of one's individual existence. Becoming otherwise by way of fleeing and going is due to friendship and association having become otherwise.

Chaḍḍitabhāvenāti parivattitabhāvena. Hatthagamanavasena aññathābhāvo pubbe savase vattitānaṃ idāni vase avattanabhāvena.

'By the state of being discarded' means by the state of being transformed. Becoming otherwise by way of passing into another's hands is due to what was formerly under one's own control now being in a state of not being under one's control.

Ācamehīti [V 2.0160] ācamanaṃ mukhavikkhālanaṃ kārehi. Yasmā mukhaṃ vikkhālentā hi hatthapāde dhovitvā vikkhālenti, tasmā “ācamitvā”ti vatvā pacchāpi tassa atthaṃ dassento “mukhaṃ vikkhāletvā”ti āha. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva.

'Ācamehi' means have mouth-rinsing done. Because when rinsing the mouth, they wash their hands and feet before rinsing, therefore, after saying 'having rinsed,' he clarifies the meaning further by saying, 'having rinsed the mouth.' The rest is easily understood.

Piyajātikasuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

The elucidation of the hidden meaning of the Commentary on the Piyajātika Sutta is complete.

8. Bāhitikasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Bāhitika Sutta

359. Sāvajjatāya [V 2.0161][M 2.0161] upārambhaṃ arahatīti opārambho. Tenāha “dosaṃ āropanāraho”ti. Bālā upārambhavatthumaññaṃ amūlakampi naṃ āropentā ugghosenti, tasmā te anāmasitvā “viññūhī”ti idaṃ padaṃ gahetvā pañhena ñātuṃ icchitena atthena upārambhādīnaṃ upari uttaraṃ paripūretuṃ nāsakkhimhā. Taṃ kāraṇanti taṃ uppattikāraṇaṃ. Yadi hi mayā “viññūhī”ti padaṃ pakkhipitvā vuttaṃ bhaveyya, pañhā me paripuṇṇā bhaveyya, na pana vuttā. Idāni pana taṃ kāraṇaṃ uttaraṃ āyasmatā ānandena “viññūhī”ti evaṃ vadantena paripūritaṃ.

359. 'Opārambho' is that which deserves reproach due to blameworthiness. Therefore, he said, 'worthy of having fault imputed.' Fools, imputing even a baseless matter as a ground for reproach, proclaim it. Therefore, without consulting them, and taking up the word 'by the wise,' we were unable to complete the answer concerning reproach and so on with the meaning we wished to know through the question. 'That reason' means that cause of its arising. For if the word 'by the wise' had been included and spoken by me, my question would have been complete, but it was not so stated. Now, however, that reason has been completed by the Venerable Ānanda, who supplied the answer by saying 'by the wise.'

360. Kosallapaṭipakkhato akosallaṃ vuccati avijjā, taṃsamuṭṭhānato akosallasambhūto. Avajjaṃ vuccati garahitabbaṃ, saha avajjehīti sāvajjo, gārayho. Rāgādidosehi sadoso. Tehi eva sabyābajjho, tato eva sampati āyatiñca sadukkho. Sabyābajjhādiko nissandavipāko.

360. Unskillfulness (akosallaṃ) is called ignorance because it is the opposite of skillfulness; 'born of unskillfulness' (akosallasambhūto) is so called because it arises from that. 'Blameworthy' (avajjaṃ) is said to be that which should be censured; 'with blame' (sāvajjo) means with blameworthy things, reprehensible. 'With faults' (sadoso) means with faults such as lust. Because of these, it is harmful (sabyābajjho), and from that, it is painful (sadukkho) both in the present and in the future. The flowing-out result begins with harmfulness.

Tathā attho vutto bhaveyyāti pucchāsabhāgenapi attho vutto bhaveyya, pucchantassa pana na tāva cittārādhanaṃ. Tenāha – “evaṃ byākaraṇaṃ pana na bhāriya”nti, garukaraṇaṃ na hoti visārajjaṃ na siyāti adhippāyo. Tenāha – “appahīnaakusalopi hi pahānaṃ vaṇṇeyyā”ti. Evarūpo pana yathākārī tathāvādī na hoti, na evaṃ bhagavāti āha “bhagavā”tiādi. Evaṃ byākāsīti “sabbākusaladhammapahīno kho, mahārāja, tathāgato”ti evaṃ byākāsi. Sukkapakkhepi eseva nayoti iminā “sabbesaṃyeva kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upasampadaṃ vaṇṇetī”ti vutte yathā pucchā, tathā attho vutto bhaveyya, evaṃ byākaraṇaṃ pana na bhāriyaṃ, asampāditakusaladhammopi upasampadaṃ vaṇṇeyya. Bhagavā pana sammadeva sampāditakusalattā yathākārī tathāvādīti dassetuṃ “evaṃ byākāsī”ti imamatthaṃ dasseti. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva.

The meaning should be stated thus: even if the meaning were stated in accordance with the question, the questioner's mind would not yet be satisfied. Therefore, he said: 'But such an explanation is not weighty,' the intention being that it is not impressive and would not inspire confidence. Therefore, he said: 'For even one who has not abandoned unwholesome states might praise their abandonment.' Such a person, however, is not one who acts as he speaks; the Blessed One is not so, thus it is said, 'the Blessed One,' and so on. 'He answered thus' means he answered in this way: 'The Tathāgata, O great king, has indeed abandoned all unwholesome states.' This is the same method for the bright side as well.
