'Departed ancestors' are former relatives who have passed on to the realm of the departed. The duty to departed ancestors is to give offerings at the proper times to those worthy of gifts and to dedicate the merit to them—this is the meaning of 'ancestral offering.' The duty to the deities is the worship of deities at the proper times with perfumes, flowers, ointments, incense, and food—this is the meaning of 'deity offering.' The performance of royal duties and service is the duty to the king. 'This body too'—this is said with reference to one's own body. With this meaning in mind, it is said, 'The meaning should be understood in this manner.'

447. Pañca dussīlyakammānīti niccasīlapaṭipakkhadhammā. Dasa akusalakammapathadhammā dasa dussīlyakammāni. Adhammacārī eva visamacārī kāyavisamādicaraṇatoti visamacārīpadassa attho visuṃ na vutto.

447. The five immoral actions—these are qualities opposed to constant virtue. The ten unwholesome courses of action are the ten immoral actions. 'One who behaves unlawfully' is the same as 'one who behaves unevenly'; because of uneven bodily conduct and the like, the meaning of the term 'uneven conduct' is not stated separately.

448-453. Osaranti [V 2.0198] apasakkanti, khīyantīti attho. Tenāha “parihāyantī”ti. Abhisarantīti abhivaḍḍhanavasena pavattanti. Tenāha “vaḍḍhantī”ti. Tatrāti brahmaloke. Assāti brahmaloke uppannassa dhanañjānissa. Tato paṭṭhāyāti yadā bhagavatā “eso, bhikkhave, sāriputto”tiādi vuttaṃ, tato paṭṭhāya. Catusaccavinimuttanti niddhāretvā vibhajitvā vuccamānehi saccehi vimuttaṃ. Atthato pana tato pubbepi saccavimuttaṃ kathaṃ na kathesiyeva saccavimuttassa niyyānassa abhāvato.

448-453. 'They recede' (osaranti) means they draw back (apasakkanti); that is, they decrease. Therefore, it is said, 'they decline' (parihāyanti). 'They advance' (abhisaranti) means they proceed by way of growth. Therefore, it is said, 'they increase' (vaḍḍhanti). 'There' (tatra) means in the Brahma-world. 'Of him' (assa) means of Dhanañjāni, who was born in the Brahma-world. 'From then on' (tato paṭṭhāya) means from the time when the Blessed One said, 'This, monks, is Sāriputta,' and so on. 'Liberated from the four truths' (catusaccavinimuttaṃ) means liberated from the truths that are spoken of after having been ascertained and analyzed. But in meaning, even before that, how could he have spoken of something as liberated from the truths, since there is no escape that is itself liberated from the truths?

Dhanañjānisuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

The Elucidation of the Hidden Meaning in the Commentary on the Dhanañjāni Sutta is complete.

8. Vāseṭṭhasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Vāseṭṭha Sutta

454. Jātiṃ [V 2.0199][M 2.0198] sodhetukāmā hontīti sahavāsīnaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ kiriyā parādhena vā asāruppattena vā jātiyā upakkilesaṃ āsaṅkāya taṃ sodhetukāmā honti. Mante sodhetukāmā hontīti mantavacane ācariyamaticodanāya aññena vākyena kenaci kāraṇena saṃsaye uppanne taṃ sodhetukāmā honti. Antarāti vemajjhe, aññatthevā antarāsaddoti tassa aññā kathāti vacanaṃ avagantabbaṃ. Khantīmettānuddayādiguṇasampanno eva “sīlavāti guṇavā”tiāha. Tehi sīlassa vissajjanakālepi “sīlavā”ti vuccati. Sampannasīlattā vā tehi samannāgato eva hotīti āha “sīlavāti guṇavā”ti. Ācārasampannoti sādhu ācāravatto.

454. 'They wish to purify their birth' means they wish to purify their caste, suspecting a defilement of their caste due to the actions, offense, or unsuitability of their fellow Brahmins. 'They wish to purify the hymns' means they wish to purify the Vedic hymns when doubt arises in their recitation due to a challenge from the teacher's opinion or for some other reason. 'Antarā' means 'in the middle'; the saying, 'The word `antarā` is indeed in another sense,' should be understood as 'it is another matter.' One endowed with qualities such as patience, loving-kindness, and compassion is called 'virtuous and possessed of good qualities.' Even at a time of abandoning virtue, he is called 'virtuous' by them. Or, because he is possessed of accomplished virtue, he is indeed endowed with them; therefore it is said, 'virtuous and possessed of good qualities.' 'Accomplished in conduct' means one of good conduct.

455. Sikkhitāti tevijjānaṃ sikkhitā tumhe, na dāni tumhehi kiñci kattabbaṃ atthīti attho. Paṭiññātāti paṭijānitvā ṭhitā.

455. 'Sikkhitā' means you are learned in the three knowledges; the meaning is that there is now nothing more for you to do. 'Paṭiññātā' means having professed, they stand firm.

Vedattayasaṅkhātā tisso vijjā ajjhayantīti tevijjā. Tenāha “tivedāna”nti. Tayo vede aṇanti ajjhayantīti brāhmaṇā, tesaṃ. Yaṃ ekaṃ padampi akkhātaṃ, taṃ atthato byañjanato ca kevalino adhiyino appapayogena. Niṭṭhāgatamhāti nipphattiṃ gatā amhā tevijjāya sakasamayassa kathane.

Because they study the three knowledges, known as the triad of Vedas, they are called 'tevijjā' (possessors of the three knowledges). Therefore, it is said, 'of the possessors of the three Vedas' (tivedānaṃ). Brahmins are those who study, that is, learn, the three Vedas. Whatever single word is uttered, they, being accomplished and well-versed, understand it fully in meaning and letter with little effort. 'We have reached the culmination' (niṭṭhāgatamhā) means we have attained consummation in the exposition of our own doctrine concerning the three knowledges.

Manokammato hi vattasampadātikāraṇūpacārenāyamattho vuttoti āha – “tena samannāgato hi ācārasampanno hotī”ti.

For this meaning is stated figuratively, by treating mental action as the primary cause of the accomplishment of conduct; hence it is said, 'For, being endowed with that, one is accomplished in conduct.'

Khayātītanti vaḍḍhipakkhe ṭhitanti attho. Sukkapakkhapāṭipadato paṭṭhāya hi cando vaḍḍhatīti vuccati, na khīyatīti. Vandamānā janā namakkāraṃ karonti.

'Khayātītaṃ' means standing in the waxing phase. For the moon is said to increase from the first day of the bright fortnight onward, not to wane. People, venerating, pay homage.

Atthadassanenāti vivaraṇena dassanapariṇāyakaṭṭhena lokassa cakkhu hutvā samuppannaṃ.

'Atthadassanena' means by explanation, with the characteristic of being a guide to vision, having arisen as the eye of the world.

456. Tiṭṭhatu tāva brāhmaṇacintāti – “kiṃ jātiyā brāhmaṇo hoti udāhu bhavati kammunā”ti ayaṃ brāhmaṇavicāro tāva tiṭṭhatu[M 2.0199]. Jātidassanatthaṃ tiṇarukkhakīṭapaṭaṅgato paṭṭhāya loke [V 2.0200] jātivibhaṅgaṃ vitthārato kathessāmīti tesaṃ cittasampahaṃsanatthaṃ desetabbamatthaṃ paṭijānāti. Tattha aññamaññā hi jātiyoti idaṃ kāraṇavacanaṃ, yasmā imā jātiyo nāma aññamaññaṃ visiṭṭhā, tasmā jātivibhaṅgaṃ byākarissāmīti.

456. Let the Brahmin's thought wait for now—'Is one a Brahmin by birth or does one become so by action?'—this inquiry about Brahmins can wait. To demonstrate the nature of birth, starting from grass, trees, insects, and moths, I will explain in detail the classification of births in the world—thus he promises the matter to be taught for the purpose of delighting their minds. Herein, 'for these births are distinct from one another' is a statement of reason: because these so-called births are distinct from one another, therefore I will explain the classification of births.

Yasmā idha upādinnakajāti byākātabbabhāvena āgatā, tassā pana nidassanabhāvena itarā, tasmā “jātivibhaṅgaṃ pāṇāna”nti pāḷiyaṃ vuttaṃ. Tesaṃ tesaṃ pāṇānaṃ jātiyoti attho. Evanti nidassanaṃ kathetvā nidassitabbe kathiyamāne. Tassāti vāseṭṭhassa. Kāmaṃ “tesaṃ vohaṃ byakkhissa”nti ubhopi māṇave nissāya desanā āgatā, tathāpi tattha tattha “evaṃ, vāseṭṭha, jānāhī”tiādinā vāseṭṭhameva ālapanto bhagavā tameva iminā niyāmena pamukhaṃ akāsi. Tena vuttaṃ “tassāti vāseṭṭhassā”ti. Jātibhedo jātiviseso, jātiyā bhedo pākaṭo bhavissati nidassanena vibhūtabhāvaṃ āpāditena paṭiññātassa atthassa vibhūtabhāvāpattito. Āma na vaṭṭatīti kammanānatāya eva upādinnanānatāya paṭikkhepapadametaṃ, na bījanānatāya anupādinnanānatāya paṭikkhepapadanti dassetuṃ “kammaṃ hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tassattho – taṃtaṃyonikhipanamattaṃ kammassa sāmatthiyaṃ, taṃtaṃyoniniyatā pana ye vaṇṇavisesā, te taṃtaṃyonisiddhiyāva siddhā hontīti taṃ pana yonikhipanakammaṃ taṃtaṃyonivisiṭṭha-visesābhibhūtāya payoganipphattiyā, asaṃmucchitāya eva vā paccayabhūtāya bhavapatthanāya abhisaṅkhatamevāti viññātabbapaccayavisesena vinā phalavisesābhāvato etaṃ samīhitakammaṃ patthanādīhi ca bhinnasattitaṃ visiṭṭhasāmatthiyaṃ vā āpajjitvā cakkhundriyādivisiṭṭhaphalanibbattakaṃ jāyati, evaṃ yonikhipanataṃyoniniyatavisesāvahatā hotīti. Therena hi bījanānatā viya kammanānatāpi upādinnakanānatāya siyā nu kho paccayoti codanaṃ paṭikkhipitvā paccayavisesavisiṭṭhā kammanānatā pana paccayoti nicchitanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Because here birth based on clinging is to be explained, while the other is by way of illustration, therefore it is said in the text, 'the classification of births among beings.' The meaning is the birth of each and every one of those beings. Thus, having stated the illustration, what is to be illustrated is being discussed. 'His' refers to Vāseṭṭha. Although the teaching is given with reference to both young men, as in 'I will explain to you both,' yet here and there the Blessed One addresses Vāseṭṭha alone, saying, 'Thus, Vāseṭṭha, you should know,' etc., making him foremost in this manner. Therefore, it is said, '“his” refers to Vāseṭṭha.' The distinction of birth, the variety of birth, the division of birth will become evident; by the illustration, the meaning of the promised statement will become clear by means of its manifestation. 'No, it is not right'—this is a term of refutation regarding the diversity of what is acquired through the diversity of kamma. It is not a term of refutation regarding the diversity of what is not acquired through the diversity of seed. To show this, 'kamma is...' and so on is said. The meaning is this: the mere casting into a particular womb is the capacity of kamma. However, those particular characteristics determined by a particular womb are established by the success of that womb itself. But that kamma of casting into a womb is conditioned by the aspiration for existence, which becomes a condition that is either unconfused or is the result of an application overcome by the specific distinction of that particular womb. Thus, because without a specific determining condition there is no specific result, it should be understood that this intended kamma, having attained a distinct power or a special capacity through aspiration and so on, arises as a producer of distinctive results like the eye faculty, etc. In this way, the act of casting into a womb brings about the distinctions determined by that womb. For the Elder, the objection, 'Could it be that the diversity of kamma, like the diversity of seed, is a condition for the diversity of what is acquired?' is rejected, and it should be seen as certain that the diversity of kamma, distinguished by specific conditions, is indeed the condition.

Nānāvaṇṇāti nānappakāravaṇṇā. Tālanāḷikerādīnaṃ loke abhiññātatiṇajātibhāvato visesena gayhati abhiññātasotanayena. Jātiyā brāhmaṇovāti aṭṭhānapayutto eva-saddo, jātiyāva [M 2.0200] brāhmaṇo bhaveyyāti yojanā. Na ca gayhatīti tiṇarukkhādīsu viya brāhmaṇesu jātiniyatassa liṅgassa anupalabbhanato, pivanabhuñjanakathanahasanādikiriyāya brāhmaṇabhāvena ekantikaliṅganiyatāya mantajjhenādiṃ vinā anupalabbhanato ca. Vacībhedenevāti āhaccavacaneneva.

"Of various colors" means of various kinds of colors. Things like palms and coconuts are grasped with distinction by way of what is well-known, because they are well-known types of grass in the world. Regarding "By birth, a brahmin," the word 'eva' is used in an inappropriate context; the construction should be: "Only by birth could one be a brahmin." And "it is not grasped" because among brahmins, unlike among grasses, trees, and so on, a sign determined by birth is not found; and because, apart from chanting mantras and meditation, an action such as drinking, eating, speaking, or laughing, which is determined as a conclusive sign of being a brahmin, is not found. "By a difference in speech alone" means by a mere assertion.

Kīṭe paṭaṅgetiādīsu jātinānatā labbhati aññamaññaliṅgavisiṭṭhatādassanā. Kunthā kīṭakā[V 2.0201], khajjakhādakā kipillikā. Uppatitvāti uḍḍetvā uḍḍetvā. Paṭabhāvaṃ gacchantīti vā paṭaṅgā, na khuddakapāṇakā kīṭā nāma. Tesampi kīṭakānaṃ.

Among insects, grasshoppers, and so on, diversity of birth is found, because they are seen to be distinguished by mutual signs. `Kunthā` are small insects; `khajjakhādakā` are ants. `Uppatitvā` means having flown up repeatedly. Alternatively, they are `paṭaṅgā` because they attain a winged state; they are not the tiny creatures called `kīṭā`. This applies even to those small insects.

Kāḷakādayoti kalandakādayo.

The Kāḷaka and so on means the Kalandaka and so on.

Udaraṃyeva nesaṃ pādā udareneva sampajjanato.

Their feet are their very belly, because they move by means of the belly.

Saññāpubbako vidhi aniccoti dassento “udake”ti āha yathā “vīrassa bhāvo vīriya”nti.

Showing that a rule based on convention is not absolute, he said, 'in water,' just as 'the state of a hero is heroism.'

Pattasamudāye pakkhasaddoti “pattehi yantī”ti vuttaṃ. Na hi avayavabyatirekena samudāyo atthi.

The word 'wing' refers to an aggregate of feathers; thus it is said, 'they go by means of feathers.' For an aggregate does not exist apart from its constituent parts.

Saṅkhepena vutto “jātivasena nānā”tiādinā. Ettha padatthe dubbiññeyyaṃ natthīti sambandhamattaṃ dassetuṃ “tatrāyaṃ yojanā”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Na hi brāhmaṇānaṃ edisaṃ sīsaṃ hoti, khattiyānaṃ edisanti niyamo atthi yathā hatthiassamigādīna”nti idameva vākyaṃ sabbattha netabbaṃ. Taṃ saṃṅkhipitvā dassento “iminā nayena sabbaṃ yojetabba”nti āha.

In brief, it is stated as 'diverse due to birth,' and so forth. Here, there is no difficulty in understanding the meaning of the words; it is merely to show the connection, hence it is said, 'here is the application,' and so forth. 'There is no fixed rule that Brahmins have heads of this kind, or Khattiyas heads of that kind, as with elephants, horses, deer, and so forth.' This very statement should be applied everywhere. Summarizing this, he says, 'In this way, everything should be connected.'

Tassāti yathāvuttanigamanavacanassa ayaṃ yojanā idāni vuccamānā yojanā veditabbā.

Of that previously stated concluding statement, this is the explanation; the interpretation now being given should be understood.

457. Vokāranti vokaraṇaṃ, yena visiṭṭhatāya na vokarīyati jātibhedoti attho. Tenāha “nānatta”nti.

457. `Vokāra` means distinguishing. The meaning is that by which a difference of birth is not specifically distinguished. Therefore, he said, 'diversity.'

Gorakkhādiupajīvanena ājīvavipanno, hiṃsādinā sīlavipanno, nikkhittavattatādinā ācāravipannoti. Sāmaññajotanā visese niviṭṭhā hotīti āha “gorakkhanti khettarakkha”nti. “Goti hi pathaviyā nāma”nti. Tehi tehi upāyehi sikkhitabbaṭṭhena sippaṃ, tattha kosallaṃ. Paresaṃ [M 2.0201] īsanaṭṭhena hiṃsanaṭṭhena isso, so assa atthīti isso yodhājīviko, issassa kammaṃ paharaṇaṃ, usuṃ sattiñca nissāya pavattā jīvikā issattaṃ. Tenāha “āvudhajīvika”nti. Yaṃ nissāya assa jīvikā, tadeva dassetuṃ “usuñca sattiñcā”ti vuttaṃ.

By making a living through cattle-tending and so forth, one is deficient in livelihood; by harming and so forth, one is deficient in virtue; by abandoning prescribed duties and so forth, one is deficient in conduct. The explanation of the general term is established in the specific instance; hence it is said: '`Gorakkha` means guarding fields.' For '`go`' is a name for the earth. A craft is so-called because it is to be trained in by various means; proficiency is skill in that. An `issa` (master) is so-called in the sense of ruling or harming others; one who has this is an `issa`, one who lives as a warrior. The work of an `issa` is striking; the livelihood that proceeds depending on the arrow and the spear is `issatta` (mastery). Therefore, it is said: 'one who lives by weapons.' To show that on which his livelihood depends, it is said: 'the arrow and the spear.'

Brahmaṃ [V 2.0202] vuccati vedo, taṃ aṇati jānātīti brāhmaṇo, jānanañca porāṇehi brāhmaṇehi vihitaniyāmena brāhmaṇehi katopasamena anuṭṭhānatapena yathā “ājīvasīlācāravipanno natthī”ti brāhmaṇadhammikehi lokiyapaṇḍitehi ca sampaṭicchito, tathā paṭipajjanamevāti āha “evaṃ brāhmaṇasamayena…pe… sādhetvā”ti. Evaṃ santeti evaṃ ājīvasīlācāravipannassa abrāhmaṇabhāve sati na jātiyā brāhmaṇo hoti, guṇehi pana ājīvasīlācārasampattisaṅkhātehi brāhmaṇo hoti, tasmā guṇānaṃyeva brāhmaṇabhāvakaraṇato catuvaṇṇavibhāge yattha katthaci kule jāto yo sīlādiguṇasampannatāya guṇavā, so vuttalakkhaṇena nippariyāyato bāhitapāpatāya brāhmaṇoti ayamettha brāhmaṇabhāve ñāyoti, evaṃ ñāyaṃ atthato āpannaṃ katvā. Nanti tameva yathāvuttaṃ ñāyaṃ. Yo brāhmaṇassa saṃvaṇṇitāyāti mātuyā ubhatosujātatādikulavaṇṇena saṃvaṇṇitāya pasatthāya yathārūpāya brāhmaṇassa mātā bhavituṃ yuttā, tathārūpāya mātarisambhūto. Etena catunnaṃ yonīnaṃ yattha katthaci visesaniṭṭhā katā. Tenāha “tatrāpi visesenā”ti. Evaṃ sāmaññato visesaniṭṭhāvasena “yonijaṃ mattisambhava”nti padassa atthaṃ vatvā idāni sāmaññajotanaṃ anādiyitvā visesajotanāvaseneva atthaṃ vattuṃ “yācāya”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Parisuddhauppattimaggasaṅkhātā yoni vuttāti anupakkuṭṭhabhāvena parisuddhauppattimaggasaṅkhātā yā cāyaṃ yoni vuttāti sambandho. Tatopi jātasambhūtattāti tato yonito jātattā mātāpettisampattito sambhūtattā.

`Brahma` is said to be the Veda; one who studies or knows it is a `brāhmaṇa`. And the knowing, and the very practice according to the rule established by the ancient brahmins—with the calm effected by brahmins and with non-arising asceticism—is accepted by brahmins who are followers of the Dhamma and by worldly wise people, such that one is not deficient in livelihood, virtue, and conduct. Thus he says, 'in this way, by the brahmin convention... having accomplished...' This being so, since one who is deficient in livelihood, virtue, and conduct is in a state of not being a brahmin, one is not a brahmin by birth. Rather, one is a brahmin through qualities, that is, the accomplishment of livelihood, virtue, and conduct. Therefore, since it is qualities alone that make one a brahmin, whoever, born in any family whatsoever within the division of the four castes, is virtuous through the accomplishment of qualities like virtue, is a brahmin in the definitive sense due to having banished evil according to the stated characteristic. This is the principle here regarding being a brahmin. Having thus arrived at this principle in terms of meaning... `Naṃ` refers to that very principle as stated. 'Of one praised as a brahmin' means born of a mother who is praised and commended for her pure birth on both sides and her lineage, a mother of such a kind as is fit to be the mother of a brahmin. By this, a specific conclusion is made regarding any of the four kinds of birth. Therefore he says, 'therein also specifically.' Having thus explained the meaning of the phrase 'womb-born, mother-produced' by way of a general statement and a specific conclusion, now, disregarding the general explanation, in order to state the meaning only by way of the specific explanation, he says 'because of...' and so on. 'The womb, described as the path of pure origin, is stated'—the connection is: 'this womb which is described as the path of pure origin, being uncorrupted.' 'Because of being born and produced from that' means because of being born from that womb and produced from the excellence of mother and father.

Visiṭṭhattāti samudāyabhūtā manussā rāgādinā visiṭṭhattā. Rāgādinā saha kiñcanenāti sakiñcano. Tatheva rāgādisaṅkhātena palibodhanaṭṭhena saha palibodhenāti sapalibodho. Sabbagahaṇapaṭinissaggenāti upādānasaṅkhātassa sabbassa gahaṇassa paṭinissajjanena. Yasmā bāhitapāpo attano santānato bahikatapāpo, tasmā tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇanti [M 2.0202] attho vattabbo. Evarūpo etissā kathāya upadeso nānappakārato vibhatto, tasmā tattha tattha vuttanayeneva veditabbo.

`Visiṭṭhattā` means because humans, who exist as an aggregate, are distinguished by lust and so forth. `Sakiñcano` means with an impediment, that is, with an impediment along with lust and so forth. Similarly, `sapalibodho` means with an obstruction, that is, with an obstruction in the sense of being an obstacle, which is reckoned as lust and so forth. `Sabbagahaṇapaṭinissaggena` means by the relinquishing of all grasping, that is, by the relinquishing of all grasping which is reckoned as clinging. Because `bāhitapāpo` means one who has banished evil from his own mental continuum, therefore, 'him I call a brahmin'—this is the meaning to be supplied. Such is the instruction of this discourse, analyzed in various ways. Therefore, it should be understood according to the method stated in each respective case.

458. Gahitadaṇḍesūti paresaṃ daṇḍena viheṭhanaṃ anidhāya ādinnadaṇḍesu.

458. `Gahitadaṇḍesu` means among those who have taken up the rod, not inflicting violence on others with the rod.

459. Kiñci gahaṇanti taṇhāgāhādīsu kiñci gāhaṃ.

459. `Kiñci gahaṇaṃ` refers to any kind of grasping, such as the grasping of craving and so forth.

Yena kāmabhavena mānusakehi pañcahi kāmaguṇehi yuñjati, taṃ mānusakaṃ yogaṃ. “Mānusakaṃ [V 2.0203] yoga”nti ettha ca ekadesaṃ gahetvā vuttaṃ, esa nayo “dibbayoga”nti etthāpi. Sabbayogavisaṃyuttanti padadvayena vuttehi sabbakilesayogehi vippayuttaṃ.

That sensual nature by which one is yoked to the five human strands of sensual pleasure is the 'human yoke.' And here in 'human yoke,' it is spoken of by taking a part for the whole; this same method applies also in 'divine yoke.' 'Disjoined from all yokes' means disjoined from all the yokes of the defilements spoken of by these two terms.

Ratinti abhiratiṃ āsattiṃ. Kusalabhāvanāyāti kāyabhāvanādi kusaladhammabhāvanāya ukkaṇṭhitaṃ. Vīriyavantanti vīriyasabbhāvena vīraṃ niddisati, vīrabhāvo hi vīriyanti.

`Rati` means delight, attachment. 'With the cultivation of the wholesome' means discontented with the cultivation of wholesome states such as the development of the body and so on. `Vīriyavantaṃ` (energetic) indicates a hero by the very nature of energy; for heroism is energy.

Sundaraṃ ṭhānanti nibbānaṃ. Sundarāya paṭipattiyā ariyapaṭipattiyā.

`Sundaraṃ ṭhānaṃ` means Nibbāna. By the beautiful practice means by the noble practice.

Nibbattinti pariyosānaṃ. Atīteti atītakoṭṭhāse. Kiñcanakārakoti palibodhahetubhūto.

`Nibbattim` means the culmination. `Atīte` means in the past division. `Kiñcanakārako` means a cause of obstruction.

Asekkhe sīlakkhandhādike mahante guṇe. Pañcannaṃ mārānaṃ vijitattā vijitavijayaṃ.

In the great qualities of the adept, such as the aggregate of virtue. `Vijitavijayaṃ` means one who has won the victory, because the five Māras have been conquered.

460. Idaṃ ajānantāti “jātiyā brāhmaṇo”ti idaṃ lokasamaññāmattanti ajānantā. Ye brāhmaṇesu nāmagottaṃ nāma tatiyaṃ diṭṭhābhinivesaṃ janenti, sāva nesaṃ diṭṭhi. Kataṃ abhisaṅkhatanti parikappanavaseneva kataṃ ṭhapitaṃ tadupacitaṃ, na hetupaccayasamāyogena. Samuccāti sammutiyā. Kā pana sā sammutīti āha “samaññāyā”ti, lokasamaññātenāti attho. Sammā pana paramatthato ajānantānaṃ nāmagottaṃ evaṃ kappetīti āha “no ce”tiādi. Taṃ pana asantampi paramatthato santatāyeva abhinivisanti, tesamayaṃ dosoti dassetuṃ “evaṃ pakappita”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Tenāha bhagavā – “janapadaniruttiṃ nābhiniveseyyā”ti [M 2.0203] (ma. ni. 3.331). Ajānantā noti ettha no-saddo avadhāraṇattho – “na no samaṃ atthi tathāgatenā”tiādīsu (khu. pā. 6.3) viyāti āha “ajānantāva evaṃ vadantī”ti.

460. 'Idaṃ ajānanta' means not knowing that 'a brahmin by birth' is merely a worldly convention. Those who, regarding brahmins, generate an adherence to a third view based on name and clan—that is their view. 'Kataṃ abhisaṅkhataṃ' means what is made and established merely by way of conceptualization, accumulated through that, not by the combination of causes and conditions. 'Samuccā' means by convention. What, then, is that convention? He says, 'by designation'—meaning by worldly designation. But for those who do not rightly know in the ultimate sense, name and clan are conceived thus, as he says: 'if not,' and so forth. Though it is non-existent in the ultimate sense, they adhere to it as if it were existent; to show this fault of theirs, it is said: 'thus conceived,' and so forth. Therefore, the Blessed One said: 'One should not be attached to regional dialects' (MN 3.331). In 'ajānantā no', the word 'no' has the meaning of emphasis—as in 'there is none equal to the Tathāgata,' and so forth (Khp. 6.3)—thus he says: 'it is precisely those not knowing who speak thus.'

Nippariyāyanti bhāvanapuṃsakaniddeso, nippariyāyena ujukamevāti attho, na pubbe viya “yo hi kocī”ti pariyāyavasena. “Na jaccā”ti gāthāya pubbaddhena jātivādaṃ paṭikkhipanto pacchimaddhena kammavādaṃ patiṭṭhapento. Tatthāti tissaṃ gāthāyaṃ. Upaḍḍhagāthāya vitthāraṇatthanti upaḍḍhagāthāya atthaṃ vitthāretuṃ “kassako kammunā”ti vuttaṃ. Tattha purimāya catūhi pādehi, pacchime dvīhi dvinnampi sādhāraṇato attho vitthārito. Tattha kasikammādīti ādi-saddena sippakammavāṇijādi saṅgaho.

'Nippariyāyaṃ' is a designation in the neuter gender, meaning directly and straightforwardly, not as before by way of circumlocution with 'whoever.' With 'Na jaccā'—in the first half of the verse, he rejects the doctrine of birth, while in the latter half, he establishes the doctrine of kamma. 'Tattha' means in this verse. 'To elaborate on the half-verse' means that to elaborate on the meaning of the half-verse, it is said: 'a farmer by kamma,' and so forth. There, by the first four lines and by the latter two, the meaning common to both is elaborated. There, in 'farming, and so forth'—by the word 'and so forth,' crafts, trade, and so forth are included.

Paṭiccasamuppādapadhānavacanaviññeyyo [V 2.0204] paccayo paṭiccasamuppādasaddassa attho paccayuppannāpekkhāya hotīti āha – “iminā paccayena etaṃ hotī”ti. Yaṃ panettha vattabbaṃ, taṃ visuddhimagge (visuddhi. 2.570) taṃsaṃvaṇṇanāyañca (visuddhi. mahāṭī. 2.570) vuttanayena veditabbaṃ. Sammānāvamānārahakuleti sammānārahe khattiyādikule, avamānārahe caṇḍālādikule kammavasena upapatti hoti kammassa vipaccamānokāsakaratāya vinā tādisāya uccanīcakulanibbattiyā abhāvato. Aḍḍhadaliddatādi aññāpi hīnapaṇītatā.

The meaning of the word 'paṭiccasamuppāda' is 'condition,' which is to be understood from the primary statement of dependent origination; it is relative to what has arisen from a condition, thus he says: 'With this as a condition, that comes to be.' Whatever should be stated here, that should be understood according to the method stated in the Visuddhimagga (Vism. 2.570) and its commentary (Vism-mhṭ. 2.570). 'In families worthy of honor and dishonor' means an arising occurs in families worthy of honor, such as the Khattiya class, and in families worthy of dishonor, such as the Caṇḍāla class, due to kamma creating the opportunity for ripening, because without such a birth in a high or low family, it would not occur. 'Wealth, poverty, and so forth' refers to other inferior and superior states.

Kammunāti cettha yathā lokapajāsattasaddehi eko evattho vutto, evaṃ sesasaddehipi, adhippāyaviseso pana tattha atthīti dassetuṃ “purimapadena cetthā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Nāyaṃ loko brahmanimmito kammena uppajjanato. Na hi sannihitakāraṇānaṃ phalānaṃ aññena uppattidiṭṭhi yujjati. Tenāha “diṭṭhiyā paṭisedho veditabbo”ti. Yaṃ panettha vattabbaṃ taṃ visuddhimaggasaṃvaṇṇanādīsuvuttanayena veditabbaṃ. Tathā lokassa paṭhamuppatti na brahmunāti “kammunā hi tāsu tāsū”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tatiyena “ayaṃ loko ādito pabhuti pabhavakammunā vattatī”ti vuttamatthaṃ nigameti.Vuttassevatthassa sūcanañhi nigamanaṃ. Taṃ pana niyamatthaṃ hotīti āha “kammeneva baddhā hutvā pavattanti, na aññathā”ti[M 2.0204]. Catutthena padena. Yāyatoti gacchato. Nibbattatoti nibbattantassa. Pavattatoti pavattantassa.

Here, in 'by kamma,' just as a single meaning is expressed by the words 'world,' 'people,' and 'beings,' so too with the remaining words. However, to show that there is a particular intention, it is said, 'By the first term here,' and so forth. This world is not created by Brahmā, because it arises from kamma. For the view that effects of present causes arise from something else is not tenable. Therefore he says, 'This should be understood as a rejection of that view.' Whatever should be stated here is to be understood in the way it is stated in the commentary on the Visuddhimagga and so on. Similarly, that the initial arising of the world is not from Brahmā is stated with 'For by kamma in this and that,' and so forth. By the third statement, he concludes the meaning stated as: 'This world, from the beginning onward, proceeds due to kamma as its origin.' For a conclusion is indeed an indication of the meaning already stated. And it serves the purpose of determination, as he says: 'Bound by kamma alone do they proceed, not otherwise.' By the fourth term: 'Yāyato' means 'of one who goes.' 'Nibbattato' means 'of one who is produced.' 'Pavattato' means 'of one who continues.'

Dhutadhammā visesato taṇhāya santattavasena vattantīti āha “tapenāti dhutaṅgatapenā”ti. Methunavirati visesato brāhmaṇānaṃ brahmacariyanti sā idha brahmacariyenāti adhippetāti āha “brahmacariyenāti methunaviratiyā”ti. Etenāti iminā “tapenā”tiādīhi catūhi padehi vuttena. Seṭṭhenāti uttamena. Saṃkilesavisuddhiyā parisuddhena. Brahmanti brahmabhāvaṃ seṭṭhabhāvaṃ. So panettha atthato brāhmaṇabhāvoti āha “brāhmaṇabhāvaṃ āvahatī”ti.

Because the ascetic practices proceed especially by way of scorching craving, he says, 'by austerity, meaning by the austerity of the dhutaṅgas.' Abstinence from sexual intercourse is especially the brahmacariya of brahmins; that is intended here by the term 'brahmacariya,' hence it is said, 'by brahmacariya, meaning by abstinence from sexual intercourse.' 'By this' means by what is said by these four terms beginning with 'by austerity.' 'By the best' means by the highest. 'By purification from defilements' means by what is thoroughly pure. 'Brahma' means the state of Brahma, the highest state. Here, that means in substance the state of a brahmin, hence it is said, 'it brings about the state of a brahmin.'

Brahmā ca sakko cāti sakkagarukānaṃ sakko sakkenapi garukātabbato, brahmagarukānaṃ brahmā brahmunāpi garukātabbato. Vijānatanti paramatthabrāhmaṇassa visesaṃ jānantānaṃ viññūnaṃ. Aviññuno hi appamāṇaṃ. Tenāha – “paṇḍitāna”nti. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva.

'Brahmā and Sakka' are mentioned because for those who revere Sakka, the true brahmin is to be revered even by Sakka, and for those who revere Brahmā, he is to be revered even by Brahmā. 'They understand' means the wise ones who discern the distinction of a brahmin in the ultimate sense. For to the ignorant, he is immeasurable. Therefore, it is said: 'of the wise.' The rest is easily understood.

Vāseṭṭhasuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

The Explanation of the Hidden Meaning in the Commentary on the Vāseṭṭha Sutta is complete.

9. Subhasuttavaṇṇanā

9. The Commentary on the Subha Sutta

462. Tudisaññāto [V 2.0205] gāmo nigamo etassāti todeyyo, tassa attajo todeyyaputtoti āha “tudigāmā”tiādi. Ārādhakoti saṃrādhako. Dhammanisanti yasmā sampādanena paripūraṇena icchitā, tasmā vuttaṃ “sampādako paripūrako”ti. Ñāyati nicchayena gameti nibbānaṃ, taṃ vā ñāyati paṭivijjhīyati etenāti ñāyo, tato etassa sampādakahetubhāvato ñāyo dhammo ariyamaggo taṃ ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ. Tenāha “kāraṇadhamma”nti. Anavajjanti avajjapaṭipakkhaṃ.

462. One from the village or town known as Tudi is a Todeyya; his son is Todeyyaputta. Thus it is said, 'from the village of Tudi,' and so forth. 'Ārādhaka' means an accomplisher. Regarding 'nisanti' in 'dhammanisanti': because it is desired through accomplishment and fulfillment, it is said to mean 'the accomplisher, the fulfiller.' One goes (`ñāyati`) to Nibbāna with certainty by this, or Nibbāna is penetrated (`paṭivijjhīyati`) by this; therefore it is 'ñāya' (the way). Because this is the cause for its accomplishment, the `ñāya` is the Dhamma, the Noble Path; this is the 'just Dhamma' (`ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ`). Therefore he says, 'the causal Dhamma.' 'Anavajja' means the opposite of blameworthy.

463. Vaṭṭacārakato niyyātīti niyyānikaṃ īkārassa rassattaṃ ya-kārassa ca ka-kāraṃ katvā. Niyyāne vā niyuttaṃ, niyyānaṃ sīlanti vā niyyānikaṃ, tappaṭipakkhato aniyyānikaṃ. Sā pana atthato akusalakiriyāti āha “akusalapaṭipada”nti.

463. It is 'niyyānika' because it leads out (`niyyāti`) from the prison of the round of rebirths (`vaṭṭacārakato`), by shortening the `ī` and changing the `ya` to `ka`. Or, it is 'niyyānika' because it is employed in the leading out, or because its nature is to lead out; its opposite is 'aniyyānika.' But that, in meaning, is an unwholesome action, thus he says, 'unwholesome practice.'

Bahubhāvavācako [M 2.0205] idha mahāsaddo “mahājano”tiādīsuviyāti āha “mahantehi bahūhī”ti. Atthoti payojanaṃ. Mahantānīti bahulāni. Kiccānīti kātabbāni. Adhikaraṇānīti adhikārajīvikārūpāni. Gharāvāsakammameva pañcabalikaraṇadasaatthaṭṭhānabhāvato lokayātrāya ca sampavattiṭṭhānabhāvato jīvitavuttiyā vā hetubhāvato gharāvāsakammaṭṭhānaṃ.

Here, the word 'mahā' expresses multiplicity, as in 'mahājano' and so forth, hence it is said, 'by the great, by the many.' 'Attha' means purpose. 'Mahantāni' means abundant. 'Kiccāni' means duties. 'Adhikaraṇāni' refers to matters of administration and livelihood. Household life itself, due to its being the basis for the five offerings and the ten grounds of affairs, and its being the basis for the continuation of worldly life, or its being the cause of sustenance, is the 'basis of household activity' (`gharāvāsakammaṭṭhāna`).

“Appakenapi medhāvī, pābhatena vicakkhaṇo;

Samuṭṭhāpeti attānaṃ, aṇuṃ aggiṃva sandhama”nti. (jā. 1.1.4);

“Even with little, a wise and discerning person, with a small provision, establishes himself, like one fanning a tiny fire.”

Gāthāya vuttanayena cūḷantevāsikassa viya.

In the manner described in the verse, like a junior pupil.

464. Ayoniso pavattitaṃ vāṇijjakammaṃ viya apāyabhūtaṃ kasikammaṃ nidassanabhāve ṭhapetvā ayonisomanasikaraṇavasena pavattaṃ gharāvāsakiccaṃ sandhāyāha – “yathā kasi…pe… evaṃ gharāvāsakammaṭṭhānampī”ti. Brāhmaṇabhatto ahosīti so kira bahū brāhmaṇe dhanaṃ datvā yaññaṃ kāresi. Uparīti “upari upaṭṭhātīti vadehī”ti brāhmaṇehi attano samayena ācikkhāpitopi yathā upaṭṭhitameva kathetvā kālaṃ katvā niraye nibbatto, atha brāhmaṇā – “iminā [V 2.0206] amhākaṃ yaññe doso dinno”ti kujjhitvā tassa kaḷevaraṃ susānaṃ netuṃ nādaṃsu. Athassa ñātakehi sahasse dinne taṃ sahassaṃ gahetvā gehato nīharituṃ adaṃsu. Kassapasammāsambuddhakāle chattiṃsa itthiyo “ekā vatthaṃ adāsi, ekā gandhaṃ, ekā sumanamāla”ntiādinā taṃ taṃ dānamayaṃ puññaṃ katvā āyupariyosāne tāvatiṃsabhavane sakkassa devarañño paricārikā hutvā nibbattiṃsu sahassaaccharāparivārikā, sakkassa devarañño vejayantarathaṃ pesetvā pakkosāpitena guttilācariyabhūtena mahābodhisattena pucchitā taṃ taṃ attanā kataṃ puññaṃ byākariṃsu. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “sakalāya guttilavimānakathāya dīpetabba”nti. Vaṇijjakammaṭṭhānaṃ vipajjamānanti ettha tassa vipajjamānākāro heṭṭhā vutto. Evaṃ pabbajjakammaṭṭhānampi vipajjamānaṃ appaphalaṃ hotīti ānetvā sambandho. Sīlesu aparipūrakārinotiādi tassa vipajjanākāradassanaṃ. Jhānādisukhanti ettha ādi-saddena abhiññāvipassanādisukhassa viya sabrahmacārīhi saddhiṃ sīlasampadādisukhassa [M 2.0206] saṅgaho daṭṭhabbo. Arahattampi pāpuṇāti pageva sekkhaputhujjanasampattiyoti adhippāyo.

464. Having established as an example farming, which is a state of woe, and trade, which is carried out improperly, it refers to the practice of household life that proceeds by way of unwise attention, saying: 'Just as farming… so too the practice of household life.' He was Brāhmaṇabhatta because, it is said, he gave much wealth to brahmins and had a sacrifice performed. Regarding 'above' (upari): although instructed by the brahmins at that time, 'Say, “He is attended to above,”' he spoke only of what was present and, after death, was reborn in hell. Then the brahmins, becoming angry, said, 'This man has brought fault upon our sacrifice,' and did not allow his corpse to be taken to the charnel ground. When his relatives gave a thousand, they took that sum and allowed it to be removed from the house. During the time of Kassapa the Fully Enlightened One, thirty-six women—'one gave cloth, one gave perfume, one gave a flower garland,' and so on—performed various meritorious deeds of giving. At the end of their lives, they were reborn as attendants of Sakka, king of the gods, in the Tāvatiṃsa realm, each with a retinue of a thousand celestial nymphs. When summoned by Sakka, king of the gods, who had sent his Vejayanta chariot, the Great Bodhisatta, who was then the teacher Guttila, questioned them, and they each declared the merit they had performed. Referring to this, it is said, 'It should be explained through the entire story of the Guttila Mansion.' Regarding 'trade that fails'—here, the manner of its failure was stated below. In the same way, the practice of renunciation, when it fails, yields little fruit—this connection should be brought in. The phrase beginning with 'one who does not fulfill the virtues' shows the manner of its failure. Regarding 'the happiness of jhāna, etc.'—here, by the word 'etc.,' the inclusion of the happiness of the higher knowledges, insight, and so on, as well as the happiness of the accomplishment in virtue together with fellow practitioners of the holy life, should be understood. The meaning is that one attains even arahantship, let alone the attainments of trainees and ordinary people.

Cāgasīsenāti padhānabhūtena cāgena dānena taṃ avassayaṃ katvā. Ettha te na koci aphāsukabhāvoti. Ujukaṃ katvā aviruddhaṃ katvā, sampayojetvāti attho. Tapacariyanti aggiparicaraṇaṃ, tapacariyañca brahmacariyaggahaṇā duṭṭhullabhāvato.

'By generosity as the chief thing' means making that a support by the chief act of giving, by generosity. The phrase 'Here, there is no discomfort for you' means having made it straight and unopposed; this is the meaning of 'having connected it.' 'Austerity practice' refers to fire worship. And austerity practice is coarse, in contrast to the undertaking of the holy life.

466. Ajānanabhāvanti asabbaññubhāvaṃ. Bhagavato pana sabbaññubhāvo sadevake loke jalatale pakkhittatelaṃ viya pattharitvā ṭhito, na me idaṃ patirūpaṃ, tato parivattissāmīti “brāhmaṇo, bho, gotamā”tiādimāha. Paccāharituṃ paṭipakkhena apaharituṃ. Setapokkharasadisoti puṇḍarīkapattasadisavaṇṇo. Suvaṭṭitāti vaṭṭabhāvayuttaṭṭhāne suvaṭṭā. Nāmakaṃyevāti nāmamattameva vacanamattameva. Tathābhūtānaṃ bhāvassapi abhāvena nihīnaṃ nāma hoti, nāma-saddo nihīnapariyāyo. Tenāha – “lāmakaṃyevā”ti.

466. 'The state of not knowing' means the state of non-omniscience. But the Blessed One’s omniscience is established, spread throughout the world with its gods like oil poured on the surface of water. Thinking, 'This is not proper for me; I will turn away from this,' he says, 'Brahmin Gotama, sir,' and so on. 'To turn back' means to take away by means of an opposing argument. 'Like a white lotus' means having a color similar to the petal of a white lotus. 'Well-rounded' means well-rounded in places where it is fitting to be round. 'Merely a name' means just a name, just a word. For such beings, due to the absence of the actual state, the name itself is base; the word 'name' is a synonym for 'base'. Hence it is said, 'merely base.'

467. Katamā vācā tesaṃ seyyoti tesaṃ caṅkiyādīnaṃ brāhmaṇamahāsālānaṃ vuccamānavibhāgāsu vācāsu katamā vācā seyyoti. “Seyyā”ti liṅgavipallāsena vuttaṃ. Sammutiyāti avilaṅghitasādhumariyādāya lokasammutiyā. Tenāha “lokavohārenā”ti. Mantāti mantāsaṅkhātāya paññāya mantetvā jānitvā. Tenāha “tulayitvā”ti. Atthasaṃhitanti hetusañhitaṃ. Taṃ pana ekaṃsato yuttiyuttaṃ hotīti āha – “kāraṇanissita”nti. Āvutotiādīsu ādito abhimukhaṃ ñāṇagatiyā vibandhanena āvuto, āvariyena visesato ñāṇagatiyā [V 2.0207] nibandhanena nivuto, evaṃ ophuṭo paliguṇṭhito. Pariyonaddhoti samantato onaddho chādito. Tenāha “paliveṭhito”ti.

467. 'Which speech is better for them?' means: among the various kinds of speech addressed to those great brahmin householders like Caṅkī, which speech is better? 'Better' (seyyā) is said with a reversal of gender. 'By convention' means by the worldly convention that does not transgress the proper bounds of the virtuous. Hence it is said, 'by worldly usage.' 'By reflecting' (mantā) means knowing after having reflected with the wisdom called 'mantā.' Hence it is said, 'having weighed.' 'Connected with meaning' means connected with reason. That, however, is entirely endowed with logic, hence it is said, 'based on reason.' In 'covered,' etc., `āvuto` (covered) means obstructed from the beginning by the binding of the movement of knowledge towards it; `nivuto` (enveloped) means especially bound by the binding of the movement of knowledge through covering; thus `ophuṭo` (enclosed) and `paliguṇṭhito` (entangled). 'Completely wrapped' (pariyonaddho) means bound and covered all around. Hence it is said, 'encompassed.'

468. Sace etaṃ kāraṇamatthīti “nissaṭṭhatiṇakaṭṭhupādāno aggi jalatī”ti etaṃ kāraṇaṃ sace atthi yadi siyā, so aparo tiṇakaṭṭhupādāno aggi yadi bhaveyya. Sadoso sādīnavo saparikkileso. Parisuddhoti upakkilesābhāvena sabbaso suddho. Jāti ādīnaṃ abhāvenāti jātipaccayānaṃ kammakilesānaṃ niggamena.

468. 'If this reason exists' means: if this reason—'a fire with its fuel of grass and sticks discarded burns'—were to exist, then that other fire would be one with fuel of grass and sticks. With fault, with danger, with defilements. 'Purified' means completely pure due to the absence of defilements. 'By the absence of birth, etc.' means by the departure of the conditions for birth, namely kamma and defilements.

469. Na [M 2.0207] niccalā tiṭṭhantīti tattha pakkhipitabbassa labbhamānattā yathāpaññattaṃ hutvā niccalā akampiyā na tiṭṭhanti. Taṃ dosaṃ taṃ ūnatādosaṃ.

469. ‘They do not remain unchanging’ means that because something to be inserted there is obtainable, they do not remain firm and unmoving as they were established. That is a fault, that is a fault of deficiency.

Aññasmiṃ asatīti atthabhañjakamusāvāde asati. So hi attano santakassa adātukāmatādivasena pavattassa akammapathappattassa musāvādabhāvassa viparīto añño idha adhippeto. Tathā hi itaro yebhuyyena vaḷañjitabbato voharitabbato vaḷañjakamusāvādoti āha. Na kadāci musāvādīti dve kathā na kathenti. Bāhirakānaṃ anavajjatapasammatāyapi nissitoti vattuṃ āha “sīlavā tapanissitako hoti”ti. Vivaṭamukhā mantajjhenamaṇḍitā sabbaso sajjhāyā honti, na itareti āha “pabbajitā niccaṃ sajjhāyantī”ti.

'When there is no other' means in the absence of false speech that destroys the meaning. For here, another kind of false speech is intended, one that is contrary to the nature of false speech that has reached an unwholesome course of action, such as that which arises from the desire not to give what belongs to oneself, and so forth. Thus, the other is called 'false speech for practical use' because it is generally to be used and spoken. 'Never a speaker of falsehood' means they do not speak with two tongues. To say that he is reliant even on the asceticism considered blameless by outsiders, he says, 'He is virtuous and reliant on asceticism.' Their mouths are open, adorned with the meditation on mantras; they are entirely engaged in recitation, not otherwise. Hence it is said, 'The renunciants constantly recite.'

470. Ciraṃ nikkhantoti niggato hutvā cirakāle. Na sabbaso paccakkhā honti satisammohato maggānañca aññathā karaṇato. Cirāyitattanti “ayaṃ maggo”ti kathanassa cirāyanaṃ. Vitthāyitattanti asappaṭibhānaṃ. Taṃ pana saupamāha dassetuṃ “yathā”tiādi vuttaṃ.

470. 'Having gone forth for a long time' means having gone out and been gone for a long time. They are not entirely rejected because of confusion of mindfulness and because of practicing the paths wrongly. 'Being delayed' means the delay in saying, 'This is the path.' 'Being diffuse' means lack of ready wit. To illustrate this with a simile, 'Just as,' and so forth, is said.

Balasampannoti kāyabalena samannāgato. Pamāṇakataṃ kammaṃ nāma pamāṇakarānaṃ rāgādikilesānaṃ avikkhambhitattā “pamāṇakataṃ kammaṃ nāma kāmāvacara”nti āha, tesaṃ pana vikkhambhitattā vuttaṃ “appamāṇakataṃ kammaṃ nāma rūpārūpāvacara”nti. Tatthāpi visesato appamaññābhāvanā sambhavatīti āha “tesupī”tiādi. Nirīhakattā yathā appamāṇasamaññā labbhati, taṃ dassetuṃ “pamāṇaṃ…pe… vuccatī”ti āha. Na ohīyati na tiṭṭhatīti katūpacitampi kāmāvacarakammaṃ yathādhigate mahaggatajjhāne aparihīne taṃ abhibhavitvā āsīdetvā passe ohīyakaṃ katvā paṭisandhiṃ dātuṃ samatthabhāvena na tiṭṭhati. Laggitunti āvarituṃ[V 2.0208]. Ṭhātunti patiṭṭhātuṃ. Pharitvāti paṭippharitvā. Pariyādiyitvāti tassa sāmatthiyaṃ khepetvā. Kammassa pariyādiyanaṃ nāma vipākuppādabandhanamevāti āha – “tassa vipākaṃ paṭibāhitvā”ti. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva.

'Endowed with strength' means possessing bodily strength. 'Measured action' is so called because the defilements such as lust, which do the measuring, are not suppressed; hence it is said, 'Measured action pertains to the sensual realm.' But because these are suppressed, it is said, 'Immeasurable action pertains to the form and formless realms.' There, specifically, the development of the immeasurables is possible; hence it is said, 'In those as well,' and so forth. To show how the term 'immeasurable' is obtained due to being without striving, it is said, 'Measure... is called,' and so forth. 'It is not left behind, it does not stand' means that even sensual-realm kamma that has been done and accumulated, when the attained sublime jhāna is not lost, is overpowered and suppressed by it, made to fall aside, and thus is unable to establish rebirth. 'To cling' means to obstruct. 'To stand' means to be established. 'Having pervaded' means having thoroughly pervaded. 'Having exhausted' means depleting its power. The exhaustion of action is simply the prevention of the arising of its result; hence it is said, 'having warded off its result.' The rest is easily understood.

Subhasuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

The commentary on the Subha Sutta, an elucidation of the hidden meaning, is complete.

10. Saṅgāravasuttavaṇṇanā

10. The Commentary on the Saṅgārava Sutta

473. Abhippasannāti [V 2.0209][M 2.0208] abhisamecca pasannā. Tenāha – “aveccappasādavasena pasannā”ti. Brāhmaṇī vigatamalamaccheratāya “tuyhaṃ deyyadhammaṃ ruccanakaṭṭhāne dehī”ti āha. Maggeneva hissā macchariyassa pahīnattā buddhapakkhabrāhmaṇapakkhavasena ubhatopakkhikā.

473. "Deeply devoted" means devoted having fully understood. Hence it is said, "Devoted through unwavering confidence." The brahmin woman, being free from the stain of stinginess, said, "Give the alms in a place pleasing to you." Indeed, because her stinginess was abandoned by the path itself, she is impartial, belonging to both the Buddha's faction and the brahmin's faction.

Kiṃsūti kinti pucchāvacanaṃ. Chetvā anādiyitvā vināsetvā. Sukhaṃ setīti cittasantāpābhāvena sukhena supati. Na socatīti tato eva sokaṃ nāma vināseti. Kodhanti kujjhanalakkhaṇaṃ kodhaṃ. Chetvā samucchinditvā. Sukhaṃ setīti kodhapariḷāhena apariḍayhamānattā sukhaṃ supati. Kodhavināsena vinaṭṭhadomanassattā na socati. Visamūlassāti dukkhavipākassa. Madhuraggassāti akkosakassa paccakkosanena, pahārakassa paṭippaharaṇena yaṃ sukhaṃ uppajjati, taṃ sandhāyeva “madhuraggo”ti vutto. Imasmiñhi ṭhāne pariyosānaṃ “agga”nti vuttaṃ. Ariyāti buddhādayo ariyā.

"Kiṃsū" means "what," a word of inquiry. "Having cut off" means disregarding and destroying. "He sleeps happily" means he sleeps happily because of the absence of mental distress. "He does not grieve" means he thereby destroys sorrow itself. "Anger" refers to anger, which has the characteristic of being angry. "Having cut it off" means having completely eradicated it. "He sleeps happily" means he sleeps happily because he is not burned by the torment of anger. Because his displeasure is destroyed through the destruction of anger, he does not grieve. "With a poisonous root" means having a painful result. "Sweet-tipped" refers to the happiness that arises from responding to abuse with abuse, or responding to a blow with a counter-blow; it is with reference to this that it is called "sweet-tipped." For in this context, "tipped" means the final outcome. "The noble ones" refers to noble ones such as the Buddhas.

Pañhaṃ kathesīti brāhmaṇo kira cintesi – “samaṇo gotamo lokapūjito, na sakkā yaṃ vā taṃ vā vatvā santajjetuṃ, ekaṃ saṇhapañhaṃ pucchissāmī”ti. So ekaṃ pucchāgāthaṃ abhisaṅkharitvā “sace asukassa nāma vadhaṃ rocemīti vakkhati, ye tuyhaṃ na ruccanti, te māretukāmosi, lokavadhāya uppanno kiṃ tuyhaṃ samaṇabhāvenāti niggahessāmi. Sace na kassaci vadhaṃ rocemīti vakkhati, atha naṃ tvaṃ rāgādīnampi vadhaṃ na icchasi, tasmā samaṇo hutvā āhiṇḍasīti niggaṇhissāmīti imaṃ ubhatokoṭikaṃ pañhaṃ puṭṭho samaṇo gotamo neva gilituṃ na uggilituṃ sakkhissatī”ti evaṃ cintetvā imaṃ payhaṃ pucchi. Tassa bhagavā ajjhāsayānurūpaṃ kathesi. So pañhabyākaraṇena ārādhitacitto pabbajjaṃ yāci. Satthā taṃ pabbājesi, so pabbajjākiccaṃ matthakaṃ pāpesi. Tena vuttaṃ “pabbajitvā arahattaṃ patto”ti.

The brahmin thought, "The ascetic Gotama is honored by the world; it is not possible to intimidate him by saying this or that. I will ask him a single subtle question." Having composed a single question in verse, he thought, "If he says, 'I approve of killing such and such a person,' then I will rebuke him by saying, 'You wish to kill those who do not please you, arisen for the destruction of the world. What is your asceticism for?' If he says, 'I do not approve of killing anyone,' then I will rebuke him by saying, 'You do not wish for the destruction even of lust and so on. Therefore, having become an ascetic, you wander about.' Thus, when asked this two-edged question, the ascetic Gotama will be able neither to swallow it nor to spit it out." Having thought thus, he asked this question. The Blessed One answered him according to his disposition. Pleased by the explanation of the question, the brahmin requested ordination. The Teacher ordained him, and he brought the duties of the ascetic life to perfection. Therefore, it is said, "Having gone forth, he attained arahantship."

Avabhūtāti adhobhūtā. Adhobhāvo sattānaṃ avaḍḍhi avamaṅgalanti āha – “avaḍḍhibhūtā avamaṅgalabhūtāyevā”ti. Paribhūtāti paribhavappattā. Vijjamānānanti pāḷiyaṃ anādare sāmivacananti tadatthaṃ dassento “vijjamānesū”tiāha. Pakaṭṭhaṃ, pavaḍḍhaṃ vā ñāṇanti paññāṇanti bhagavato ñāṇaṃ visesetvā vuttaṃ.

"Avabhūtā" means "fallen low." The state of being low is decline and misfortune for beings—thus it is said: "They have become subject to decline, subject to misfortune." "Paribhūtā" means "having met with contempt." The Pāli term `vijjamānānaṃ` is a genitive case expressing disregard; showing its meaning, the commentator said `vijjamānesu`. The term `paññāṇa` means excellent (`pakaṭṭhaṃ`) or developed (`pavaḍḍhaṃ`) knowledge; it is stated in order to specify the knowledge of the Blessed One.

474. Abhijānitvāti [V 2.0210][M 2.0209] abhivisiṭṭhena ñāṇena jānitvā. Vositavosānāti katakaraṇīyatāya sabbaso parisositaniṭṭhā. Pāramisaṅkhātanti paramukkaṃsabhāvato pāramīti saṅkhātaṃ. Tenāha “sabbadhammānaṃ pārabhūta”nti. Brahmacariyassāti sāsanabrahmacariyassa ādibhūtaṃ. Tenāha “uppādakā janakā”ti. “Idamevaṃ bhavissati idameva”nti takkanaṃ takko, so etassa atthīti takkī. Yasmā so taṃ taṃ vatthuṃ tathā tathā takkitvā gaṇhati, tasmā vuttaṃ “takkagāhī”ti. Vīmaṃsanasīlo vīmaṃsī paccakkhabhūtamatthaṃ vīmaṃsanabhūtāya paññāya kevalaṃ vīmaṃsanato. Tenāha “paññācāraṃ carāpetvā evaṃvādī”ti. Yathāvuttatakkīvīmaṃsībhāvena takkapariyāhataṃ vīmaṃsānucaritaṃ sayaṃpaṭibhānaṃ evametanti vatvā.

474. "Having fully known" means having known with distinguished knowledge. "Having reached the final end" means having a conclusion that is completely exhausted in every way because what was to be done has been done. "Declared as pāramī" means it is called pāramī because of its most excellent nature. Therefore, it is said, "having gone beyond all dhammas." "Of the holy life" refers to being the origin of the holy life of the teaching. Hence, it is said, "the generators, the progenitors." "The thought 'This will be thus, this is thus'"—such reasoning is takka; one who possesses this is takkī. Because he grasps each and every thing by reasoning in that way, it is said, "one who grasps through reasoning." One whose nature is investigation is a vīmaṃsī, from solely investigating a directly perceived object with investigative wisdom. Therefore, it is said, "having put wisdom into practice, he speaks thus." This refers to speaking thus, "it is so," declaring his own intuition, which is influenced by reasoning and guided by investigation, due to his nature of being a reasoner and investigator as described.

485. Aṭṭhitapadhānavatanti aññattha kismiñci puggale aṭṭhitapadhānavataṃ anaññasādhāraṇaṃ bhoto gotamassa padhānaṃ ahosi. Sappurisapadhānavataṃ ahosi sappurisapadhānavatādhigatānaṃ etādisānaṃ arahataṃ acchariyapuggalānaṃyeva āveṇikapadhānavataṃ ahosi. Ajānantova pakāsetīti ayaṃ pucchitamatthaṃ sayaṃ paccakkhato ajānanto eva kevalaṃ saddaṃ uppādetvāva pakāsesīti saññāya āha. Ajānanabhāve santeti ime adhidevāti paccakkhato jānane asati. Paṇḍitena manussenāti lokavohārakusalena manussena, tvaṃ pana lokavohārepi akusalo. Vacanatthañhi ajānanto yaṃ kiñci vadati. Uccena sammatanti uccaṃ supākaṭaṃ sabbaso taruṇadārakehipi sammataṃ. Ñātametaṃ yadidaṃ atthi devāti. Tenāha “susudārakāpī”tiādi. Devāti upapattidevā. Adhidevā nāma sammutidevehi adhikadevāti katvā, tadaññe ca manusse adhikabhāve kimeva vattabbaṃ. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva.

485. "One who is steadfast in striving" means that the striving of the Venerable Gotama was a steadfast striving not found in any other person elsewhere; it was uncommon. It was the striving of a true person; it was the unique striving belonging only to such amazing persons, arahants, who have attained the state of a true person's striving. "Though not knowing, he declares"—this is said with the perception that, not himself knowing directly the meaning of what was asked, he merely produces a sound and declares it. The phrase "these higher devas exist" is uttered in the absence of direct knowledge, that is, without knowing them directly. "By a wise man" means by a person skilled in worldly convention, but you are unskilled even in worldly convention. For one who does not know the meaning of a word says whatever. "Highly esteemed" means highly renowned, agreed upon by all, even by very young children. "It is known that there are devas"—therefore it is said, "even very young children," and so forth. "Devas" means devas by birth. `Adhidevā` means devas who are higher than conventional devas; what then needs to be said about other humans being in a higher state?

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Of the Papañcasūdanī, the Commentary on the Majjhima Nikāya

Saṅgāravasuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

The Clarification of the Hidden Meaning in the Exposition of the Saṅgārava Sutta is complete.

Niṭṭhitā ca brāhmaṇavaggavaṇṇanā.

And the Exposition of the Chapter on Brahmins is concluded.

Majjhimapaṇṇāsaṭīkā samattā.

The Subcommentary on the Middle Fifty is complete.
